item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
English rendering of PM's speech at the launch of development projects in Banaskantha, Gujarat
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi

Bharat Mata Ki Jai.

Bharat Mata Ki Jai.

Popular Chief Minister of Gujarat Shri Bhupendra Bhai Patel, Deputy Chief Minister Bhai Harsh Sanghvi ji, Speaker of the Legislative Assembly Shri Shankarbhai Chaudhary, all ministers of the Gujarat Government, Members of Parliament and Members of the Legislative Assembly, other public representatives, brothers and sisters.

Today, through technology, farmers from every district of the country are connected with us. Today, through technology, farmers from every village of Gujarat are connected with us. Chief Ministers of different states, ministers, all of them are with us today in this important programme for farmers. I heartily welcome all of them as well.

Today, Banaskantha has established its stature. Just now, I was watching on the screen that perhaps such a large gathering seated on charpoys has never been held anywhere in the world. For the people of the country too, it must be an amazing sight that everyone in this gathering is seated on charpoys. Today, Banaskantha has revived this great tradition of our villages. Had you informed the Guinness Book of World Records in advance, they would certainly have recorded it as a world record. It was just mentioned here a moment ago.

The responsibility that you entrusted to me has now completed twenty-five years. And look at the coincidence, after completing twenty-five years, my first visit has been to our Banaskantha. Let me remind you that after becoming Chief Minister in 2001, my first major public programme as Chief Minister was held in Deesa. The older people here will remember that Lok Kalyan Mela. That programme was perhaps historic. Three lakh people from a single district attended it. I do not believe that record has been broken to this day. That record belongs to Banaskantha. The journey began there, and today I have got the opportunity to present an account of twenty-five years of service at the same place.

Only a few days after Navratri, I have received the opportunity to come to the sacred land of Mother Amba. I bow at the feet of Mother Amba. A short while ago, projects dedicated to women, children, farmers, and livestock rearers were inaugurated and foundation stones laid here. A new instalment of PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi has also reached the accounts of crores of small farmers across the country. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to the people of Gujarat, to the people of the country, and to farmers across India.

Friends,

The people of Gujarat and Banaskantha should forgive me, but I have to speak in Hindi today because people from all over the country are connected with this programme. You permit me to speak in Hindi, don't you? Very good.

Friends,

Our farmers, our food providers, are among the strongest pillars of a Developed India. Our government has always prioritised the welfare and empowerment of farmers. Compared to 2013–14, the agricultural budget of the country has now increased more than five times. PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi has become a part of the lives of crores of small farmers. Today, more than ₹18,000 crore has been transferred into the accounts of nearly ten crore farmers. More than fifty lakh farmers of Gujarat have also benefited from it. More than ₹1,000 crore has been deposited into their accounts. In Banaskantha alone, nearly ₹50 crore has reached the accounts of lakhs of farming families.

Friends,

Because of our government's policies over the past years, farmers have received benefits or savings worth more than ₹50 lakh crore. Fifty lakh crore rupees. Let me give you an example of just five schemes. Around ₹4.5 lakh crore under PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi has directly reached the bank accounts of small farmers. Sister, you have defeated me. I thought you would sit down after a while because your hands would start hurting. I request the SPG personnel to collect that beautiful picture which this daughter has brought. Otherwise, she will grow tired holding it up. They will collect it from here, my child. Please stay where you are. Let the SPG personnel collect it. After Independence, the needs of small farmers were never truly understood. Nobody paid attention to them. Yet small farmers account for more than 85 percent of all farmers in our country. More than 85 percent. It is our government that understood their concerns and supported them through PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi.

Friends,

Over the past few years, global uncertainties caused fertiliser prices to surge sharply. But a government dedicated to farmers did not allow that burden to fall upon them. The government spent nearly ₹16 lakh crore on this. To ensure that fertilisers remain affordable for you, we had to spend ₹16 lakh crore from the national treasury, so that the burden would not fall upon our farmers.

Friends,

Previous governments repeatedly misled farmers on Minimum Support Price. But ours is the government that fulfilled its MSP promise. Over the past twelve years, farmers growing wheat and paddy have received ₹24 lakh crore in MSP payments directly into their accounts.

Friends,

Our government has provided farmers with a powerful safety net through the PM Fasal Bima Yojana. We launched crop insurance on a large scale. During the past ten to twelve years, farmers have received more than ₹2 lakh crore in crop insurance compensation. Whenever crops suffered losses, over ₹2 lakh crore reached farmers through insurance support. We are continuously trying to reduce farmers' irrigation costs as well. PM-KUSUM is playing an increasingly significant role in this effort. Under this scheme, nearly twelve lakh solar pumps have already been provided. Twelve lakh pumps powered by solar energy have been given to farmers for irrigation. Because of this, the need for electricity and diesel has reduced substantially. If these solar pumps had not been provided, farmers would have had to purchase more than 80 crore litres of diesel. That entire expense has been saved by lakhs of farmers. And besides that, additional electricity has also been generated. If viewed in one way, these five schemes and decisions alone have either directly benefited farmers or saved them the equivalent of ₹50 lakh crore. This is an enormous figure. These ₹50 lakh crore have increased farmers’ incomes and strengthened Indian agriculture.

Friends,

Agriculture is our tradition. Agriculture is our culture. Agriculture is our culture. During the past twelve years, our government has extensively integrated science and technology into farming. We have linked agriculture and animal husbandry with scientific methods. Soil Health Cards are an excellent example of this. Earlier, farmers found it difficult to determine what type of fertilizer their fields required and in what quantity. Soil Health Cards solved this problem. Today, more than 26 crore Soil Health Cards are in the hands of farmers. These have modernised farming practices.

Friends,

Changing weather patterns are a major challenge for farmers. Therefore, our effort is to continuously provide farmers with new seed varieties that are better suited to changing climatic conditions. Over the past years, around three thousand new seed varieties have been made available to farmers.

Friends,

Animal husbandry is an important part of our rural economy, and our sisters have a major role in it. During the past decade, we have strongly promoted the use of science and technology in animal husbandry and the dairy sector. When livestock breeds improve, milk production increases. As Shankarbhai was saying earlier, we want one cow to produce as much milk as four cows once did. If animals receive timely vaccination and treatment, losses due to disease are reduced. In other words, healthier animals mean higher incomes for our livestock-rearing brothers and sisters.

Friends,

You are all familiar with the National Gokul Mission. Through it, indigenous breeds are being preserved and scientific breeding is being promoted. The new research centre established in Banaskantha will further strengthen this mission. Indigenous cattle breeds such as Gir, Sahiwal, and Kankrej, and buffalo breeds such as Mehsana, Murrah, and Jaffarabadi, will be preserved here. At the same time, major work will be done to improve their quality. For the Kankrej breed, this is the first facility of its kind in the country. Consider a farmer who owns a high-quality cow that produces more milk and remains healthy at a lower cost. Naturally, that farmer would want future generations of that cow to retain those same qualities. Modern technologies such as IVF help achieve exactly that. They increase the likelihood that superior traits will pass on to future generations. The direct benefit of this goes to livestock rearers.

Friends,

Protecting livestock from disease is also one of our priorities. Foot-and-mouth disease affects both animal health and milk production. Therefore, we launched a nationwide free vaccination campaign. So far, nearly 150 crore vaccine doses have been administered to animals. The livestock of more than eight crore farmers have received free vaccinations. This has also reduced the financial burden on livestock rearers.

Friends,

The impact of these efforts is visible in milk production as well. In 2013–14, a cow or buffalo produced on average less than five litres of milk per day. This was the situation when you sent me to Delhi. Less than five litres a day. Today, the national average has increased to around eight litres per day. India’s growth rate in milk productivity is the fastest in the world. India ranks number one globally in milk production. The benefits have reached villages, and the incomes of farming families have increased.

Friends,

We want livestock rearers to earn not only from milk but also from dung. Infrastructure is being developed for producing biogas, bio-CNG, and organic fertilisers from dung and agricultural residues. Institutions like Banas Dairy have an important role in this. Today, foundation stones have also been laid for two bio-CNG plants. Our objective is clear: healthier livestock, higher milk production, and complete utilisation of dung. We are transforming animal husbandry into not merely a tradition but also a strong means of increasing farmers’ incomes and enriching villages. I was interacting with the women here earlier. They told me they supply milk worth ₹2 crore. Milk worth ₹2 crore. Then I asked them how much education they had received. They replied, “Four books,” and yet they supply milk worth ₹2 crore.

Friends,

Over the past years, we have worked with a holistic approach for the prosperity of villages. Just look at the fisheries sector and see how much it has expanded. You will be pleased to know that India’s seafood exports have more than doubled. Our fishermen go out to sea, catch fish and shrimp, and sell them. Today, this sector has made enormous progress, and demand across the world has risen sharply. Cooperation in the fisheries sector is also being promoted.

Friends,

There is another sector that has provided an additional source of income for our farmers. That sector is beekeeping. Over the past twelve years, honey production has doubled. I remember that when I came to Banaskantha, I urged all of you to bring about a Sweet Revolution, a Honey Revolution. Today Banaskantha is setting new records in honey production. When I was interacting with the women earlier, they told me they sell honey worth ₹35 lakh. You will be proud to know that India has become the world's second-largest exporter of natural honey. In this Sweet Revolution, the contribution of our women’s self-help groups is also steadily increasing.

Friends,

A few days ago, on 7th October, I completed twenty-five years as head of government. It feels as though it happened only yesterday. Yes, it feels like yesterday itself, when I first took the oath on 7th October 2001. You all gave your Narendra Bhai immense affection and immense love.Today, I felt a little awkward here. Whatever is said in the rest of the country is one thing, but here Shankarbhai said, “Prime Minister Sahib, Prime Minister Sahib.” Tell me honestly, how will such an address go down my throat? Here, people habitually say, “Our Narendra Bhai has come.” Doesn't it feel better to say that? What joy is there in saying “Prime Minister Sahib”? And when my brothers from Gujarat say “Our Narendra Bhai,” my heart overflows with emotion. More than affection, every Gujarati taught me something. They guided me towards the right path and inspired me. At that time, I knew nothing about government offices, government functioning, or files. A person from an ordinary family, whose generations had never even dreamed of becoming the head of a village, was entrusted by you with the responsibility of serving first Gujarat and then the nation. Earlier while speaking with the women, they asked me how ideas such as Jyotigram, bringing water, natural farming, and initiatives for livestock came to me. I told them that there was no special formula. You taught me everything, and I simply went and implemented it.

Friends,

I have always known only two things: service to the people is service to the nation, and the development of Gujarat leads to the development of India. Everything else, how to work and how to move forward, you taught me. Whatever I have been able to do for the nation belongs to all the citizens of India, and to all of you as well. For this, I will remain indebted to you for my entire life. Until my final breath, I will remain devoted to service. Service, service, and service to the people of the country and to all of you.

Friends,

The senior citizens present here will still remember the old days. Twenty-five years ago, when I used to come here, there were severe problems of electricity and water. Even then, I used to say that we must save electricity and water. Farmers would protest against me, saying, “Who is Modi to tell us to save water? He won't even give us electricity.” I kept arguing with you, and eventually you accepted what I was saying. And today, just look at where we have come from and where we have reached. Those old problems now remain only in memories. Today, I will once again tell you the same thing: we must save water, and we must save electricity as well.

Friends,

The waters of the Narmada and modern technologies such as drip irrigation have transformed Banaskantha. They have changed both the face and the destiny of Banaskantha. Banaskantha’s potatoes are now world-famous. No one can come to a person from Banaskantha and say, “I will turn potatoes into gold,” because he will reply, “I am already doing that.” We have a cooperative brand like Banas Dairy here, which is expanding the cooperative movement to other parts of the country, including Kashi. I am especially grateful to Banas Dairy because even in my Kashi, people are benefiting from your experience and your service. Now, even the French fries potato processing plant has expanded its capacity. This will make it possible to purchase a larger quantity of potatoes. This is a major facility and support for potato farmers.

Friends,

A Cluster Development Programme is being implemented for farmers engaged in fruit and vegetable cultivation. Under this programme, twelve clusters have been approved today. These clusters are associated with fruits and vegetables such as tomatoes, potatoes, chillies, grapes, bananas, onions, oranges, pomegranates, and cocoa. Under this initiative, farmers will be supported in establishing new orchards and rejuvenating old ones. People will be trained and guided for the rejuvenation of older orchards, and subsidies will be provided for the entire project. The two clusters approved in North Gujarat will greatly benefit potato farmers of Banaskantha and Sabarkantha.

Friends,

Today, several other development projects related to Gujarat have also been inaugurated and launched. Gujarat has received two new railway services: the Ahmedabad–Varanasi Sabarmati Express and the Mehsana–Becharaji–Sabarmati MEMU train. Both are highly significant rail connectivity projects. In addition, the Ahmedabad Metro service is also being expanded. Today, the foundation stone has been laid for metro projects connecting GIFT City and the airport. The Ahmedabad–Mehsana Highway is now set to be expanded from four lanes to eight lanes.

Friends,

Today, more than 4,000 modern Anganwadis are also being inaugurated for the children of Gujarat. Nearly four lakh children and pregnant mothers will benefit from them.

Friends,

Every such effort is aimed at making India a developed nation. Today, every farmer, every young person, and every daughter and sister in the country is moving forward with the resolve of building a Developed India. But unfortunately, some people do not like this. Some people are unable to accept it. These are people who want to see the country in difficulty. They derive satisfaction from seeing the nation in trouble. Whenever challenges arise for the country, they feel happy.

Friends,

A recent example of this is the war taking place around Iran and the Gulf region. At a time when India is united in dealing with its consequences, these people were busy spreading rumours. Rumours were spread among farmers that fertilisers would not be available. Artificial queues were created and the atmosphere was disturbed. Women were frightened by being told that cooking gas would no longer be available, asking them how they would cook food and how their children would go to school. Their plan was to create panic and disorder in the country so that they could defame Modi.

Friends,

I want to remind the farmer brothers and sisters of this country that I had said Modi would stand firmly with you. And you can see that even though the war is still continuing, Modi did not allow any shortage of fertilisers for farmers. We did not allow fertiliser supplies to run short.

Friends,

Because of this war, fertiliser prices around the world have risen sharply. The chemicals used in producing fertilisers have also become much more expensive. Yet the government did not allow this burden to fall on farmers. A bag of urea that costs around ₹3,000 elsewhere in the world is available to Indian farmers for less than ₹300. The global price of a bag of urea is around ₹3,000, but the government bears that burden and provides it to you for around ₹300. The price of a bag of DAP fertiliser has crossed ₹5,000 globally. But Indian farmers receive the same bag for around ₹1,350. The nation is providing this support so that our farmers become stronger and their lives improve.

Friends,

In a world full of uncertainty, India’s rapid development has become a new source of hope for the entire world. In such a situation, we must continue moving forward on the path of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat - One India, Great India. And tomorrow, the 31st of October, is a day to strengthen this resolve. Tomorrow is the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and National Unity Day. The entire nation will celebrate National Unity Day. On this day, the Run for Unity is organised across the country. Reports are coming in from all directions about the grand preparations being made for the Run for Unity. I would especially urge all citizens of the country, particularly our young friends, to participate enthusiastically in the Run for Unity tomorrow morning.

Friends,

Every year, the Unity Festival is celebrated in Ekta Nagar on the morning of 31st October. But this year, keeping the Run for Unity and other programmes in mind, it will be held in the evening instead of the morning. This is a change from previous years. Tomorrow at 5:30 in the evening, a grand Unity Festival will be celebrated in Ekta Nagar. The programme will be organised on a very large scale. You should watch it on television. There will be such a parade on the soil of Gujarat that it will remind you of the Republic Day celebrations in Delhi. Do watch it. There will be parades by police and security forces, and impressive tableaux will be displayed. I urge all citizens of the country to join this programme tomorrow evening as well. From Kashmir to Kanyakumari, from Kutch to Kamakhya, the entire nation should pay tribute to Sardar Patel and reaffirm the resolve of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat. With this appeal, I once again extend my best wishes to all of you for these development works.

Thank you very much.

The sisters seated at the back are offering their blessings to me. Mothers, I bow at your feet. Your blessings give me tremendous strength. I am deeply grateful to all of you.

Bharat Mata Ki Jai!

Bharat Mata Ki Jai!

Disclaimer: This is an approximate English translation of the Prime Minister’s address. The original address was delivered in Hindi, with some portions in Gujarati, which have been translated to convey their intended meaning.

****

MJPS/SS/VJ/ST

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Adoni - Mantralayam and Hyderabad nearby areas, during the month of September 2026
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 3:04PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Adoni - Mantralayam and Hyderabad nearby areas , during the month of September 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.

These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G, and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analysed in real-time using advanced Software Systems.

TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 1. Hyderabad 63 Kms, Hotspot locations –2 and walk test 21.5Km, during 15th-16th September 2026 in AP LSA. 2.Kurnool District Adoni-Mantralayam and nearby areas 201.8Kms, Hotspot locations – 6, during 17th-18th September 2026 in AP LSA. These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Hyderabad. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area/ route under test on the day/ time of conducting the drive test.

Drive Test Route Map: The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating City drive, Inter-operator calling and Hotspots, as per the legends shown on the map: -

Key Parameters Assessed

  1. Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G).
  2. Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).
  3. Call Silence Instance: Number of call silence instance occurred during the calls.
  4. Data Servies: Download/ Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate

The overall mobile network performance in Balasore City for the key parameters has been summarised below: -

The overall mobile network performance across Hyderabad city and nearby areas (Andhra Pradesh LSA)

a)   Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 321/8478 for Airtel, 2014/7767 for BSNL, 1439/7740 for RJIL and 1139/8287 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.

The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having Limited service out of the total samples collected, was 0/8478 for Airtel, 0/7767 for BSNL, 0/7740 for RJIL and 0/8287 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.

b)    Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/74 for Airtel, 4/72 for BSNL, 1/74 for RJIL and 0/71 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

c)    Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances, measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 0/69 for Airtel, 0/58 for BSNL 6/67 RJIL and 6/69 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

d)    Out of the total calls established, the number of calls with a poor speech quality score (Mean Opinion Score below 3) were 19/441 for Airtel, 201/326 for BSNL, 66/453 for RJIL and 44/460 for VIL.

e)    Data Download and Upload Throughput:

i)  Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 82.88 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 7.13 Mbps for BSNL (3G), 145.79 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 41.41 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 14.75 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 4.35 Mbps for BSNL (3G), 11.40 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 12.83 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed

The overall mobile network performance across Adoni-Mantralayam and nearby areas (Andhra Pradesh LSA)

  1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 1323/37685 for Airtel, 8339/35351 for BSNL, 633/36991 for RJIL and 4155/37273 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.

The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having Limited service out of the total samples collected, was 0/37685 for Airtel, 140/35351 for BSNL, 0/36991 for RJIL and 6/37273 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.

b)    Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/331 for Airtel, 15/317 for BSNL, 0/330 for RJIL and 6/310 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

c)    Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances, measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 12/313 for Airtel, 29/291 for BSNL 2/314 RJIL and 11/307 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

d)   Out of the total calls established, the number of calls with a poor speech quality score (Mean Opinion Score below 3) were 83/2431 for Airtel, 1022/1993 for BSNL, 157/2630 for RJIL and 150/2564 for VIL.

e)    Data Download and Upload Throughput:

i)  Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 118.55 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 10.19 Mbps for BSNL (3G), 209.11 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 12.27 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 18.73 Mbps for Airtel (5G/4G), 6.05 Mbps for BSNL (3G), 14.20 Mbps for RJIL (5G/4G) and 5.37 Mbps for VIL (5G/4G/2G). Detail of Upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map Annexed.

Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT is as under:-

City:

Hyderabad - Khajaguda, Narsingi, Attapur, Anergia, Pashambanda, Shamshabad, Gollapalle Khurd, Manchirevula and Vishal Sanjivini etc.

Adoni - Mantralayam and nearby area-Basaladoddi, Chinnatumbalam, Kup Gal, Ballekallu, Pandavagallu, Adoni, yemminganur, Halaharvi, Mantralayam, Rachumarri, Sunkeswari, Budur, Nandavaram and Chinnakottaliki etc.

Walk Test- 1. AIG Hospital Gachibowli Hyderabad 2. My Home Raka-Hafeezpet-Hyderabad 3. Rajiv Gandhi International Airport Hyderabad 4. Sri Raghavendra Swamy Matha Mantralayam

Hotspot - The hot spot locations, capturing stationary user experience are 1. Adoni Arts and Science College 2. Area Hospital Yemmiganur 3. General Post Office Koti Hyderabad 4. Mantralayam Bus Stand 5. Mantralayam Road Railway Station 6. Rajiv Gandhi International Airport Hyderabad 7. Senior Civil Court Adoni 8. Sri Raghavendra Swamy Matha Mantralayam

The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs for taking further necessary action at their end. Detailed reports of IDT are made available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in. For any clarification or additional information, an email can be sent to adv.hydreabad@trai.gov.in or Regional Office of TRAI can be contacted on telephone no.  040-23000761.

item.title: Vice-President calls for holistic rural development to realise Viksit Bharat 2047; graces Golden Jubilee Celebrations and 39th Convocation of Gandhigram Rural Institute

item.description: Vice President's Secretariat Vice-President calls for holistic rural development to realise Viksit Bharat 2047; graces Golden Jubilee Celebrations and 39th Convocation of Gandhigram Rural Institute “India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047 must begin with empowered villages”: Vice-President Gandhian ideals of self-reliance and social service remain vital for building a developed India: Vice-President Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 3:02PM by PIB Delhi The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today graced the Golden Jubilee Celebrations and…
item.content:encoded:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President calls for holistic rural development to realise Viksit Bharat 2047; graces Golden Jubilee Celebrations and 39th Convocation of Gandhigram Rural Institute
“India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047 must begin with empowered villages”: Vice-President
Gandhian ideals of self-reliance and social service remain vital for building a developed India: Vice-President
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 3:02PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today graced the Golden Jubilee Celebrations and 39th Convocation of Gandhigram Rural Institute (Deemed to be University) in Dindigul, Tamil Nadu. He conferred gold medals on meritorious students and extended his congratulations and best wishes to all the graduating students.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the Golden Jubilee Celebrations and 39th Convocation of Gandhigram Rural Institute (Deemed to be University), Dindigul, Tamil Nadu, today, and conferred gold medals on meritorious students. Emphasising that Viksit Bharat 2047 begins with developed villages, he highlighted the transformative progress in rural infrastructure and basic amenities over the past twelve years and called for ensuring greater opportunities and a dignified life for every rural citizen. Governor of Tamil Nadu Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, Chancellor Dr. K. M. Annamalai, Vice-Chancellor Dr. N. Panchanatham and other dignitaries were present.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 30, 2026

Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President emphasised that the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 can be realised only through the holistic development of villages. He stated that the real strength of Indialies in its villages and that rural development must remain a fundamental pillar of national development.

He stressed that the objective should not necessarily be to transform every village into a town, but to ensure that rural citizens have access to quality infrastructure, essential public services, livelihood opportunities and a dignified standard of living comparable to those available in urban areas.

Recalling the legacy of Mahatma Gandhi, the Vice-President said that the history of Gandhigram was closely intertwined with Gandhian philosophy. He recalled that Dr. G. Ramachandran and Dr. T. S. Soundaram Ramachandran, inspired by Mahatma Gandhi’s ideals, established the institution with the vision of promoting rural education, development and social transformation.

Highlighting the enduring power of truth and non-violence, he observed that Mahatma Gandhi had challenged the might of the British Empire through these principles and led India to freedom. Gandhian values, he said, continue to offer guidance to society and the nation.

Referring to India’s development journey over the past twelve years under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice-President highlighted significant progress in rural housing, drinking water, electricity, roads, sanitation, agriculture and digital connectivity.

He noted that, approximately 25 crore people moved out of multidimensional poverty between 2014 and 2023. He observed that various development and welfare initiatives had contributed to improving the quality of life of millions of people.

Emphasising the importance of connectivity, he said that villages must be linked to towns and cities through improved road and transport infrastructure so that opportunities in education, healthcare, markets and employment reach rural communities.

He also underlined the impact of the Swachh Bharat Mission in creating greater awareness about cleanliness. Referring to improvements in the cleanliness of public spaces, he stressed that cleanliness was not merely the responsibility of the government but a collective responsibility of every citizen.

Stating that farmers’ welfare was directly linked to the country’s food security, he highlighted the importance of supporting the farming community. He referred to the PM-KISAN scheme, under which eligible farmer families receive financial assistance of ₹6,000 annually in three instalments directly into their bank accounts.

The Vice-President observed that Artificial Intelligence, automation and digital technologies were rapidly transforming the world and changing the nature of employment. He urged students to equip themselves with emerging technologies while developing creativity, problem-solving abilities and an entrepreneurial outlook.

He encouraged them to become job creators rather than merely job seekers. Referring to the contemporary relevance of Mahatma Gandhi’s philosophy of Swadeshi, he said that promoting domestic manufacturing, indigenous technologies, local industries and innovations by young Indians represented the modern expression of Swadeshi.

The Vice-President called upon the graduating students to use their education and skills not merely for personal advancement but also for the welfare of society. He urged them to make Gandhian values of simplicity, self-reliance, social responsibility and service the guiding principles of their lives.

He also urged students to stay away from drugs and substance abuse and become ambassadors of a drug-free society by creating awareness among their friends, families and communities.

Congratulating Gandhigram Rural Institute on completing fifty years of its journey as a deemed-to-be university, the Vice-President expressed confidence that it would continue to emerge as a leading centre for sustainable rural development, inclusive growth and innovative research.

On the occasion, the Vice-President conferred Honorary Doctorates (Honoris Causa) on three distinguished personalities in recognition of their outstanding contributions in their respective fields: Thavathiru Kundrakudi Ponnambala Adigalar, renowned spiritual leader and Tamil scholar; Shri S. Nambi Narayanan, former senior aerospace scientist of ISRO; and Professor S. S. M. Sundaram, distinguished academician.

At the 39th Convocation of Gandhigram Rural Institute ( Deemed to be University), Dindigul, Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan conferred Honorary Doctorates (Honoris Causa) on Thavathiru Kundrakudi Ponnambala Adigalar, renowned spiritual and Tamil scholar; Shri S. Nambi Narayanan, former senior aerospace scientist of ISRO; and Professor S. S. M. Sundaram, distinguished academician, in recognition of their valuable contributions to spirituality, Tamil scholarship, science and education.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 30, 2026

As part of efforts to strengthen the institution’s academic and infrastructure facilities, the Vice-President inaugurated two new buildings, the Examination and Seminar Halls and the Pushpkunj Heritage Building.

During the Golden Jubilee Celebrations of Gandhigram Rural Institute, Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated two new buildings and laid the foundation stones for three new projects, including a 30-classroom academic complex. He also released the book “Inclusivity of India’s Ageing Population” and unveiled the Golden Jubilee Commemorative Postage Stamp and Postal Cover, marking a significant milestone in the institution’s journey.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 30, 2026

He also digitally laid the foundation stones for three projects: a 22 kV Power House and Control Room, an Academic Building for the School of Education, and an Academic Building Complex comprising 30 classrooms.

The Vice-President released the book “Inclusivity of India’s Ageing Population”. He also unveiled a Golden Jubilee Commemorative Postage Stamp and Postal Cover, marking an important milestone in the institution’s journey.

The Governor of Tamil Nadu, Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar; Chancellor, Dr. K. M. Annamalai; Vice-Chancellor, Dr. N. Panchanatham; Registrar, Dr. K. Marimuthu; faculty members, researchers, students, parents and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

***

PR/ASM/VM

TRAI assesses Mobile Network Quality across Leh and Nearby Areas Route under J&K LSA, during the month of August 2026
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 2:44PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Leh and nearby areas route under J&K LSA, during the month of August 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.

These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analyzed in real-time using advanced Software Systems.

TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 62.6 Km, Hotspot locations - 07, Walk Test - 1.1 Km, Inter Operator Calling at 01 location and on Highway drive - 396.3 Km during 17th Aug 2026 to 21st Aug 2026 in J&K LSA. These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Delhi. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area / route under test on the day / time of conducting the drive test.

Drive Test Route Map: The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating City drive, Inter-operator calling, Hotspots, Walk test & Highways drive as per the legends shown on the map: - 

Figure-1: Drive test routes

Key Parameters Assessed

    1. Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G).
    2. Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).
    3. Call Silence Instance: Number of call silence instances occurred during the calls.
    4. Data Services: Download / Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate.

The overall mobile network performance in Leh, Nubra Valley and Pangong areas route for the key parameters has been summarized below: -

  1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 583/9318 for Airtel, 966/8977 for BSNL & 770/8371 for RJIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure-I.
  2. Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/83 for Airtel, 5/77 for BSNL & 1/76 for RJIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-I.
  3. Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 2/75 for Airtel, 2/75 for BSNL & 1/72 for RJIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-I.
  4. Data Download and Upload Throughput:
      1. Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 121.65 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 8.00 Mbps for BSNL (4G) & 267.13 Mbps for RJIL (5G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-I.
      1. Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 22.13 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 4.87 Mbps for BSNL (4G) & 21.20 Mbps for RJIL (5G). Details of Upload throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-I.

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of Annexure-I.

The overall mobile network performance on Leh to Nubra Valley highway route for the key parameters has been summarized below: -

  1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 4040/11146 for Airtel, 3361/11313 for BSNL & 3530/9209 for RJIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure-II.
  2. Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 12/108 for Airtel, 13/95 for BSNL & 4/85 for RJIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-II.
  3. Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 14/91 for Airtel, 6/71 for BSNL & 16/78 for RJIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-II.
  1. Data Download and Upload Throughput:
      1. Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 109.57 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 16.39 Mbps for BSNL (4G) & 122.16 Mbps for RJIL (5G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-II.
      1. Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 14.21 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 7.81 Mbps for BSNL (4G) & 12.02 Mbps for RJIL (5G). Details of Upload throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-II.

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of Annexure-II.

The overall mobile network performance on Nubra Valley to Pangong highway route for the key parameters has been summarized below: -

  1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 4950/12272 for Airtel, 3203/12041 for BSNL & 5105/9930 for RJIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure-III.
  2. Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 11/67 for Airtel, 17/64 for BSNL & 16/60 for RJIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-III.
  3. Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 18/66 for Airtel, 16/59 for BSNL & 24/52 for RJIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-III.
  4. Data Download and Upload Throughput:
      1. Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 80.59 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 8.86 Mbps for BSNL (4G) & 44.48 Mbps for RJIL (5G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-III.
      1. Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 14.69 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 3.51 Mbps for BSNL (4G) & 3.94 Mbps for RJIL (5G). Details of Upload throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-III.

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of Annexure-III.

The overall mobile network performance on Sakti to Sangam highway for the key parameters has been summarized below: -

  1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 800/6295 for Airtel, 2140/6252 for BSNL &  893/5597 for RJIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure-IV.
  2. Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 1/32 for Airtel, 5/27 for BSNL & 2/30 for RJIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-IV.
  1. Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 2/31 for Airtel, 15/26 for BSNL & 5/30 for RJIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-IV.

d) Data Download and Upload Throughput:

      1. Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 96.97 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 6.00 Mbps for BSNL (4G), and 203.25 Mbps for RJIL (5G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-IV.
      1. Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 14.67 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 4.14 Mbps for BSNL (4G) & 18.84 Mbps for RJIL (5G). Details of Upload throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-IV.

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of Annexure-IV.

Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT are as below: -

  1. City - The areas covered in the city drive are Lakjung, Tsati, Yurtung, Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport, Leh Palace, Sankar Gompa, Leh, Choglamsar and Spituk etc. under Leh and nearby areas.
  2. Highway - The area covered in the highway route are Leh to Nubra Valley via Power House,

View Point Khadungla road, South Pullu, Shiv Shankar Temple, North Pullu, Khardung

Viewpoint, Khalsar and Diskit etc., Nubra Valley to Pangong via Tsati, Agham, Sakti, Zingral, Tsoltak, Tangtse, Muglib, Spangmik and Pangong beach etc. & Sakti to Sangam via Chemrey, Karu, Thiksey, Shey, Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport, Indus Viewpoint and Sangam Point

Leh Ladakh etc.

  1. Hotspot - The hotspot locations, capturing stationary user experience are Army Hospital

Hundar, Artisan Bazaar, EJM College, Gurudwara Sri Pathar Sahib, Leh Airport, Leh Market

& SNM Hospital.

d) Walk Test - The walk test conducted on 17th Aug 2026, covered Leh Market capturing mobile network behaviors in crowded pedestrian environments.

The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs for taking further necessary action at their end. Detailed reports of IDT are made available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in. item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
India to Host ICAR- CGIAR Science and Partnership Week 2027 in New Delhi from April 12–17; Over 5,000 Delegates Expected to participate
CGIAR Science and Partnership Week 2027 to Showcase India's Agricultural Transformation and Global Research Partnerships
CGIAR and ICAR to bring their work in India closer together around national priorities: Dr M L Jat
India to Promote South-South Cooperation and Share Agricultural Innovations with Global South: Dr. M. L. Jat
India–CGIAR Partnership Demonstrates the Transformative Power of Science and Technology: Dr. Ismahane Elouafi
Science, Technology and Global Partnerships Have Transformed India's Agricultural Landscape: Dr. Himanshu Pathak
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 2:29PM by PIB Delhi

CGIAR and the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) today announced that New Delhi will host CGIAR Science and Partnership Week from 12th  to 17th April 2027. The event is organized by ICAR, of the Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India, and CGIAR.

 

The week will bring researchers, farmers, governments, startups and businesses from around the world to New Delhi. Together, they will look at the innovations already reaching farmers and where more work is needed to reach many more.

India is a natural host. ICAR leads one of the world’s largest national agricultural research systems, and its scientists have worked with CGIAR for more than 50 years. Ten CGIAR research centers now work in India, on crops, water, livestock, fish, nutrition, and policy.

India’s agricultural science also reaches well beyond its borders. A groundnut sample from India, conserved and shared by ICRISAT, contributed to varieties now grown in Malawi, Uganda, Mozambique, and Zambia. Hyderabad’s Center of Excellence for South–South Cooperation in Agriculture shares proven farming innovations across Asia, Africa, and Latin America.

 

Dr. M. L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR highlighted the longstanding partnership between India and CGIAR, which has played a significant role in strengthening agricultural research and development in the country for over five decades.

 

He noted that CGIAR, an international agricultural research partnership comprising 15 research centres working across more than 100 countries, has contributed significantly to global agricultural advancement. Its collaboration with India, particularly through ICAR, has supported important developments in crop improvement, natural resource management, food security and agricultural productivity

Referring to India's agricultural transformation since the Green Revolution, Dr. Jat highlighted how collaboration with international research institutions, including CIMMYT, IRRI and ICRISAT, contributed to strengthening India's food production capabilities. From a food-deficit nation dependent on imports, India has emerged as a major food-producing and exporting country.

He emphasised that the CGIAR Science and Partnership Week 2027 will provide an important platform to strengthen international cooperation and facilitate the exchange of scientific knowledge, technologies and best practices.

Dr. Jat stated that India's priority would be to promote South-South cooperation and share its successful agricultural innovations with the Global South, particularly African countries. He highlighted India's progress in climate-resilient agriculture, digital agriculture and AgriStack, agricultural mechanisation, millets, natural farming and sustainable agricultural practices as areas offering considerable opportunities for international collaboration.

He further noted that the event would deliberate on emerging priorities across the agri-food value chain, including climate resilience, water management, soil health, public-private partnerships, startups, youth and women's participation, and the role of media in communicating agricultural science and innovations.

Dr. Ismahane Elouafi, Executive Managing Director, CGIAR, emphasised that the upcoming event would celebrate the achievements of this longstanding partnership while developing a forward-looking agenda for the next 50 years of agricultural cooperation. She highlighted that India has shown what strong national science can achieve at scale. Seed and knowledge from India already help farmers in Africa and Asia. In April, we want to build on that exchange and consider together where science can do more, she added.

She also underscored the importance of recognising the contribution of science and scientists in improving human well-being and strengthening food systems. Referring to the successful first edition held in Nairobi, Kenya, in April 2025, she expressed confidence that the India edition would further strengthen global partnerships and bring together stakeholders to develop solutions for emerging agricultural challenges.

Dr. Himanshu Pathak, Director General, ICRISAT  says “India's agricultural journey from a food-deficit nation to a major food-producing and exporting country reflects the transformative power of science, technology and international partnerships. Through CGIAR Science and Partnership Week 2027, we aim to showcase India's agricultural achievements, share our innovations with the world and learn from global advancements to co-create solutions for the emerging challenges of agriculture and food systems.”

The first CGIAR Science Week took place in Nairobi, Kenya, in April 2025, where CGIAR launched its current research portfolio. The New Delhi edition will focus on how we move from science to impact and how partnership can advance South–South cooperation. It will also explore how agricultural research and innovation can contribute to India’s vision for 2047.

The program and speakers will be announced in the coming months.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare is conducting Nationwide Digital Life Certificate Campaign 5 from 1st to 30th November, 2026
Camps to be held at 2000 Districts/Cities across the country, Largest ever DLC Campaign
Promotion of Digital Empowerment of Pensioners using Face Authentication technology
Saturation model adopted to achieve 2.30 crore DLCs with 1.50 crore Face Authenticated DLCs
19 Banks, 785 District Post offices, 56 Welfare Associations, MeitY & UIDAI  teams, CGDA, Railways, DoT, EPFO, State Governments to collaborate in the month-long campaign
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 1:35PM by PIB Delhi

Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare will be conducting the 5th Nation-wide Digital Life Certificate campaign in 2000 cities/ Districts across India from November 1-30, 2026. The department has notified the guidelines through O.M. dated 13th August, 2026. This is the biggest-ever DLC Campaign undertaken.

A Whole of Government approach will be adopted through coordination with Pension Disbursing Banks, India Post Payments Bank, Pensioners’ Welfare Associations, CGDA, DoT, Railways, EPFO, State Governments, UIDAI & MeitY with the objective of reaching pensioners in the remotest corners of the country.

The focus is majorly on promoting Face Authentication Technology. Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and UIDAI will provide technical support during this Campaign. Face Authentication for Digital Life Certificate is a seamless and fast mode for DLC generation which can be used on Android as well as iOS, making it easy and convenient for elderly Pensioners.

DD, AIR and PIB teams are actively geared up to provide full support to this campaign for Audio, Visual and Print publicity. Outreach efforts will be further complemented by SMSs, tweets (#DLCCampaign5), Jingles and Short films to spread awareness about the campaign.

The Campaign will be conducted in an ‘Utsav’ mode by offering a bouquet of services such as such as Health Check-ups, Aadhar updation for pensioners. Doorstep services will be provided to pensioners where required. Grievance officers will handle grievances regarding DLCs with an immediate resolution approach.

The campaign will be monitored by senior officials from DoPPW who will carry out on-ground reviews in identified states. Mega Camps will be held by stakeholders in areas having high concentration of pensioners and these Mega Camps will be attended by Senior officials from DPPW.

 

*****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
19th India–BLEU Joint Economic Commission Session Held in Luxembourg to Strengthen Trade and Economic Cooperation
Discussions Cover Key Sectors, Including Logistics, Renewable Energy, FinTech, Healthcare and Agro-Food Processing
India–BLEU JEC Explores Opportunities to Deepen Cooperation in Aerospace, Research, Innovation and Higher Education
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 12:45PM by PIB Delhi

The 19th Session of the India–Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Joint Economic Commission (JEC) was held in Luxembourg on 29 October 2026. The meeting provided a platform for India, Belgium and Luxembourg to review bilateral trade and investment relations and discuss opportunities to further strengthen economic cooperation across key sectors.

The JEC was co-chaired by Commerce Secretary, Government of India, Shri Rajesh Agrawal; Director-General for Geo-Economy and Economic Diplomacy, Belgian Federal Public Service Foreign Affairs, Foreign Trade and Development Cooperation, H.E. Mr. Filip Vanden Bulcke; and Secretary General of the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs, Defence, Development Cooperation and Foreign Trade, Luxembourg, H.E. Mr. Henri Schumacher.

The 19th Session reviewed existing trade and investment relations between India, Belgium and Luxembourg and deliberated on ways to enhance economic engagement, facilitate trade and investment flows, and strengthen cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

The discussions covered a broad range of priority sectors, including logistics, with a focus on air connectivity and ports, renewable energy and clean technology, financial services and FinTech, digital transformation and information and communication technology (ICT), healthcare and life sciences, Ayurveda and traditional medicine, and the agro and food processing industry.

The meeting resolved to explore opportunities to deepen cooperation in aerospace, research and innovation, higher education and skill development. Market-related issues were also discussed with a view to addressing trade concerns, facilitating market access and identifying opportunities to further strengthen economic ties.

The JEC provided an opportunity for the three sides to exchange views on their economic priorities, review sectoral cooperation and identify avenues for enhancing business engagement and investment partnerships. The discussions reaffirmed the importance of sustained dialogue and cooperation in advancing mutually beneficial economic relations between India, Belgium and Luxembourg.

Following the JEC session, Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal interacted with CEOs of Luxembourg-based companies during a business interaction. He highlighted India's strong economic growth and investment potential and underscored opportunities for collaboration in financial services, advanced manufacturing, logistics, clean energy, digital technologies, healthcare, and research and innovation. He encouraged Luxembourg companies to explore long-term investments, technology partnerships and opportunities to integrate with Indian firms to serve global value chains.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
FIRST TRAINING SQUADRON OF THE INDIAN NAVY DEPARTS COLOMBO, SRI LANKA
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 11:27AM by PIB Delhi

Ships of the First Training Squadron (1TS) of the Indian Navy, comprising INS Tir, INS Sujata and ICGS Sarathi, departed Colombo, Sri Lanka, on 29 Oct 2026, marking the conclusion of a successful port call. The visit featured bilateral engagements between the Indian Navy (IN) and the Sri Lanka Navy (SLN), reinforcing defence cooperation and the maritime partnership between the two nations.

During the port call, the Senior Officer, 1TS, accompanied by the Commanding Officers of the ships, called on the Commander, Western Naval Area, Sri Lanka Navy. The interaction reaffirmed the close bilateral ties and the shared commitment of both navies to enhancing maritime cooperation.

As part of the professional engagements, sea trainees of 1TS visited the Naval and Maritime Academy (NMA), Trincomalee, and interacted with their Sri Lankan counterparts. In a reciprocal engagement, SLN cadets from NMA visited the 1TS ships and gained insights into the squadron’s training facilities and activities. These interactions provided opportunities for the exchange of experiences and fostered professional camaraderie among the trainees of both navies.

As part of its community outreach initiatives, Indian Navy personnel participated in a beach clean-up activity, promoting environmental sustainability. The ships were also opened to visitors, including members of the local community and the Indian diaspora, providing an opportunity to interact with the crew and gain an insight into the Indian Navy’s training and operational activities.

On departure from Colombo, the ships of 1TS undertook a Passage Exercise (PASSEX) with SLNS Nandimithra. The exercise facilitated coordinated maritime manoeuvres and enhanced operational coordination and interoperability between the two maritime forces.

The visit underscored the enduring maritime partnership between India and Sri Lanka and reaffirmed their shared commitment to regional maritime cooperation and capacity building, in line with the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).

*****

VM/AS

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
DRI busts a big clandestine synthetic drug manufacturing laboratory in Uttar Pradesh; seizes approx. 1,100 kg drugs and precursor chemicals; two arrested
Intelligence-led joint operation uncovers a fully functional illicit drug manufacturing facility in a remote village in Jalaun district
Posted On: 30 OCT 2026 11:05AM by PIB Delhi

In a major crackdown on illicit synthetic drug manufacturing in the country, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) busted a big clandestine drug manufacturing laboratory operating in a remote village in Jalaun district, Uttar Pradesh. The operation led to the massive seizure of approximately 1,100 kg drugs and precursor chemicals, along with manufacturing equipment. Two persons have been arrested in connection with the case.

Acting on specific intelligence, a large team of DRI officers, with operational assistance from UP ATS, launched a coordinated operation at the suspected premises in the early hours of 29th October 2026.
The search of the premises revealed a well-established and functional laboratory for the manufacture of synthetic drugs, resulting into huge seizure of approximately 184 kg semi-prepared drugs, along with around 582 kg precursor chemicals and associated equipment used in the manufacturing process.

In swift follow-up action, searches at the residential premises of the accused led to the recovery of around 15.4 kg finished methaqualone, along with around 153 kg chemicals and a machine used in the manufacturing process. A further search at the premises of another accused resulted in another huge seizure of around 168 kg precursor chemicals. Two persons associated with the clandestine manufacturing facility were arrested under the provisions of NDPS Act,1985.

The recovery of huge quantities of finished drugs, semi-prepared material, precursor chemicals and manufacturing equipment indicates the existence of an organised illicit drug manufacturing operation. The operation has dealt a significant blow to the illicit drug manufacturing ecosystem by dismantling a large clandestine production facility, removing substantial quantities of drugs and precursor chemicals from the illicit supply chain, and preventing the manufacture of further quantities of synthetic drugs.

DRI remains committed to dismantling clandestine drug manufacturing networks, disrupting the supply chains that sustain illicit drug production, to combat the trafficking of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances.
