item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
MSDE Calls Upon CPSEs to Accelerate Apprenticeship Engagement with Focus on Outcomes and Inclusion
National Review of Central Public Sector Enterprises held at Kaushal Bhawan, New Delhi
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 7:51PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) today convened the National Review of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) at Kaushal Bhawan, New Delhi, with a focus on strengthening apprenticeship engagement across public sector enterprises and positioning apprenticeship as a mainstream pathway from learning to livelihoods.

The review underscored the need to reposition apprenticeship not as a fallback option, but as a credible and aspirational pathway that combines theoretical learning with practical workplace experience, enabling young people to acquire industry-relevant skills and become job-ready.

Emphasising the need to shift attention from scale alone to tangible outcomes, Smt. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, said: “Apprenticeship must become a mainstream and aspirational pathway from learning to livelihoods. As the ecosystem expands, our focus must go beyond the number of apprentices engaged to what apprenticeship enables young people to become. CPSEs can play a catalytic role by expanding quality opportunities, improving participation of women and under-represented groups, and creating stronger pathways to productive employment. Our collective success should ultimately be measured through completion, certification, employability, absorption and retention.”

The apprenticeship ecosystem has achieved significant scale under the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS-2). From FY 2022-23 to 22 September 2026, 44.75 lakh apprentices were engaged, supported by 47,452 active establishments. Optional Trades accounted for 76.27% of apprenticeship engagement, reflecting the increasing importance of flexible, employer-responsive apprenticeship pathways.

During the review, CPSEs were called upon to address the gap between apprenticeship potential and actual engagement through realistic enterprise-wise intake plans aligned with the applicable 2.5%–15% apprenticeship requirement. Enterprises were encouraged to validate their workforce and portal data, establish time-bound recruitment trajectories and nominate senior-level nodal officers to monitor implementation and resolve bottlenecks.

The National Review reinforced the collective responsibility of CPSEs, States and other stakeholders to strengthen apprenticeship as an integral component of India’s skilling and employment ecosystem and provide young people with meaningful pathways to gain workplace experience, industry-relevant skills and opportunities for sustainable livelihoods.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
DoT Leads Thematic Session on ‘Intelligent Networks and Quantum Communication’ at ESTIC 2026
Session highlights AI-native 6G networks, quantum-safe communication, cybersecurity and indigenous telecom technologies
C-DOT and BSNL showcase telecom technologies, while Sanchar Saathi and Samridhh Gram are featured at outreach stalls
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 7:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, led the thematic session on ‘Intelligent Networks and Quantum Communication’ on 28 October 2026 at the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026, being held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from 27 to 29 October 2026. Chaired by the Secretary, Department of Telecommunications, the session brought together experts from industry and academia to discuss emerging communication technologies and their role in building secure, intelligent and resilient digital infrastructure.

In his opening remarks, Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications said, “India has one of the largest, most affordable telecom networks with 1.2 billion mobile network connections  and 5G services in almost every district with one of the fastest 5G rollouts in the world. Department of Telecommunications has been supporting indigenous R&D efforts from the laboratory to the market through the Telecommunications Technology Development Fund, or TTDF, and we have so far supported over 130 projects worth to the tune of about ₹ 500 crore. In addition, through the Technology Development and Investment Promotion Scheme, with an outlay of again over ₹ 200 crore, recently renewed for the five-year period up to 2031, we are also helping startups and micro, small, and medium enterprises to join the global standardization, and test solutions in live networks.”

Delivering the keynote address, Mr. N. G. Subramaniam, Chairman, Tejas Networks Ltd., spoke on ‘Engineering Intelligent, Post-Quantum Networks: Autonomous and Trusted’. He highlighted how artificial intelligence, quantum-safe technologies and blockchain can complement one another, AI can enable network intelligence and automation, quantum-safe technologies can strengthen confidentiality and cryptographic resilience, and blockchain can support shared trust and accountability. He emphasised that trust must be engineered into next-generation networks.

The session also featured invited presentations on practical applications of intelligent and secure networks. Ms. Meenal Gupta of Easiofy Solutions presented ‘AI-Powered Medical Imaging over Quantum-Secure Intelligent Healthcare Networks’, illustrating how AI-enabled medical imaging can be supported by high-bandwidth, low-latency connectivity and quantum-safe security to facilitate faster, scalable and secure diagnostics, including beyond major urban centres. Mr. Himamshu Khasnis of Signalchip Innovations spoke on ‘Intelligent and Secure Radio Access Networks: From Chips to Systems’, highlighting indigenous radio-access-network chips and systems, AI-enabled network optimisation and adaptation, and advanced and post-quantum security. His presentation also outlined the role of domestically developed chipsets, radio units and base-station solutions in strengthening India’s telecom technology ecosystem.

A panel discussion brought together experts from academia and industry, including Prof. Rohit Budhiraja, IIT Kanpur; Prof. Bhaskar Kanseri, IIT Delhi; Ms. Sonali Garg, Senior Manager, HFCL; Dr. Ravi Parkash Gandhi, Chief Revenue Officer, Reliance Jio; and Mr. Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Director General, Bharat 6G Alliance. The discussion was moderated by Dr. Rajkumar Upadhyay, CEO, Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT). The panel exchanged perspectives on intelligent networks, quantum communication, cybersecurity and the development and adoption of indigenous telecommunications technologies.

The session also provided a platform to discuss India’s longer-term vision for intelligent and quantum-secure networks. The accompanying vision document identified priority areas including indigenous 6G technologies, AI-native networks and AI-driven cyber defence, a national quantum-secure backbone, zero-trust and cyber-resilience, and skills development. It also emphasised stronger links between research, testbeds, industry and commercial deployment.

DoT’s participation in ESTIC 2026 extended beyond the thematic session to technology and public-outreach showcases. At the thematic stall, C-DOT and Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) jointly showcased technologies and solutions relating to quantum communication and Mission Critical Services. At the Ministry/Departmental Outreach Stall, DoT showcased the Sanchar Saathi and Samridhh Gram initiatives, highlighting their public-facing applications and societal relevance.

The exhibition also provided dedicated spaces for deep-tech start-ups to showcase mature technologies across the Conclave’s 12 thematic areas.

DoT continued its active participation in ESTIC, building on its engagement in ESTIC 2025, where it led the thematic session on ‘Digital Communication’, by leading the session on ‘Intelligent Networks and Quantum Communication’ at ESTIC 2026. Through these engagements, DoT has fostered collaboration among industry, academia and research institutions to advance indigenous telecom innovation, next-generation technologies and India’s future telecom ecosystem.

About ESTIC

The Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026 is being held from 27 to 29 October 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, under the theme ‘Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies’. Organised by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), under the guidance of the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser, with CSIR–National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology (NIIST) as the organising partner, the Conclave was inaugurated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 27 October 2026.

The Conclave brings together stakeholders from government, academia, research institutions, industry, deep-tech start-ups and the scientific community to deliberate on emerging technologies and their contribution to Viksit Bharat@2047. Its programme includes plenary talks, 12 thematic technical sessions, panel discussions, presentations by science and technology leaders and start-ups, exhibitions, poster presentations, and business-to-business and business-to-government meetings. The thematic areas include advanced manufacturing, energy technologies, synthetic biology, ocean and maritime technologies, intelligent networks and quantum communication, semiconductors, agri-tech, generative and autonomous artificial intelligence, robotics, advanced healthcare, immersive technologies and space science.

The Conclave also features distinguished international scientific personalities, including Nobel Laureates Prof. Joachim Frank, Sir Richard J. Roberts and Prof. Kostya Novoselov, alongside eminent Indian and international science and technology leaders. ESTIC serves as a national platform for showcasing technological advancements, identifying emerging scientific priorities and strengthening collaboration among research, industry and government.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Steps Up E-Waste Management under Special Campaign 6
Identifies 5,337 Obsolete E-Waste Items for Disposal
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 7:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) is undertaking focused efforts for the effective collection, segregation and disposal of electronic waste (e-waste). With the objective of institutionalising Swachhata and promoting efficient resource management, the activity is being undertaken as part of Special Campaign 6 for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM 6).

Under the campaign, 5,337 obsolete and e-waste items have been identified for disposal. The obsolete/ e-waste items are being disposed of through auction, thereby generating revenue and facilitating the optimal utilisation of available space. The disposal process has generated revenue amounting to ₹11,40,220/- so far and resulted in the clearance of approximately 600 sq. ft. of space.

The campaign places special emphasis on the systematic identification, segregation and responsible disposal of obsolete electronic items, while ensuring better utilisation of office space and improved workplace organisation.

Through these sustained efforts, MNRE reaffirms its commitment to Swachhata, environmentally responsible waste management and efficient administrative practices under Special Campaign 6.

item.dc:creator: Lok Sabha Secretariat
item.description: Lok Sabha Secretariat LOK SABHA SPEAKER EMPHASISES THE NEED FOR MUTUAL RESPECT EVEN AMID DIFFERENCES OF OPINION IN A DEMOCRACY SANT KABIR'S TEACHINGS OF COMPASSION, EQUALITY AND SOCIAL HARMONY REMAIN RELEVANT EVEN AFTER SIX CENTURIES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER LOK SABHA SPEAKER CALLS FOR INTROSPECTION AND RESTRAINT IN SPEECH AND ETHICAL CONDUCT PEOPLE ARE REMEMBERED NOT FOR THEIR POSITIONS BUT FOR THEIR DEEDS AND CONTRIBUTIONS TO SOCIETY: LOK SABHA SPEAKER LOK SABHA SPEAKER HAILS SANT KABIR'S ROLE IN CHALLENGING SOCIAL EVILS AND BREAKING DOWN BARRIERS OF CASTE AND RELIGION Posted On: …
item.content:encoded:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
LOK SABHA SPEAKER EMPHASISES THE NEED FOR MUTUAL RESPECT EVEN AMID DIFFERENCES OF OPINION IN A DEMOCRACY
SANT KABIR'S TEACHINGS OF COMPASSION, EQUALITY AND SOCIAL HARMONY REMAIN RELEVANT EVEN AFTER SIX CENTURIES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
LOK SABHA SPEAKER CALLS FOR INTROSPECTION AND RESTRAINT IN SPEECH AND ETHICAL CONDUCT
PEOPLE ARE REMEMBERED NOT FOR THEIR POSITIONS BUT FOR THEIR DEEDS AND CONTRIBUTIONS TO SOCIETY: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
LOK SABHA SPEAKER HAILS SANT KABIR'S ROLE IN CHALLENGING SOCIAL EVILS AND BREAKING DOWN BARRIERS OF CASTE AND RELIGION
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today emphasised that differences of opinion and perspective are natural in a democracy, but disagreements must always be expressed with mutual respect and dignity. He observed that Sant Kabir's teachings underscore the importance of restraint in speech, ethical conduct and respect for others, even when opinions differ.

Addressing the Sant Kabir Mahotsav and the foundation stone-laying ceremony of the Kabir Smriti Bhawan at Kabirdham Ashram in Lakhimpur Kheri, Uttar Pradesh, Shri Birla said that Sant Kabir's timeless message of compassion, equality and social harmony continues to guide society even after six centuries. He observed that wider dissemination of Sant Kabir's teachings would foster sensitivity, mutual understanding and social harmony.

Recalling Sant Kabir's remarkable contribution to social reforms, Shri Birla said that, at a time when society was divided by caste distinctions, religious differences and social prejudices, Sant Kabir challenged prevailing orthodoxies and worked to break down divisive barriers. Through his simple yet profound couplets, composed in the language of the common people, he conveyed universal messages of truth, morality, equality and righteous conduct. Shri Birla observed that the enduring relevance of these teachings demonstrates their extraordinary power to inspire positive social transformation across generations.

Highlighting the importance of introspection, Shri Birla referred to Sant Kabir's celebrated couplet: "बुरा जो देखन मैं चला, बुरा न मिलिया कोय; जो दिल खोजा आपना, मुझसे बुरा न कोय।" He observed that, instead of finding faults in others, individuals should reflect on their own conduct and shortcomings. Such introspection, he said, fosters wisdom and humility and encourages a more compassionate approach towards fellow human beings.

Shri Birla further observed that an individual's true legacy is determined not by their position or status, but by their actions and contributions to society. Referring to Sant Kabir's simple life and enduring influence, he said that his noble deeds, selfless service and a commitment to the welfare of others leave a lasting impression on society.

Speaking about the significance of the Kabir Smriti Bhawan, Shri Birla expressed confidence that the institution would disseminate Sant Kabir's message among the people and inspire future generations to embrace his ideals. He underscored the need to take Sant Kabir's spiritual wisdom, people-centric outlook and rational expression to every section of society.

On the occasion, Shri Birla paid his respects to Sant Asang Dev Ji Maharaj and appreciated his lifelong dedication to social service and the dissemination of Sant Kabir's teachings across India and beyond. He observed that the lives of saints, marked by sacrifice, discipline and selfless dedication, provide spiritual strength and inspiration to society. He also acknowledged the contributions of saints and followers who have devoted their lives to carrying forward Sant Kabir's message.

Shri Birla called upon everyone to draw inspiration from Sant Kabir's teachings, practise restraint in speech, cultivate the habit of self-reflection and work towards bringing about positive change in the lives of others.

Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Shri Keshav Prasad Maurya, Sant Asang Dev Ji Maharaj, several public representatives, saints and a large number of followers of Sant Kabir were present on the occasion.

लखीमपुर खीरी, उत्तर प्रदेश में आयोजित संत कबीर महोत्सव एवं कबीर स्मृति भवन के भूमि पूजन एवं शिलान्यास समारोह में सम्मिलित हुआ। संत कबीर की वाणी भारतीय संत परंपरा की वह अमूल्य धरोहर है, जो सदियों से मानवता को सत्य, प्रेम, समरसता और आत्मचिंतन का मार्ग दिखाती आई है। उनके विचार सामाजिक रूढ़ियों से ऊपर उठकर मानवीय मूल्यों, सदाचार और पारस्परिक सम्मान को जीवन का आधार बनाने की प्रेरणा देते हैं। पूज्य संत श्री असंग देव जी महाराज के जन्मोत्सव के पावन अवसर पर उन्हें हार्दिक शुभकामनाएँ। कबीर धाम के माध्यम से संत कबीर के विचारों को जन-जन तक पहुँचाने का उनका सतत प्रयास समाज को आध्यात्मिक चेतना और नैतिक मूल्यों से जोड़ने की दिशा में सराहनीय है। कबीर स्मृति भवन का निर्माण संत कबीर की अमर वाणी, साहित्यिक विरासत और लोकमंगल के संदेश को भावी पीढ़ियों तक पहुँचाने का महत्वपूर्ण माध्यम बनेगा। विश्वास है कि यह भवन सत्य, सद्भाव और मानवीय संवेदना के उन मूल्यों को निरंतर आलोकित करेगा, जिनमें एक समरस और सशक्त समाज की नींव निहित है।

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Education
item.description: Ministry of Education Union Minister of State for Education Felicitates Winners of Viksit Bharat Buildathon 2025 Viksit Bharat Buildathon 2025 Officially Enters the Guinness World Records as the “Largest Innovation Solution Competition” with 2,87,967 Project Submissions Buildathon Empowers Students to Think Creatively, Identify Problems and Develop Solutions: Shri Jayant Chaudhary Shri Jayant Chaudhary Calls for Collective Action on E-Waste Management, Highlights ULLAS’s Role in Promoting Adult Literacy Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 7:22PM by PIB…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
Union Minister of State for Education Felicitates Winners of Viksit Bharat Buildathon 2025
Viksit Bharat Buildathon 2025 Officially Enters the Guinness World Records as the “Largest Innovation Solution Competition” with 2,87,967 Project Submissions
Buildathon Empowers Students to Think Creatively, Identify Problems and Develop Solutions: Shri Jayant Chaudhary
Shri Jayant Chaudhary Calls for Collective Action on E-Waste Management, Highlights ULLAS’s Role in Promoting Adult Literacy
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 7:22PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary today felicitated 10 National level winning teams and innovators of Viksit Bharat Buildathon (VBB) 2025 in New Delhi. The Guinness World Records certification for VBB 2025 as the “Largest Innovation Solution Competition,” was also presented at the function, marking a historic milestone for school education and grassroots innovation in India. As part of the Event, the Minister also launched the ‘Guidelines for Teacher Education Institutions (TEIs) under ULLAS – Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram’. He also distributed prizes to the student winners of the quiz competition based on e-waste.

Addressing the Event, Shri Jayant Chaudhary reiterated the importance of fostering confidence, creativity, innovation and independent thinking among children to mould them into future leaders. Highlighting the Buildathon Initiative, he noted that students were encouraged to identify problems and develop solutions independently, without predefined problems or solutions. He appreciated the participation of lakhs of students nationwide and acknowledged the role of teachers in mentoring and guiding them.

Expressing concern at the growing challenge of e-waste, Shri Chaudhary stressed on the need to involve schoolchildren in addressing it, thereby paving the way for its systematic management. He added that it was the shared responsibility of institutions, communities and citizens to address the issue.

Acknowledging the role of ULLAS in promoting adult literacy and restoring learners' dignity and confidence, he said that the new Guidelines would enable student teachers to play a vital role in empowering the nation.

Secretary, DARPG, Ms. Nivedita Shukla Verma; Secretary, DoSEL, Shri T. K. Anil Kumar; senior officials of the Ministry of Education; representatives and heads of autonomous bodies, education departments of States/UTs and partner institutions, attended the Event.

Viksit Bharat Buildathon 2025

Organised by the Department of School Education & Literacy (DoSEL), Union Ministry of Education, in collaboration with Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), NITI Aayog, and the All-India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), VBB 2025 was initiated to foster creative problem-solving, entrepreneurship, and scientific curiosity among school students. Centred around four foundational pillars—Atmanirbhar Bharat, Swadeshi, Vocal for Local, and Samriddh Bharat—the Initiative witnessed an unprecedented grassroots response, recording 2,87,967 project submissions across both Idea and Prototype tracks.

To evaluate the solutions, a rigorous, three-tier assessment framework was instituted at the district, state and national levels led by multidisciplinary expert panels. Following comprehensive evaluations, 10 national awardees, 100 state awardees and 1,000 district awardees were selected.

An award pool of over ₹1 crore was instituted across district, state and national levels. The 10 national winning teams were awarded a total cash prize of ₹17.50 lakhs . Under the Prototype Track, each of the five top winning teams was awarded ₹2,50,000, recognizing their functional working models. Each of the five winning teams under the Idea Track received ₹1,00,000 to encourage the incubation and scaling of their creative concepts. The winners who were felicitated today belonged to Assam, Delhi, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Keralam, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh.

Special Campaign 6.0

Initiatives taken by both the Departments (DoSEL and the Department of Higher Education) under the Ministry under Special Campaign 6.0 highlighting the efforts to generate awareness about e-waste and e-waste collection endeavours, were presented at the Event. Secretary, DOSEL, Shri Anil Kumar also handed over the e-waste collected during the Campaign to the authorised recycler/refurbisher.

Under the Campaign, DoSEL had undertaken extensive drives to promote responsible e-waste management in schools across the country. Several activities were organised in schools today, including handing over of collected e-waste to authorised recyclers/refurbishers, e-waste-themed morning assemblies and e-waste based quizzes.

Guidelines for TEIs under ULLAS

The ‘Guidelines for Teacher Education Institutions (TEIs) under ULLAS – Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram’ released at the Event, envisages the participation of student teachers enrolled in NCTE-recognised teacher education programmes such as B.Ed., B.P.Ed., M.Ed., M.P.Ed. and other recognised programmes as Volunteer Teachers.

Under the Guidelines, each student teacher will be required to facilitate the literacy and certification of five to eight non-literate learners, with provision for academic credits linked to successful learner certification. Developed by DoSEL after extensive consultations with concerned stakeholders, the Guidelines also clearly define the roles and responsibilities of NCTE, NCERT, CNCL, SCERTs, DIETs, State Literacy Mission Authorities (SLMAs), District Authorities, TEIs and student teachers for effective implementation.

item.content:encoded:
Rajya Sabha Secretariat
Vice-President of India and Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Meets Delegation of European Parliament’s Committee on Foreign Affairs (AFET)
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President and Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today met a delegation from the European Parliament’s Committee on Foreign Affairs (AFET) led by H.E. Mr. David McAllister at Parliament House, New Delhi. He said that India-EU relations have witnessed remarkable progress in recent years across a range of sectors and thanked the leadership of both India and EU for taking it forward.

Emphasizing the shared foundation of the relationship, Shri Radhakrishnan noted that as the two largest democracies and open market economies, with diverse and pluralistic societies, India and the European Union share a common interest in shaping a resilient multipolar global order. He highlighted that institutional linkages established since the visit of the College of Commissioners in 2025, led by H.E. President Ursula von der Leyen with a whole-of-government approach, have yielded fruitful results.

Recalling high-level engagements, the Chairman mentioned that the President of the European Council and the President of the European Commission attended as Guests of Honour during the Republic Day celebrations. Their state visit for the 16th India-EU Summit provided tremendous momentum to the partnership.

Focusing on trade and investment, Shri Radhakrishnan highlighted that India and the European Union together represent a combined market of around USD 25 trillion and nearly two billion people. Terming the the proposed Free Trade Agreement as ‘Mother of all deals’,  the   Chairman expressed hope that it would be signed this year and sought the requisite support of the European Parliament in its fruition.

Addressing cooperation in technology, research, and innovation, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan appreciated the significant role played by the India-EU Trade and Technology Council (TTC) in high-level strategic coordination. He also expressed satisfaction with the conclusion of negotiations on India’s association with the prestigious Horizon Europe programme.

During the meeting, the Chairman also expressed his deepest condolences over the tragic train accident in Spain today.

Members of Rajya Sabha Shri Sanjay Kumar Jha (President, India-Germany Parliamentary Friendship Group); Shri Surendra Singh Nagar (President, India-Poland Parliamentary Friendship Group); Shri Amar Pal Maurya (President, India-Poland Parliamentary Friendship Group); and Smt. P.T. Usha (President, India-Germany Parliamentary Friendship Group) also attended the meeting.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas Makes Significant Progress under Special Campaign 6 ; Frees Over 3.42 Lakh Sq. Ft. of Space and Generates ₹49.46 Crore through Scrap Disposal
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 6:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (MoPNG), along with its Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and other organisations, is actively implementing Special Campaign 6 , with a focus on cleanliness, efficient record management, disposal of scrap and e-waste, and optimum utilisation of office space.

As part of Special Campaign 6 , the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas and its Oil & Gas CPSEs have made significant progress in promoting cleanliness and optimum utilisation of office space. As per the CPSE-wise progress figures compiled for the campaign, 3.42 lakh square feet of space has been freed, registering an increase of 13.20% over the achievement of the previous year (3.03 lakh square feet).

The campaign has generated ₹49.46 crore through the disposal of scrap and e-waste, against a target of ₹41 crore, achieving 120.63% of the target. These achievements underscore the Ministry’s commitment to institutionalising cleanliness, ensuring scientific disposal of scrap and e-waste, and enhancing administrative efficiency across the Oil & Gas sector.

The Ministry continues to monitor the progress of the campaign and has encouraged all its organisations to intensify their efforts towards achieving the assigned targets, ensuring responsible disposal of e-waste and maintaining cleanliness at offices and installations.

Special Campaign 6 reinforces the Ministry's commitment to Swachhata, environmental responsibility, efficient record management and improved administrative functioning across the Oil & Gas sector.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
PM to Inaugurate Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 on 2nd November, 2026
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy to Organise the Summit from 2–5 November at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 6:41PM by PIB Delhi

· Over 130 Countries Expected to Participate; Summit to Bring Together Global Leaders, Investors, Industry and Innovators

· Australia, Denmark, European Union, France, Germany, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, United Kingdom to Participate as Country Partners

· Thirteen States and Union Territories will participate in the Summit, including Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal, showcasing their renewable energy potential, investment opportunities and manufacturing capabilities.

. National and Global Exhibitors to Showcase Renewable Energy Technologies; National Hackathon, Renewable Energy Quiz and REGen Pavilion Among Key Attractions

The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Government of India, is organising the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRESE) 2026 from 2–5 November 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The Hon'ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, will inaugurate the Summit on 2nd November 2026.

Shri Santosh Sarangi, Secretary, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, Government of India, while addressing media persons here today said, “India's clean energy transition is entering a decisive phase. With 308 GW of installed non-fossil fuel capacity, we are firmly on course to reach our 500 GW target by 2030. Realising this ambition will require approximately USD 220 billion in investment between 2027 and 2030, alongside accelerated deployment of energy storage, stronger transmission networks and expanded domestic manufacturing capabilities. The Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 will provide a vital platform to connect global capital, technology and industry expertise with India's growing clean energy opportunities, translating investment potential into projects, partnerships and progress.”

The four-day event, themed 'Invest. Innovate. Inspire.', is expected to bring together participants from over 130 countries, including ministers, policymakers, industry leaders, investors, financial institutions, manufacturers, innovators, researchers and representatives of multilateral organisations. The Summit will be organised alongside the 9th Session of the International Solar Alliance (ISA) Assembly and the 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen (ICGH). The three events will provide a common platform for discussions on renewable energy investment, international cooperation, emerging technologies and clean energy deployment.

Australia, Denmark, the European Union, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, and the United Kingdom will participate as country partners. Delegations from several other countries are also expected to attend the Summit to explore cooperation opportunities in renewable energy financing, green hydrogen, energy storage, clean energy manufacturing, and technology development.

Thirteen Indian states will participate as Partner States and showcase their renewable energy potential, investment opportunities, policy initiatives and manufacturing capabilities. Other participating states will also highlight opportunities for renewable energy development and investment.

India ranks third globally in renewable energy and solar installed capacity and fourth in wind power capacity, as it advances towards its target of 500 GW by 2030. India invested USD 63.7 billion in its renewable energy sector during July 2024–June 2026, as per BloombergNEF. Building on this momentum, the Summit will bring together global policymakers, investors, industry leaders and innovators to strengthen international cooperation, mobilise investment and accelerate renewable energy deployment, particularly across emerging economies and the Global South. The four-day conference will feature high-level plenaries, ministerial discussions, CEO roundtables, and country and state sessions focused on financing, policy, technology, and skilling. Discussions will cover clean energy investment, emerging technologies, manufacturing, energy storage, and workforce development, with an emphasis on technology exchange, scalable solutions, and greater participation and leadership by women in the global energy transition.

The co-located 9th ISA Assembly will reinforce India’s global leadership in advancing solar energy by taking its successful policies, technologies, and implementation models to countries across the Global South. As ISA’s apex decision-making body, the Assembly will bring together ministers and representatives from Signatory & Member Countries to set priorities and guide collective action on solar deployment, financing and capacity building. Building on India's experience with flagship initiatives such as PM-KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar, ISA is helping countries adapt and scale proven solutions through country-led programmes, investment mobilisation, and institutional partnerships, translating India's renewable energy success into tangible benefits worldwide.

An accompanying exhibition will feature 400+ leading manufacturers, developers, technology providers, public and private sector companies, startups and research institutions from India and abroad. The exhibition will showcase emerging technologies and solutions across the renewable energy sector and provide opportunities for business networking, investment facilitation and technology partnerships.

The Summit will also recognise and award winners of the Bharat Renewable Energy Hackathon 2026, a pre-event initiative that brought together students, startups, researchers and innovators to develop solutions to ten real-world renewable energy challenges across two tracks: Early Stage and Growth Stage.

The RE National Renewable Energy Quiz 2026, conducted through regional rounds across the country, will conclude with its Grand Finale at Bharat Mandapam. The REGen Pavilion will provide a dedicated platform for students, young innovators, entrepreneurs and researchers to showcase ideas and engage with industry leaders.

The Summit will offer B2B, B2G, and G2G engagements, connecting investors, manufacturers, technology providers, and government representatives to explore investment opportunities, partnerships, and project development.

For more details, visit: www.bresummit.in

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Heavy Industries
Ministry of Heavy Industries and its Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) & Autonomous Bodies(ABs) observe Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 and Special Campaign 6
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 6:23PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) along with its Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and Autonomous Bodies (ABs) actively participated in the nationwide Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) – 2026 campaign, organized from 17th September to 17th October 2026 under the joint aegis of the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS) and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA).

This year’s theme, “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat,” underscores the importance of collective participation in promoting cleanliness, sustainability, and awareness.

MHI along with CPSEs and ABs has reinforced its commitment towards a clean, sustainable and progressive nation. As a part of the Campaign, 81 Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) were identified & transformed and 85 Public Places were cleaned. To raise awareness and to give wide coverage 286 tweets were posted on X (formely Twitter) highlighting the significant activities undertaken by the Ministry along with its CPSEs/ABs under SHS–2026 campaign.

MHI, along with its CPSEs and ABs, is also actively participating in the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) 6 from 2nd to 31st October, 2026.

Key targets achieved during the implementation phase of Special Campaign 6 till 27th    October 2026 are as under:

  • 1,424 cleanliness campaigns conducted across office campuses and industrial units.
  • 47,97,239 sq. ft. of space freed due to scrap disposal.
  • 34,440 physical files have been reviewed and 25,899 physical files have been weeded out.
  • 1,02,144 e-files have been reviewed and 93,606 e-files have been closed.
  • 3,839 e-waste items have been collected, segregated and disposed of.

Under SHS–2026, Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd. (BHEL) brought together the spirit of honouring mothers and protecting the environment through the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” plantation campaign. Tree plantation, Swachhata pledge and a walkathon marked Gandhi Jayanti and Shastri Jayanti celebrations organized at HPEP Hyderabad. 1,440 saplings were planted across 2 acres in the Piplani Township area at HEP Bhopal.

BHEL organized “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” plantation campaign at HPEP, Hyderabad and HEP Bhopal

Cement Corporation of India Ltd. (CCIL) Rajban conducted an awareness session at Primary School, Rajban on hygiene, waste segregation & plastic reduction. A Cleanliness Pledge was also taken by students at Primary School Rajban.

CCIL Rajban conducted an awareness session at Primary School Rajban

National Automotive Board (NAB) organized a drawing competition and group discussion in a school and a plantation drive was also organized under Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam at Manesar Gurugram.

 

Under the Clean Public Spaces initiative, HMT Machine Tools Ltd. conducted cleanliness drives at Ajmer and, a tree plantation drive was conducted under Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam campaign to promote environmental sustainability and a cleaner, greener future at HMT Township, Jalahalli, Bengaluru.

HMT Limited conducted plantation drives at the HMT Township in Jalahalli, Bengaluru

Bridge and Roof Co. Ltd. (B&R) organized cleanliness drives at Russel Street, Kolkata, and G.T. Road, Howrah, health check-up camps and tree plantation at Howrah Works, West Bengal, and Vadinar, Gujarat, promoting cleanliness, health and environmental sustainability.

B&R transforms Cleanliness Target Unit (CTU) at Mawdiangdiang Shillong, Meghalaya

SHS-2026 and Special Campaign 6 both witnessed active and enthusiastic participation from MHI and its CPSEs/ABs, reinforcing the spirit of collective responsibility and public participation towards a cleaner and greener India. The campaign reaffirmed their commitment towards promoting sustainable practices and advancing the vision of Swachh Bharat – Viksit Bharat.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From The Streets To Self-Reliance
A Journey Of Dignity And Renewed Hope
Rehabilitation And Livelihood Support Under The SMILE Scheme
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 6:14PM by PIB Delhi

At 46, Meera Thakur (name changed) could transform her life from one marked by homelessness, illness and uncertainty to one defined by confidence, dignity and self-reliance. This could become possible by the strong support and encouragement through great initiative.

Her journey reflects the role of comprehensive rehabilitation and livelihood support under the SMILE (Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

A Class XI pass who had previously worked in flower garland making and catering assistance, Meera faced serious personal and financial difficulties following a breakdown in her family life. With limited support, she moved between places in search of shelter and employment.

After losing her savings and essential documents, she fell seriously ill, lost her livelihood and eventually became homeless. With no dependable source of income, she sought alms at temples and other public places to meet her basic needs and medical expenses. Suffering from acute anaemia and extreme weakness, she required medical attention, sustained care and a safe environment in which to rebuild her life.

On 16 March 2024, Meera was rescued from the premises of the District Court Shani Mandir in Indore Madhya Pradesh by the Param Pujya Rakshak Aadinath Welfare and Educational Society (PRAWES) team and brought into the rehabilitation system. She was admitted to Aurobindo Hospital, where she received medical treatment and nutritional support for severe anaemia. She also underwent successful cataract surgeries in both eyes, helping improve her vision and overall well-being.

Under the SMILE Scheme, she received comprehensive institutional care, including safe accommodation, medical treatment, psychological counselling and sustained rehabilitation support. This secure and supportive environment helped her regain physical strength, emotional stability and trust in others.

As her health improved, Meera began participating in yoga, meditation and music therapy sessions. She also took part in a cultural programme during Ram Navami, portraying Shabri in a theatrical performance that reflected her growing confidence and willingness to engage with others. She went on to acquire skills in making carpets and door mats from old sarees, tailoring, pearl garland making, incense-stick production and crafting eco-friendly products such as cow-dung idols, diyas and havan kunds. In July 2025, she participated in a workshop organised by the National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), further strengthening her rehabilitation and skill-development journey.

Over time, Meera emerged as a responsible and respected member of the rehabilitation centre. She took on ward-management responsibilities and actively supported the well-being of fellow women residents. Today, she has moved beyond dependence on begging and is using her skills to earn a livelihood. She has taken responsibility for kitchen operations at the rehabilitation centre, independently preparing breakfast each day for approximately 50–60 beneficiaries. Her contribution reflects her culinary abilities, discipline and commitment to collective well-being.

Alongside these responsibilities, Meera participates in fairs, public markets and exhibitions to sell her handmade products, earning approximately Rs 8,000 per month. From an uncertain income of around Rs 200 per day through begging, she has progressed towards a more structured and dignified means of livelihood through handicrafts and other skills. She has regained confidence, developed leadership abilities and found new ways to contribute to the lives of others. She aspires to achieve greater financial independence, secure a stable livelihood and eventually live in an independent home with other rehabilitated women. She also hopes to use her experiences to support people facing similar hardships.

Meera’s journey demonstrates how rescue, healthcare, psychological support, vocational training and livelihood opportunities can work together to facilitate meaningful rehabilitation. Through sustained assistance under the SMILE Scheme, she has moved from vulnerability towards independence and from uncertainty towards renewed hope. Her story underscores the importance of a comprehensive rehabilitation approach that goes beyond immediate relief to help individuals rebuild their lives with dignity, confidence and opportunities for sustainable livelihood.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Textiles
Ministry of Textiles to Open PLI Scheme Portal for accepting new applications from 1st November 2026
Minimum Turnover criterion for Part 2 of the Scheme reduced to ₹100 Crore
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Textiles is set to reopen the application portal for the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Textiles for accepting new applications under Round 4 of the Scheme from 1st November 2026 till 31st December 2026 to promote the manufacturing of Man-Made Fibre (MMF) Apparel, MMF Fabrics and Technical Textiles, enhance domestic manufacturing capabilities, attract investment, generate employment and strengthen India's position in global textile value chains.

To facilitate wider participation under the Scheme, the following key modifications have also been made in the Scheme:

1. Reduction in Minimum Turnover Criterion: The minimum turnover requirement has been reduced from ₹200 crore to ₹100 crore under Part 2 category of the scheme, enabling greater participation by MSMEs and mid-sized manufacturing units.

2. Extension of Scheme Tenure: The scheme tenure has been extended up to Financial Year 2033–34 exclusively for applicants approved under Round 4. The extended tenure is intended to provide these applicants with a longer investment and operational horizon for establishing and scaling up their manufacturing capacities.

3. Migration of Existing Participant Companies of the Scheme to Round 4: All existing participant companies of Round 1, 2 & 3, in any part of the Scheme, that have not claimed or received any incentive so far, are also eligible to migrate under Round 4, subject to withdrawal of their existing applications under Round 1, 2 and 3, as applicable.

The online application portal https://pli.texmin.gov.in will remain open from 1st November 2026 till 31st December 2026. Eligible companies are encouraged to submit their applications within the stipulated period in accordance with the applicable scheme guidelines.

item.category: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
item.description: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Cabinet approves Rs 10,000 Crore Scheme to Make India a Global Container Manufacturing Hub Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme to raise domestic capacity ten-fold to 7.5 lakh TEUs and strengthen India's maritime supply chain Sonowal thanks PM Modi for Make in India push: A strong step to reduce import dependence and secure our logistics chain Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, today approved the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Cabinet approves Rs 10,000 Crore Scheme to Make India a Global Container Manufacturing Hub
Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme to raise domestic capacity ten-fold to 7.5 lakh TEUs and strengthen India's maritime supply chain
Sonowal thanks PM Modi for Make in India push: A strong step to reduce import dependence and secure our logistics chain
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, today approved the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme (CMPS), a Rs 10,000 crore programme announced in the Union Budget 2026-27 to build a globally competitive container manufacturing ecosystem in India. The scheme will run from FY 2027-28 to FY 2039-40, with three years for setting up facilities and ten years of production support.

The scheme will support new factories as well as the expansion of existing units. It aims to lift India's annual container manufacturing capacity around ten-fold, to 7.5 lakh TEUs, from about 70,000 TEUs today. Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal welcomed this announcement by thanking Prime Minister Narendra Modi for emboldening Make In India push in container manufacturing in the country.

"I express my heartfelt gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his visionary leadership. His Make in India push is giving our container manufacturers the confidence to build at scale, and this scheme is a strong step to reduce import dependence," Sarbananda Sonowal said.

India's trade depends on containers, but almost all of them are made abroad. India's container traffic is projected to grow from about 24 million TEUs in 2024 to 175 million TEUs by 2047 under the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision, which makes home-grown capacity critical.

What the scheme offers

  • Interest Subvention Assistance (Rs 859 crore): 3 per cent a year on eligible term loans for greenfield plants of at least 1,00,000 TEUs a year and brownfield expansions of at least 25,000 TEUs a year.
  • Operational Expenditure Assistance (Rs 8,891 crore): support for every container made to global shipping standards and sold by an eligible manufacturer, to bridge the cost gap with imports. Domestic content must rise from 70 per cent to 90 per cent.
  • Testing and Certification (Rs 150 crore): common facilities, such as dynamic longitudinal impact testing, to reduce dependence on overseas testing.
  • Scheme management (Rs 100 crore): administration, monitoring and capacity building.
  • Land at major ports: leasing support at 25 per cent of the notified rate.

An Inter-Ministerial Steering Committee chaired by the Secretary, Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, will approve guidelines and sanction assistance.

The scheme is expected to create about 3,000 direct and more than 50,000 indirect jobs, in steel, components and logistics. It will also support ancillary industries such as corner castings, specialised steel, wooden frames and paints. The government estimates it will generate about Rs 75,000 crore of economic output by FY 2039-40, more than seven times the support provided. Demand is expected from replacement of the global fleet, the Bharat Container Shipping Line, and new mega ports such as Vadhavan and Galathea Bay.

"Containers are the backbone of our trade. By making them in India, we strengthen the maritime logistics supply chain on which our ports, our exporters and our shipping lines depend, and we take another step towards a self-reliant India and the goals of Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047," Sonowal added.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Corporate Affairs

Demonstrating a…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Corporate Affairs
MCA’s cleanliness drive ‘Special campaign 6.0’ yield impressive revenue of Rs. 10,50,520 through e-waste management, recycling initiatives
MCA successfully addresses public grievances, resolving 316 out of 330 pending CPGRAMs, clear 217 public grievances out of 435 pending appeals
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) has successfully driven significant operational efficiency, cleanliness, and record management milestones under the ongoing Special Campaign 6.0. Demonstrating a strong commitment to institutional excellence and environmental responsibility, the Ministry recorded remarkable outcomes across multiple key performance indicators.

As part of the nationwide cleanliness drive, all 75 planned cleanliness campaigns were successfully conducted well before time. This year, the Ministry has exceeded its initial projections by initiating additional drives. This proactive approach resulted in freeing up of 15,740 square feet of office space and projections are that more space will be opened up as the clean-up continues.

Furthermore, the campaign yielded an impressive revenue of Rs. 10,50,520 through e-waste management and recycling initiatives, successfully processing electronic and electrical equipment.

In the domain of record management and grievance redressal, the Ministry made rapid progress by weeding out 850 files out of identified 2,523 physical files for weeding, alongside reviewing 8,823 physical files out of 9,309 target files. Additionally, the administration successfully addressed public grievances, resolving 316 out of 330 pending CPGRAMs, and cleared 217 public grievance appeals out of 435 pending appeals.

Parliamentary and PMO reference targets are also being systematically monitored to ensure timely administrative action.

These achievements underscore that the Ministry is dedicated to fostering a transparent, accountable, and citizen-centric governance framework by promoting sustainable e-waste recycling, reclaiming valuable office space, and accelerating administrative responsiveness.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tourism
Indian Culinary Institute Signs MoU with Jawaharlal Nehru University for Recognition of BBA and MBA Programmes
MoU to enable award of degrees by JNU to students completing BBA and MBA programmes at Indian Culinary Institute
Collaboration to enhance higher education and employment opportunities for students in India and abroad
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 5:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Culinary Institute (ICI), an institute under the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), New Delhi, today at Kartavya Bhawan, New Delhi. The MoU was signed by Smt. Santishree Dhulipudi Pandit, Vice-Chancellor, JNU, and Shri Gyan Bhushan, Director, ICI, on behalf of their respective institutions, in the presence of Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister for Tourism and Culture, and Shri Bhuvnesh Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Tourism. Senior officials from the Ministry of Tourism, JNU and ICI were also present on the occasion.

The MoU provides for the recognition of ICI’s BBA (Culinary Arts & Food Business) and MBA (Culinary Management) programmes by JNU, enabling the university to award degrees to students successfully completing these programmes at ICI.

The BBA and MBA programmes offered by ICI aim to develop highly skilled chefs and hospitality professionals to meet the growing requirements of the hotel, hospitality and allied industries. The programmes focus on equipping students with the requisite skills, knowledge and professional competencies to excel in the hospitality sector. They also seek to nurture culinary professionals who contribute to the distinct identity and offerings of hotels and restaurants.

The recognition of ICI’s BBA and MBA programmes by JNU, commencing from the next academic year, is expected to enhance academic and professional opportunities for students. The collaboration will facilitate access to higher education and improve employment and placement prospects for graduates, both in India and abroad, while contributing to the growing demand for skilled professionals in India’s hospitality sector.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Barriers To Global Innovation: A Journey Of Ambition And Opportunity
National Overseas Scholarship Enables SC Student to Pursue Higher Education at Brown University, USA
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi

Growing up in a middle-class Scheduled Caste family, Aarav Patel (name changed) aspired to build a career at the intersection of technology, business and innovation.

He envisioned establishing successful technology-driven enterprises and making a meaningful contribution to society through his work. However, limited financial resources, inadequate mentorship and a lack of professional networks in advanced science and engineering careers presented significant challenges.

The high cost of pursuing quality higher education at leading international universities posed a major financial barrier. In addition, limited access to experienced mentors and professional networks made it difficult to navigate advanced academic opportunities and understand potential career pathways in science and engineering. Despite these constraints, he remained committed to acquiring the knowledge, skills and global exposure necessary to pursue his ambitions.

The National Overseas Scholarship (NOS) Scheme provided crucial financial assistance, enabling him to pursue a Master of Science (MSc) degree at Brown University in the United States. During the financial year 2023–24, assistance amounting to US$ 89,816 was provided, with support approved on 26 June 2023. The assistance covered tuition fees, maintenance allowance, visa fees, medical insurance and travel expenses.

By addressing the substantial financial requirements associated with overseas education, the scheme helped the beneficiary access an advanced academic environment and acquire specialised knowledge, skills and credentials relevant to his professional aspirations. His international educational experience strengthened his understanding of technology, innovation and business development.

Today, the beneficiary is a business owner and director, working towards his ambition of building successful technology-driven enterprises. The qualification and exposure gained through his studies have provided him with a stronger foundation to pursue entrepreneurial opportunities. His family continues to belong to the middle-income segment, while the educational opportunity has expanded his professional horizons and equipped him with capabilities to pursue future growth.

The National Overseas Scholarship Scheme reflects the Government of India's commitment to expanding access to higher education for eligible students from Scheduled Castes and other specified categories, in accordance with the scheme's guidelines. By supporting tuition and other essential expenses associated with overseas study, the scheme helps eligible students access international academic institutions, strengthen their professional capabilities and pursue their aspirations.

The beneficiary's journey demonstrates how targeted educational assistance can help bridge financial barriers, widen access to global learning opportunities and nurture the aspirations of future professionals and entrepreneurs. From overcoming financial constraints to pursuing global education and entrepreneurship, his story highlights the transformative potential of educational opportunity in building a foundation for innovation, ambition and social progress.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Government Facilitating Startup-Industry Linkages to Take Indigenous Innovations to the Market, says Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh
Dr Jitendra Singh visits the exhibition at ESTIC 2026, featuring selected 50 deep-tech startups, 13 departmental stalls and 10 departmental technologies, reflecting the breadth of India’s scientific and technological capabilities
ESTIC-2026 Provides a Platform for Startups, Scientific Institutions and Industry to Explore Collaboration: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Indigenous Technologies Reflect India’s Growing Scientific and Technological Capabilities, says the Union Minister
Modi Govt Focused on Connecting Innovation with Practical Applications and Wider Adoption: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Dr. Jitendra Singh Urges Stakeholders to Leverage Opportunities to Strengthen India’s Innovation Ecosystem
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 5:15PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State for PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, has called for stronger linkages between StartUps and industry, emphasising the Government’s role in facilitating partnerships that can help indigenous innovations move from research and development to wider commercial adoption.

The Minister said that India’s expanding innovation ecosystem offers significant opportunities for startups to connect with industry and other potential technology adopters, develop practical applications and scale up their solutions. He urged stakeholders to come forward and make effective use of these opportunities to strengthen India’s innovation-led growth.

Dr. Jitendra Singh visited the exhibition of StartUps, scientific institutions and departmental technologies at the 'Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave' (ESTIC)-2026, being held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from October 27 to 29.

The conclave features selected 50 deep-tech startups, 13 departmental stalls and 10 departmental technologies, reflecting the breadth of India’s scientific and technological capabilities.

During his visit, the Minister reviewed a range of innovations demonstrating how scientific research is addressing challenges across sectors, from food and nutrition to advanced electronics. Among the exhibits was CSIR Designer Rice, a high-protein, low-glycaemic-index rice developed at CSIR–National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology (CSIR-NIIST).

The rice contains approximately 20 per cent protein and has a reported glycaemic index of 54, placing it in the low-GI category. Developed using rice fractions and structural modification, the innovation represents an effort to create food products with improved nutritional characteristics and potential relevance for people seeking better dietary management.

The exhibition also showcased JEET, the SCMC4212 microcontroller unit developed by Signalchip, reflecting India's growing capabilities in indigenous semiconductor and electronic-system design. Powered by a Yati 32-bit RISC-V CPU and an Avarta 32-bit digital signal processor, the microcontroller integrates memory, power-management and other functional capabilities in a compact design. Its potential applications include flight controllers, Internet of Things devices, smart devices, robotics and industrial automation. Such home-grown technologies can contribute to the development of domestic capabilities in strategic and emerging technology domains.

Other displays included bio-based packaging and reusable or application-specific products, illustrating the wider scope of innovation in materials and sustainability. Together, the exhibits demonstrate how India's scientific institutions, entrepreneurs and technology developers are working across diverse fields to develop solutions with practical applications, while creating opportunities for technology partnerships and commercial deployment.

Dr. Jitendra Singh has consistently advocated stronger coordination among research institutions, startups, industry and government to ensure that scientific discoveries translate into tangible economic and societal benefits. The exhibition at ESTIC-2026 provides an opportunity for startups to engage directly with prospective partners, identify applications for their technologies and explore pathways for scaling up their innovations.

The Minister urged industry leaders, investors, research institutions and other stakeholders to actively engage with startups and indigenous technology developers, build mutually beneficial partnerships and help take promising Indian innovations to wider markets. Stronger collaboration across the innovation ecosystem, he said, can help accelerate technology adoption, strengthen domestic technological capabilities and advance the national vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Substance Dependence To Self-Reliance Karim Nagar Telangana’s Neel’s Journey Of Recovery
Rehabilitation Support through the Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 5:01PM by PIB Delhi

Recovery from substance dependence help individuals rebuild their health, relationships and economic stability.

The journey of NEEL (name changed), a 25-year-old graduate from Karimnagar, Telangana, highlights the role of comprehensive rehabilitation and continued support in helping individuals work towards a healthier and more stable life.

NEEL began consuming alcohol and cannabis due to peer influence and family stress. Over time, substance use affected his work performance, health and family relationships. He experienced financial instability, social isolation, emotional disconnection and declining confidence. His family was also affected financially and emotionally, but continued to support him through treatment and rehabilitation.

On 22 May 2026, NEEL received support through the Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA) at Prakriti Environment Society in Karimnagar, Telangana. The assistance included medical treatment, detoxification, individual counselling, behavioural therapy, emotional and psychological support, and family counselling.

Vocational guidance, follow-up care and relapse prevention services further supported his recovery and helped him work towards rebuilding his personal and professional life.

Family motivation and comprehensive rehabilitation support helped NEEL develop healthier habits, strengthen family relationships and regain confidence. The combination of counselling, treatment and continued care supported his efforts to maintain sobriety and move towards a more stable and independent future.

Today, NEEL is maintaining sobriety, working regularly and earning approximately Rs 15,000 per month. His regular income has enabled him to contribute to his family’s well-being, while improved relationships and renewed confidence have helped him move forward with greater stability.

NEEL’s journey demonstrates the importance of accessible treatment, professional counselling, family participation and sustained follow-up care in supporting recovery from substance dependence.

The rehabilitation services provided through the IRCA at Prakriti Environment Society highlight how comprehensive support can help individuals rebuild their lives, restore family relationships and work towards social and economic reintegration.

***

item.title: INS SAHYADRI ARRIVES AT BUSAN, REPUBLIC OF KOREA, FOR INDIA-RoKN BILATERAL EXERCISE

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
INS SAHYADRI ARRIVES AT BUSAN, REPUBLIC OF KOREA, FOR INDIA-RoKN BILATERAL EXERCISE
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 4:58PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Naval Ship Sahyadri, an indigenously designed and built guided missile stealth frigate of the Indian Navy, arrived at Busan Naval Harbour, Republic of Korea, on 26 Oct 2026 to participate in the India-Republic of Korea Navy (IN-RoKN) Bilateral Exercise. The visit marks another step towards strengthening maritime cooperation and enhancing interoperability between the two navies in the Indo-Pacific.

INS Sahyadri was accorded a warm welcome by the Republic of Korea Navy (RoKN), reflecting the growing engagement and enduring strategic partnership between India and the Republic of Korea.

During the harbour phase, personnel of both navies will participate in professional interactions, cross-deck visits, cross-training activities and sporting events. These activities will facilitate the exchange of operational experiences and Best Practices, while fostering mutual understanding and professional camaraderie. The Commanding Officer of INS Sahyadri will also call on senior RoKN officials. The harbour phase will be followed by coordinated maritime activities at sea involving INS Sahyadri and ROKS Munmu the Great, providing opportunities to strengthen operational coordination, enhance interoperability and consolidate professional ties between the two navies.

The exercise underscores the shared commitment of India and the Republic of Korea to strengthening maritime cooperation and contributing to peace, stability and security in the Indo-Pacific. It also reflects the Indian Navy’s continued efforts to build enduring partnerships with friendly foreign navies through professional engagement and operational cooperation.

***

VM/SPS                                                                                                     216/26

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Gonda, Bahraich, Shravasti & Balrampur City, Prayagraj to Gonda and Gonda to Bahraich Highway under UPE LSA, during the month of September 2026
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 4:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted through its appointed agency across Gonda, Bahraich, Shravasti and Balrampur City under UPE LSA, during the month of September 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). The performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters, captured during IDT are published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services. These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc.

These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Bhopal. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area/ route under test on the day/ time of conducting the drive test.

The drive tests conducted across City drive – 367.7 KMs in Gonda, Bahraich, Shravasti and Balrampur and 2.7 Km walk Test in Gonda & Balrampur City and 256 KMs Highway drive from Prayagraj to Gonda and Gonda to Bahraich, from 7th September 2026 to 10th September 2026 in UPE LSA.

Drive Test Route Map: The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating City drive, Inter-operator calling, Hotspots and Walk tests, as per the legends shown on the map: -

Key Parameters Assessed

  1. Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G).
  2. Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence (Mute) Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).
  3. Call Silence (Mute) Instance: Number of call silence (Mute) instance occurred during the calls.
  4. Data Servies: Download/ Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate

The overall mobile network performance in Gonda, Bahraich, Shravasti and Balrampur City & Prayagraj to Gonda & Gonda to Bahraich Highway for the key parameters has been summarised below: -

  1. Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, were 818/ 19284 for Airtel, 7289/ 16823 for BSNL, 919/ 18995 for RJIL and 1775/ 19266 for VIL for Gonda City and 485/ 23477 for Airtel, 11807/ 19472 for BSNL, 1796/ 23226 for RJIL and 1369/ 23442 for VIL for Bahraich City and 114/ 8605 for Airtel, 3271/ 7994 for BSNL, 411/ 8466 for RJIL and 159/ 8666 for VIL for Balrampur City. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed.
  2. Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 1/ 171 for Airtel, 23/ 162 for BSNL, 0/ 171 for RJIL and 0/ 171 for VIL for for Gonda City and 1/ 205 for Airtel, 6/ 159 for BSNL, 0/ 206 for RJIL and 1/ 205 for VIL for Bahraich City and 2/ 78 for Airtel, 2/ 72 for BSNL, 0/ 78 for RJIL and 0/ 78 for VIL for Balrampur City. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map Annexed.
  3. Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances, measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 2/ 161 for Airtel, 6/ 166 for RJIL and 8/ 165 for VIL for for Gonda City and 0/ 196 for Airtel, 10/ 200 for RJIL and 1/ 199 for VIL for Bahraich City and 1/ 73 for Airtel, 2/ 74 for RJIL and 0/ 73 for VIL for Balrampur City. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed.

d)    Data Download and Upload Throughput:

i)  Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 94.98 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 1.15 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 167.44 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 34.31 Mbps for VIL (5G) for Gonda City and 105.94 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 7.30 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 146.74 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 41.12 Mbps for VIL (5G) for Bahraich City and 130.93 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 4.09 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 167.93 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 31.66 Mbps for VIL (4G) for Balrampur City. Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 14.59 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 1.86 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 18.94 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 9.53 Mbps for VIL (5G) for Gonda City and 17.60 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 2.88 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 12.09 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 11.86 Mbps for VIL (5G) for Bahraich City and 21.40 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 2.16 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 16.90 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 12.79 Mbps for VIL (4G) for Balrampur City. Detail of Upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed.

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map Annexed.

Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT is as under: -

  1. City – Gonda- Banghusra, Jhanjhari, Police line, Balpur Jot, Keswapur Pahrwa, Veerpur, Janki Nagar, Semra Damman, Tulsipur and Sekhapur etc.

Bahraich- Begampur, Godan Basahi, Mohammad Nagar, Bakshi pura, Dikauli, Doob Kalan, Pachdewari, Gilaula, Khutehna, Chakujot, Jagtapur and Kamla Bhari etc.

Balrampur- Harbaspur, Bishunipur, Bishunapur, Dhusah, Benijot, Pahalwara koeliha, Shravasti, Ikauna, Khargaura Basti, Gopalpur and Ararpakar etc

  1. Hotspots: District Court Gonda, District Hospital Bahraich, District Hospital Balrampur, Government Bus Stand Gonda, Government Polytechnic College Gonda, Railway Station Bahraich, Railway Station Balrampur etc.
  2. Walk Test: Gonda Junction Railway Station and Railway Station Balrampur etc.
  3. Highway: i) Prayagraj to Gonda- Passing through Mau Aima, Bela Pratapgarh, Sultanpur, Faizabad, Ayodhya and Nawabganj etc.

         ii) Gonda to Bahraich- Passing through Pipra Bazar, Manohar Jot, Suhelwa, Imaliya Ganj and Chilwariya etc.

Click here to see Annexure

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
MIB Extends IFFI 2026 Media Accreditation Deadline till 4th November 2026
Film Enthusiasts can also Register as Delegates to Experience a New World of Cinema
Posted On: 28 OCT 2026 12:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has extended the last date for media accreditation for the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 till 4th November 2026.

Media professionals planning to cover the festival, scheduled to be held in Panaji, Goa, from 20th to 28th November 2026, can submit their applications through the official Press Information Bureau (PIB) accreditation portal.

Eligible media persons are advised to complete their registration and upload the required documents before the revised deadline.

Registration Link: https://accreditation.pib.gov.in/eventregistration/login.aspx

For queries, applicants may contact iffi.mediadesk@pib.gov.in.

Accredited media professionals will have access to various festival activities, including:

•           Film screenings

•           Panel discussions

•           Interactions with filmmakers and cinema professionals

•           Networking opportunities

•           Other activities related to festival coverage

Media professionals who are already registered on the portal for previous edition (56th) of IFFI, can use the same credentials to log in and update their documents as required.

Apply early to secure your place at one of Asia’s most celebrated film festivals, connect with voices shaping the world of cinema, discover stories beyond the screen and be part of IFFI’s vibrant celebration of filmmaking, creativity and culture.

Furthermore, film enthusiasts who are not media persons may also register for IFFI as Delegates vide https://www.iffigoa.org/delegate-registration and enjoy the rich tapestry of films and other activities on offer at 57th IFFI 2026.

 

About IFFI

Born in 1952, the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) is South Asia’s oldest and largest celebration of cinema. Jointly hosted by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC), Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India and the Entertainment Society of Goa (ESG), State Government of Goa, IFFI brings together filmmakers, legends and emerging voices from across the world. With international competitions, cultural showcases, masterclasses and tributes, the festival celebrates diverse stories, languages and cinematic traditions against the vibrant backdrop of Goa.

For more information and latest details about the 57th IFFI 2026 please visit https://www.iffigoa.org/.

****

Mahesh Kumar/Aparajita Priyadarshini
