item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
Union Education Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi Inaugurates CBSE Experience Centre in New Delhi
Experience Centre to Promote Experiential Learning and Future-Ready Education
Fostering curiosity, creativity and confidence among students is essential to realise the vision of a developed India by 2047: Shri Pralhad Joshi
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 8:30PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Education, Shri Pralhad Joshi, today inaugurated the CBSE Experience Centre at the CBSE Integrated Complex, Dwarka, New Delhi. Established at CBSE headquarters, the Centre offers students an immersive learning environment taking them beyond textbooks. It provides an opportunity to explore the evolution of education, engage with emerging technologies, and gain insights into future career opportunities.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Pralhad Joshi emphasised on the need to move beyond rote learning and an excessive focus on examination scores towards an education system that recognised students’ individual interests, abilities and learning capacities. He highlighted that learning should extend beyond textbooks and enable students to understand concepts, apply their knowledge and develop confidence through real-life experiences.

The Minister said that the CBSE Experience Centre reflected the objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, which emphasised on experiential and holistic learning. He noted that such initiatives could nurture curiosity, encourage independent thinking and creativity, and prepare students to face challenges with greater confidence.

Highlighting the importance of practical learning, the Minister emphasised that students should not merely study scientific concepts but also observe, experiment, and understand them through hands-on experiences. Referring to the role of Atal Tinkering Labs in encouraging innovation and scientific temper, he stated that 10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs were already operational across the country, and that the government had decided to establish 50,000 additional labs.

 

 

Shri Pralhad Joshi observed that education should equip young people with the knowledge, skills and values required to contribute meaningfully to society and the nation’s development. Emphasising on India’s growing potential in technology, manufacturing and innovation, he underscored the need to prepare students for the evolving demands of the global workforce. Referring to the recently launched Seva First Innovation Challenge, the Minister noted that opportunities for practical experimentation and problem-solving can help nurture the next generation of innovators.

 

The Minister also expressed confidence that the Experience Centre would contribute to making school education more engaging, practical and student-centred. He emphasised that fostering curiosity, creativity and confidence among students was essential for preparing future generations to contribute to the vision of a developed India by 2047.

The CBSE Experience Centre will take visitors through the changing story of education in India. It connects ancient traditions with modern learning and new career opportunities. The Centre houses 12 broad zones and 21 exhibits spread across 6,000 square feet. RFID-enabled smart cards allow visitors to interact with the exhibits, participate in activities and access personalised takeaways and game-based leaderboards.

The experience opens with ‘Shiksha Ki Kahani’, a film narrated using a representational voice personifying river Saraswati. It traces the evolution of knowledge and education in India, from the gurukul system and historic learning centres like Nalanda to modern schools and digital classrooms. It also highlights the role of today's students in taking forward this legacy and contributing to the Viksit Bharat’s vision.

A special section tracks the rise of CBSE through historical photographs and archival material. This includes records from the year 1935 and provides a glimpse into the role of the Board in the evolution of the school education system. The Centre also introduces students to the history of Earth through a Visual and Interactive Geological timeline spanning millions of years.

The Centre will also introduce students to career exploration. Interactive exhibits such as ‘Career Explorer’, ‘Future of Professions’ and ‘Magic Mirror: Future You’ will enable visitors to explore different career options and understand how the nature of work may change in the years ahead. The experience also includes holographic interactions with eminent personalities including Dr. B. R. Ambedkar and Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

A dedicated kiosk on ‘Exam Warriors’, the book by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi focuses on encouraging students to develop a healthier approach to examinations. It highlights the importance of confidence, stress management and a positive attitude.

The Centre's final experience, ‘Eduverse’, combines motion-based interaction and multisensory elements. It will take visitors across various natural landscapes, from forests, oceans and the Himalayas to the Moon and other planets. It returns to Earth with a simple but important message: natural systems are interconnected, and every individual is part of this living planet.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
India widens its Maritime Partnerships in Busan, from Shipbuilding Supply Chains to Ship Recycling
Sarbananda Sonowal held bilateral meet with Marina Hadjimanolis as Cyprus Backs India’s EU Recognition for Ship Recycling
Sonowal leads talks on tapping Korea’s expertise to build Make-in-India LNG/LPG Cargo Tanks and Cryogenic Structures to boost Green Shipping
India's maritime transformation offers immense opportunities for stronger investment, innovation and enduring India-Korea partnerships: Sarbananda Sonowal
Korean maritime companies express interest in India’s growing shipbuilding, port infrastructure and shipping sectors
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 8:23PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal, held a series of meetings in Busan, South Korea, with South Korean maritime institutions, shipbuilders and shipping companies, and with Cyprus’ Shipping Deputy Minister, as India works to build the supply chain, finance, technology and markets behind its shipbuilding ambitions.

The talks covered shipbuilding investment, marine equipment manufacturing, maritime financing, port development, shipping, green technology and sustainable ship recycling. The government aims to make India a globally competitive shipbuilding, shipping and maritime services hub by 2047.

"India's shipbuilding landscape is on a fast growth trajectory backed by vision and policy initiatives of the Indian government led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi," Sarbananda Sonowal said.

Key takeaways from the day

  • Recycling: Cyprus backed India's bid for EU recognition of eligible ship-recycling yards.
  • Green Shipping: Korean makers and Indian yards explored partnerships in LPG and LNG cargo tanks, cryogenic structures and large ship blocks.
  • Finance: Sonowal presented the opportunity of Maritime Development Fund (MDF) and Sagarmala Finance Corp. (SMFC) to Korean maritime financiers.
  • Fleet and markets: Possibilities explored as leading Korean shipping line expressed interest to invest in India flagging, made in India containers and in the upcoming Vadhvan Port.

In a bilateral meeting, Cyprus' Shipping Deputy Minister, Marina Hadjimanolis, reaffirmed her country's support for India's effort to win European Union (EU) recognition for eligible Indian ship-recycling facilities.

The two ministers also discussed shipping, shipbuilding, maritime investment, seafarer welfare and maritime services. Hadjimanolis said about 25 leading Cypriot companies are expected to visit India in November to explore partnerships in shipping, ship management, maritime technology and related sectors. Both sides welcomed the India-Cyprus strategic partnership and stressed turning it into commercial outcomes.

"I look forward to working with you to translate our Strategic Partnership into concrete and mutually beneficial maritime outcomes," Sarbananda Sonowal said.

In his meeting with Kim Jin-jong, CEO of Sejin Heavy Industries, discussions focused on potential manufacturing partnerships in large shipbuilding blocks, LPG and LNG cargo tanks, cryogenic structures, which keep gas liquefied at very low temperatures, and other specialised marine equipment. The Indian delegation highlighted opportunities from new shipbuilding clusters and the expansion of existing yards. Cochin Shipyard Ltd (CSL) also explored block fabrication with Sejin, as it expressed their openness to evaluate its possibility. Building tanks and cryogenic capability in India would add depth to the nation's shipbuilding base.

“India’s growing maritime ecosystem offers immense opportunities for Korean expertise and Indian manufacturing capabilities to come together. A modern green fleet needs specialised capability, from cryogenic tanks to ship blocks. Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision, we are building that capability at home with the best partners in the world, and green shipping in India will be the stronger for it,” said Sarbananda Sonowal.

 

During his meeting with Yang Won-chang, President of the Korea Marine Equipment Research Institute (KOMERI), Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal discussed collaboration in marine equipment manufacturing, research and development, testing, certification, green propulsion and smart maritime technologies. The two sides explored institutional cooperation between KOMERI and the proposed India Ship Technology Center (ISTC), alongside opportunities for Korean marine equipment makers to partner with Indian companies. Sonowal invited KOMERI and interested Korean equipment makers to visit India and explore concrete areas of technical and industrial collaboration.

“We are developing the India Ship Technology Center as a national platform for ship design, research, testing and training. Testing and certification at home, with Korean technical expertise, will help Indian-made marine equipment meet international standards and prepare our yards for green propulsion and smart ship technologies,” Sonowal said.

Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal led Indian delegation had a fruitful discussions with Jay Y. Lee, Senior Executive Vice President led team of HMM on flagging its vessels in India, recruiting Indian seafarers, utilising Indian ship-recycling facilities compliant with the Hong Kong Convention (HKC), and expanding shipping services to additional Indian ports not currently covered by HMM's network. During the discussion with Ahn Byung-gil, CEO of Korea Ocean Business Corporation (KOBC), investment and business opportunities in India’s growing maritime sector, particularly in port infrastructure and shipping, were explored.

Sonowal invited greater collaboration between Korean maritime financing institutions and Indian stakeholders. India has approved a shipbuilding support package of about $7.8 billion, mega shipbuilding clusters are under development, and a pipeline of more than 400 vessels is worth an estimated $23 billion.

The meetings opened new avenues for cooperation with global maritime players, supporting India's goal of becoming a global hub for shipbuilding, shipping and maritime services by 2047.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Legislative Department Organises Medical Health Check-up Camp under ‘Special Campaign 6’ to Promote Preventive Healthcare and Employee Welfare
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 8:19PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the ‘Special Campaign 6’, the Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, organised a Medical Health Check-up Camp on 27th October, 2026, on the 4th Floor, Kartavya Bhawan-II, New Delhi, under the guidance of Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Legislative Department, with the objective of promoting health awareness.

Shri T.S. Muralidharan, JS&LC, attended the Medical Health Check-up Camp along with other senior officers and staff members of the Department. The camp was conducted by INDIA-AIDS (NGO), which facilitated the participation of doctors and accompanying staff from Rajiv Gandhi Cancer Institute and Research Centre. The doctors and accompanying staff provided medical consultations and guidance to the participants.

The Health Check-up Camp aimed to raise awareness about preventive healthcare, the importance of regular health check-ups, and the adoption of healthy lifestyle practices. The initiative also encouraged officers and staff members to remain conscious of their health and seek timely medical advice, thereby contributing to employee welfare and promoting a healthy working environment.

Shri T.S. Muralidharan, JS&LC, emphasised the importance of health awareness and preventive healthcare among officers and staff members. He also expressed his appreciation and gratitude to the doctors and their team for their valuable contribution, professional services, and efforts in making the camp a success.

The initiative, undertaken as part of 'Special Campaign 6', reflected the Department’s commitment to employee welfare and to fostering a healthy and positive working environment.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Union MoS Raksha Khadse Highlights Role of India-New Zealand Rugby Series in Advancing Sports Diplomacy and Youth Development
Rajgir, Bihar hosts historic U20 series marking 100 years of sporting ties, bringing young athletes together through international competition and cultural exchange
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 8:15PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Smt. Raksha Khadse addressed the significance of the India–New Zealand U20 Rugby Series in strengthening sports diplomacy, expanding international exposure for young athletes and advancing cooperation in sports development. Held at the Rajgir Sports Complex in Bihar under the 100 Years of Unity through Sport initiative, the series marks a century of sporting ties between India and New Zealand.

The historic India-New Zealand U20 Rugby Series concluded at the Rajgir Sports Complex in Bihar on Tuesday, marking an important milestone in the sporting relationship between the two countries as part of the 100 Years of Unity through Sport initiative.



 

The event was graced by Shri Samrat Chaudhary, Chief Minister of Bihar, Smt Raksha Khadse, Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India; Ms Shreyasi Singh, Minister of Sports and Youth Affairs, Government of Bihar; Shri Matt Ayers, Acting High Commissioner of New Zealand in India; Shri Sanjay Mayukh, President, Rugby Football Association of Bihar and Member of Legislative Council - Bihar; and Mr Rahul Bose, President, Rugby India.

100 years of India–New Zealand sporting ties

The series formed part of the 100 Years of Unity through Sport initiative, reflecting the role of sport in strengthening India’s international relationships and cultural connections. Bringing together young athletes from India and New Zealand, the exchange highlighted how sport can serve as a powerful instrument of soft power, fostering mutual understanding, friendship and long-term collaboration between nations.

India–New Zealand U20 Rugby Series Brings Young Athletes Together

Bringing together the U20 men’s and women’s teams from India and New Zealand, the series provided a platform for young athletes to connect through rugby, shared learning and cultural exchange. The programme featured joint training sessions, cultural interactions and four highly-competitive Rugby Sevens matches, including for the first time in history, two mixed-team matches in which national players from two nations played alongside each other, resulting in free-flowing exciting rugby. There can be no better example of sport dissolving boundaries.



 

Smt Raksha Khadse, Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India, said, “Under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India continues to strengthen its global engagement through sport, recognising its potential as a powerful instrument of soft power. The India–New Zealand U20 Rugby Series exemplifies how sport can transcend borders, foster mutual understanding and bring nations together through a shared spirit of unity and friendship. As India and New Zealand celebrate 100 years of sporting ties, exchanges such as this demonstrate how sporting partnerships can strengthen bilateral relations, encourage cultural dialogue and create lasting connections between young people across nations.”

Ms Shreyasi Singh, Minister of Sports and Industries, Government of Bihar, said, “Under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the guidance of Hon’ble Chief Minister of Bihar Shri Samrat Chaudhary, Bihar is committed to strengthening its sporting ecosystem and creating greater opportunities for young athletes. It is a matter of pride for Bihar to host this special India–New Zealand rugby exchange in Rajgir, celebrating 100 years of sporting ties between the two countries. Sport brings people and cultures together, and this series provides young athletes from both nations an opportunity to share experiences, learn from one another and build lasting connections, further strengthening international sporting collaboration and cultural understanding.”



 

Mr Rahul Bose, President, Rugby India, said, “The India-New Zealand U20 Rugby Series is about much more than the game itself. As we mark 100 years of sporting ties between our countries, bringing these young players together reflects the values that make rugby special: respect, teamwork and friendship. The mixed-team matches were a particularly meaningful part of this exchange, with Indian and New Zealand players standing alongside one another as teammates. We hope the relationships built here in Rajgir will endure and create a foundation for continued collaboration between Rugby India and New Zealand Rugby.”

The visiting New Zealand delegation comprised the U20 men’s team, Tama Toa, and the U20 women’s team, Hine Toa, featuring 24 young Māori players. Their visit provided an opportunity for the players to experience Indian culture while sharing their own traditions and perspectives with their Indian counterparts.

Strengthening Bilateral Cooperation in Rugby Development

The series also builds on the growing collaboration between Rugby India and New Zealand Rugby. In May 2026, Rugby India hosted New Zealand Rugby coaching educators at Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar for a coaching development programme involving 35 Indian coaches. The programme focused on strengthening coaching capabilities and supporting the continued development of rugby in India.



 

As India and New Zealand celebrate a century of sporting ties, the series in Rajgir underscores the power of sport to strengthen bilateral relationships, encourage cultural understanding and create lasting connections between young people. It also reflects the growing role of sport in India’s international engagement, demonstrating how shared sporting experiences can build bridges between nations and contribute to a more connected global sporting community.

***** 

Ayushman Kumar

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
BRO Celebrates Project ARUNANK’S 19th Raising Day in Arunachal Pradesh
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 8:13PM by PIB Delhi

Project Arunank of the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) celebrated its 19th Raising Day at Naharlagun, Arunachal Pradesh, on October 24,  2026, marking nearly two decades of dedicated service in strengthening strategic infrastructure and improving connectivity across the challenging terrain of Arunachal Pradesh.

Raised in 2008, Project Arunank has been instrumental in developing and maintaining vital border infrastructure amid rugged mountains, dense forests and difficult climatic conditions. Its efforts have contributed to enhancing the operational preparedness of the Armed Forces while improving accessibility, mobility and opportunities for communities residing in remote areas.

The Project continues to focus on engineering excellence and sustainable infrastructure development through the adoption of modern technologies and innovative construction practices. The use of alternative construction materials, geocells, slope-protection measures and other engineering solutions has helped improve the durability, resilience and long-term performance of infrastructure in demanding terrain.

The Project has also accorded special attention to the welfare of Casual Paid Labourers (CPLs) by providing improved shelters, protective clothing, sanitation facilities and regular medical camps. It remains committed to community welfare and environmental sustainability through cycling and yoga events, cleanliness drives, cyber-awareness programmes and the planting of 25,815 trees under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign.

Through its sustained efforts, Project Arunank continues to support the operational requirements of the Defence Forces while facilitating connectivity and progress in remote communities of Arunachal Pradesh.

SR/Ruchi

Verma Distributes PPE Kits And Ayushman Cards To Safai Mitras In Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh Emphasises Safety, Dignity, And Social Security Of Safai Mitras Under The Vision Of Viksit Bharat 2047 Over 88,000 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers Provided with PPE Kits Nationwide; Local Distribution Empowers Hundreds in Moradabad Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 7:41PM by PIB Delhi Under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme of Union…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Under NAMASTE Scheme, Union Minister of State Shri B. L. Verma Distributes PPE Kits And Ayushman Cards To Safai Mitras In Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh
Emphasises Safety, Dignity, And Social Security Of Safai Mitras Under The Vision Of Viksit Bharat 2047
Over 88,000 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers Provided with PPE Kits Nationwide; Local Distribution Empowers Hundreds in Moradabad
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 7:41PM by PIB Delhi

Under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme of Union Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, a major programme for the distribution of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits and Ayushman Cards, was organised at Peeli Kothi Civil Lines area, in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh, today.

The event was part of the ongoing flagship initiative aimed at strengthening the safety, health, and social security of Safai Mitras.

Hon’ble Minister of State, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B. L. Verma, distributed the kits and cards among eligible beneficiaries.

The event was attended by Shri Anunaya Jha, District Magistrate, Moradabad; Shri Ram Gopal Anjan, Hon’ble Member of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (MLC); Dr. Shaifali Singh Chauhan, District Panchayat Chairperson; the Municipal Commissioner, Moradabad; the Managing Director of the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC); officials from the concerned departments; and other dignitaries.

 

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Verma highlighted the NAMASTE Scheme, which aims to ensure the dignity and safety of sanitation workers and empower them socially and economically.

The Minister informed the a total of 90,194 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers (SSWs) have been verified so far, whileas 88,222 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers have been provided with PPE kits and 80,180 workers have been covered under health insurance through Ayushman Cards. In addition, 3,36,492 waste pickers have been profiled across the country, he further said.

 

Focusing on local implementation, the Minister noted that in Moradabad, a total of 307 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers have been profiled and provided with PPE kits, while 1,190 waste pickers have been validated through the profiling process.

 

During the programme, PPE kits and Ayushman Cards were symbolically provided to 20 Safai Mitras each on stage, followed by the distribution of PPE kits to an additional 813 Safai Mitras.

Shri Verma strongly urged beneficiaries to use the prescribed safety equipment regularly while performing their duties, follow safe working practices, and utilise healthcare protection facilities through their Ayushman Cards.

On the occasion, the District Magistrate of Moradabad and the Managing Director of the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation also shared their views, highlighting the invaluable contribution of sanitation workers and emphasising the need for coordinated efforts to ensure their safety, health, dignity, and overall welfare.

 

The programme reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to the principle of "Priority to the Underprivileged," ensuring that individuals who have historically been disadvantaged or overlooked receive the support they deserve.

 

 

This commitment to prioritising marginalised communities reflects the Government’s broader vision of "Viksit Bharat 2047," wherein every individual will have the opportunity to contribute to and benefit from India’s development journey.

item.title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026
item.dc:creator: Prime Minister's Office
item.description: Prime Minister's Office Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026 A Viksit Bharat will be built on strong foundations of scientific research, discoveries and the spirit of innovation: PM India must innovate and lead the world in shaping the technologies of tomorrow: PM India aims to achieve self-reliance and build strength in critical technologies: PM AI can give quick answers, but it is essential to verify them: PM Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 7:39PM by PIB Delhi Prime Minister Shri Narendra…
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026
A Viksit Bharat will be built on strong foundations of scientific research, discoveries and the spirit of innovation: PM
India must innovate and lead the world in shaping the technologies of tomorrow: PM
India aims to achieve self-reliance and build strength in critical technologies: PM
AI can give quick answers, but it is essential to verify them: PM
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 7:39PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026 today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Addressing the Conclave, the Prime Minister shared his enthusiasm following a lively interaction with startup founders earlier in the day. He praised the expansive vision and bold determination of the nation's youth. “The scale at which the youth of India are thinking and the self-confidence with which they are moving forward is encouraging,” remarked Shri Modi.

Recalling his participation in the previous edition of the Conclave, the Prime Minister contrasted past decades,when India merely played catch-up by adopting or modifying foreign innovations years later, with the new mindset of 21st-century India that aims to create original technologies, set global directions, and solve worldwide challenges. Citing how the nation developed indigenous COVID-19 vaccines to inoculate its population and supply other nations, alongside reaching Mars on its maiden attempt and landing on the uncharted lunar South Pole, he outlined a bold technological vision for the country."India must embrace the technologies of the future, innovate boldly, and lead the world in creating them,” asserted PM Modi.

Highlighting India’s rich heritage of discovery ranging from the invention of Zero and the number system to astronomy, the Prime Minister noted that the country is advancing this scientific legacy with modern technology and renewed confidence, as demonstrated by several milestones over the past year. With the nation set to celebrate the birth anniversary of Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha on October 30, he chose to begin his review of recent breakthroughs with the nuclear sector."Therefore, let us begin with Nuclear Energy,” remarked Shri Modi.

Emphasizing that building a Viksit Bharat requires massive nuclear energy capacity while reliance on imported nuclear fuel poses a challenge to energy security, the Prime Minister pointed out that the nation is rapidly advancing its Fast Breeder Reactor technology. He highlighted that just a few months ago, the indigenous 500-Megawatt Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor successfully achieved First Criticality. "This has been a major step in the direction of strengthening our Long Term Strengths in the field of Nuclear Energy,” noted PM Modi.

Stating that India's ambition extends beyond domestic energy security and technological self-reliance to expanding its footprint across critical technologies, the Prime Minister highlighted major space sector achievements this year, including an Indian space startup placing a satellite into orbit on its maiden attempt using a Made-in-India rocket and the country mastering satellite docking capability. He added that numerous domestic startups are introducing novel space science solutions alongside growing participation from young scientists and entrepreneurs. "Our goal is also to expand our power in Critical Technologies,” asserted Shri Modi.

Describing the sheer breadth of India's multi-sectoral achievements as unprecedented, the Prime Minister noted that this year the country hosted the AI Impact Summit, launched its own AI Model, and began shipping India-made semiconductor chips to the world. He also pointed out that the nation is actively building battery storage capacity anchored entirely in domestically available raw materials. "The diverse sectors in which India is achieving successes is unprecedented,” observed PM Modi.

Observing that while sectors ranging from nuclear and space to AI and semiconductors have distinct requirements, they collectively signal India's rising strength and confidence in emerging technologies, the Prime Minister spotlighted the nation's unique capacity to deliver 'Solution at Scale' so that domestic breakthroughs can solve global challenges. Pointing to the success of the Digital Stack and indigenous 5G technology, he emphasized the ongoing drive to build secure, population-scale platforms. "India is moving forward in the direction of developing such Secure Solutions which can reach people on a large scale,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Contrasting the historical tendency to view science and technology as weapons with India's philosophy of using them to serve humanity, the Prime Minister stated that true scientific success lies in stepping out of the lab to improve ordinary lives, solve massive problems, and strengthen healthcare, agriculture, education, employment, and disaster resilience. Expressing satisfaction that Indian startups are prioritizing these areas, he cited startups and domestic firms working on wearable EEG technology to understand brain activity, indigenous wireless and satellite communications, specialized nutritional products, new semiconductor technologies, and solutions to utilize industrial waste like steel slag. "The real success of Science occurs when it steps out of the lab and makes the life of the common citizen better,” asserted PM Modi.

Sharing his recent experience at IIT Madras in Chennai, the Prime Minister recalled inaugurating a modern Brain Centre that has created a globally exemplary brain imaging technology platform to develop high-resolution digital 3D images of the human brain and unravel complex neurological diseases. He declared that 'Science for Society' and 'Technology for Transformation' must serve as the ultimate benchmark for scientific progress."And India is moving forward by testing itself on this very touchstone,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Underscoring that a nation's technology creation capability and self-reliance in critical technologies depend on robust research,the spirit behind his slogan Jai Vigyan, Jai Anusandhan, the Prime Minister noted the rapid momentum of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation and recalled last year's pledge at this very forum to provide one lakh crore rupees for Research, Development, and Innovation. He highlighted that over the past year, 12,000 crore rupees committed by the government for market-ready lab technologies has been matched equally by 12,000 crore rupees from private investors. "Meaning, in just one year, a total new Commitment of 24 thousand crore rupees has been made for Research and Development,” noted PM Modi.

Spotlighting the steady expansion of the domestic research ecosystem, the Prime Minister pointed to a dramatic surge in intellectual property creation over the past decade. He noted that annual patent filings have grown from fewer than 50,000 ten years ago to nearly 1.5 lakh last year, reflecting a deeper structural shift beyond mere numbers. "They are a sign of that change in which Research and Innovation are becoming a strong Culture in India,” observed Shri Modi.

Posing a vital question for the second quarter of the 21st century on how scientific judgement will evolve in the age of AI, the Prime Minister noted that leading laboratory scientists and the Nobel Laureates on stage honed their acumen through years of solving small problems, experimenting, learning from failures, questioning established patterns, and spotting overlooked details. Warning that while AI can rapidly execute routine tasks to boost productivity, it must enrich rather than restrict independent thinking, allowing researchers to use saved time for harder problems, new experiments, and idea validation. "AI can give us answers quickly, but the responsibility of testing the veracity of the answer must lie with the scientist alone,” asserted PM Modi.

Urging continuous preparation of scientists and institutions for future-shaping domains through dedicated National Missions, spanning semiconductors, quantum technologies, biotechnology, advanced materials, robotics, space, clean energy, and next-generation communications, so that new breakthroughs emerge from India, the Prime Minister emphasized that safety and security must be prioritized across AI, synthetic biology, and autonomous systems. Warning of emerging AI-era cybersecurity threats to financial networks and national security, he called for developing AI-based and quantum security solutions that protect national systems and serve humanity. "Our goal is to develop such technologies which empower India and also contribute to solving the problems of humanity,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Calling upon every researcher, industry leader, startup founder, and student at the Conclave to set a concrete three-year target identifying which technology, prototype, pilot project, or product they will help develop, the Prime Minister urged them to drive innovations that build a Viksit Bharat and make India the global hub for solutions. He stressed that the gathering must move beyond mere discussions to deliver tangible results. "This Conclave should not remain limited merely to the exchange of ideas; may it become a platform for Measurable Outcomes,” asserted PM Modi.

Concluding his address by highlighting India's status as the world's youngest nation blessed with talent and resolve, the Prime Minister stressed the need to nurture a generation that actively leads rather than merely participates in emerging science and technology. Invoking the collective spirit and conviction of 'We will do it', he extended his best wishes for the success of the Conclave."We have to prepare such a generation which is not merely a participant in Emerging Science and Technology, but leads it,” affirmed Shri Modi.

 

A Viksit Bharat will be built on strong foundations of scientific research, discoveries and the spirit of innovation. Speaking at the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave in New Delhi. https://t.co/7VshP2K7GU

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
Ministry of Culture signs MoU with Bibliothèque nationale de France to strengthen preservation of India’s manuscript heritage
Collaboration to focus on digitisation, digital access, technology exchange, conservation and research on Indic-origin manuscripts
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 7:37PM by PIB Delhi

A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed and exchanged on 26 October 2026 in Paris between the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, and the Bibliothèque nationale de France (BnF) (National Library of France), under Gyan Bharatam Mission, to strengthen institutional cooperation in the preservation, digitisation, research and dissemination of manuscript and documentary heritage. The MoU was signed by Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Government of India, and Mr Gilles Pécout, President of BnF.

 

Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Government of India, and Gilles Pécout, President of Bibliothèque nationale de France

The partnership brings together the Ministry of Culture, through Gyan Bharatam, National Archives of India, New Delhi, and National Library, Kolkata, and BnF. It establishes a framework for cooperation across five key areas: Digitisation; Cross-Sharing on the National Digital Repository; Technology Exchange; Conservation; and Research & Development.

The Ministry of Culture and BnF will work to identify and digitise Indic-origin manuscripts and collections held by BnF. The MoU further provides for exchange of expertise and knowledge in areas such as digitisation and preservation technologies, cataloguing standards, OCR/HTR tools for Indian scripts, digital humanities and manuscript conservation. Joint workshops, capacity-building programmes, research initiatives, publications, exhibitions and exchanges of scholars and experts have also been envisaged under the partnership.

 

Gyan Bharatam Mission is the Ministry of Culture's flagship initiative dedicated to the identification, documentation, conservation, digitisation, translation, research and dissemination of India's manuscript heritage. Its National Digital Repository is envisaged as a secure digital repository for Indian-origin manuscripts and Indian Knowledge Systems held in India and across the world, enabling structured, permission-based access for research and study.

Bridging centuries of knowledge and heritage, the partnership marks an important step towards strengthening international cooperation for the preservation, study and wider dissemination of India’s manuscript heritage, while creating new opportunities for scholarly and technological collaboration.

item.title: English rendering of PM’s address during inauguration of the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026
item.dc:creator: Prime Minister's Office
item.description: Prime Minister's Office English rendering of PM’s address during inauguration of the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026 Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister in my Cabinet Dr. Jitendra Singh ji, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India Ajay Sood ji, all Nobel Prize-winning scientists, all other distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen. Today, such a large number of delegates from the world of Science and Technology are present here. Our young innovators are here as well. Before coming here,…
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
English rendering of PM’s address during inauguration of the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister in my Cabinet Dr. Jitendra Singh ji, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India Ajay Sood ji, all Nobel Prize-winning scientists, all other distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen.

Today, such a large number of delegates from the world of Science and Technology are present here. Our young innovators are here as well. Before coming here, I interacted with some startup founders. The scale at which India’s youth are thinking and the confidence with which they are moving forward is truly encouraging.

Friends,

I had attended this conclave last time as well. This time, we are discussing the subject of Emerging Science and Technology. Decades ago, there was a time when Science and Technology, for India, meant catching up. Whenever something new was innovated in the world, that technology would reach us after a few years. We would adopt it or make minor improvements and move forward. But today, 21st-century India is moving ahead with a new mindset and a new confidence. Now our goal is to create new technologies for India, for the world, for today, and for the future, to determine their direction, and to develop the capability to provide solutions to global challenges. During the COVID period, we saw an example of this. When many countries around the world were struggling with vaccine availability, India developed its own vaccine, carried out vaccination on a large scale, and also supplied vaccines to other nations. This is the confidence of 21st-century India. We reach Mars in our very first attempt. We reach the South Pole of the Moon, a place where no one had reached before. And that is why I firmly believe: India must embrace the technologies of the future, innovate boldly, and lead the world in creating them.

Friends,

From the discovery of zero to the number system and astronomy, India’s tradition has always been one of knowledge and discovery. Today, we are taking this scientific heritage forward with modern technologies and renewed confidence. Some examples from the past year help us understand this transformation even better. On 30th October, the nation will celebrate the birth anniversary of Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha. Therefore, let me begin with nuclear energy.

Friends,

All of you know that for building a Developed India, we will require nuclear energy on a large scale. Dependence on imports for nuclear fuel is a challenge to our energy security. Therefore, India is rapidly advancing its Fast Breeder Reactor Technology. Just a few months ago, the country’s 500-Megawatt Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor achieved First Criticality. This is an extremely significant and important step towards strengthening our long-term capabilities in the field of nuclear energy.

Friends,

Whether it is energy security or self-reliance in technology, India’s goal is not limited to fulfilling its own needs. Our objective is also to expand our strength in critical technologies. This year, India achieved new milestones in the space sector as well. An Indian space startup successfully placed a satellite into orbit using a Made-in-India rocket in its very first attempt. India also achieved the capability of satellite docking. Today, many Indian startups are bringing new solutions in space science. The participation of young scientists and entrepreneurs in the space sector is also increasing significantly.

Friends,

The range of achievements India is making across various sectors is unprecedented. This very year, India hosted the AI Impact Summit and launched its own AI model. The first shipments of chips manufactured in India have now started reaching global markets. In the field of battery storage as well, we are working on capacity building based on raw materials available within India itself.

Friends,

From nuclear energy to space, and from AI to semiconductors, the requirements of these sectors are different. But their message is one and the same. India is strengthening both its capabilities and its confidence in emerging technologies. India possesses another strength as well: solutions at scale. Whenever a solution succeeds in India, it creates pathways for solving the problems of many countries around the world. Our Digital Stack is a wonderful example of this. Our 5G technology is another example. India is moving towards developing secure solutions that can reach people on a large scale.

Friends,

You all know that one challenge in the world of Science and Technology has always been the tendency to see it as a weapon. India, however, believes that Science and Technology are instruments for the service of humanity. The true success of science comes when it moves from the laboratory into the lives of ordinary citizens and improves them. Lab to land, the success of this technology is not determined merely by how advanced it is. Its real strength lies in how large a problem it solves and how many lives it transforms. Therefore, for us, Emerging Science and Technology means solutions that strengthen healthcare, transform agriculture, create new opportunities in education and employment, and help in disaster management. I am pleased that India’s startup revolution is giving prominence to such questions. One startup is working on wearable EEG technology that helps understand brain activity. Indian companies are developing indigenous wireless and satellite communication solutions. In the field of nutrition, products are being developed keeping special dietary needs in mind. Indian companies are working on new technologies in the semiconductor sector. Solutions for utilising industrial waste such as steel slag are also being explored in our country.

Friends,

Just a few days ago, I had the opportunity to visit Chennai. I would like to share that experience with you as well. There, I inaugurated a modern Brain Centre at IIT Madras. This centre has developed a brain imaging technology platform that is a model for the entire world. This Brain Centre is working on developing high-resolution digital 3D images of the human brain. The success of this mission will help solve many complexities associated with neurological diseases. Science for Society, Technology for Transformation, this should be the benchmark of our scientific progress. And India is moving forward while measuring itself against this benchmark.

Friends,

We all know that a country’s technology and technology-creation capability depends on its research. Research is the power that enables a nation to find solutions to its own problems and become self-reliant in critical technologies. That is why I have said: Jai Vigyan, Jai Anusandhan! For a Developed India, we are continuously strengthening our research sector. With this resolve, the Anusandhan National Research Foundation is being accelerated. Last year, on this very platform, we pledged an allocation of one lakh crore rupees for Research, Development, and Innovation. Today, the results are becoming visible. In the past year, nearly twelve thousand crore rupees have already been committed to technologies that are ready to move from the laboratory to the market. And private investors are participating equally in this effort. Alongside the government’s commitment of twelve thousand crore rupees, the private sector is also investing twelve thousand crore rupees. This means that within just one year, a total new commitment of twenty-four thousand crore rupees has been made towards Research and Development.

Friends,

India’s research ecosystem is also continuously expanding. Patent applications have seen substantial growth. Ten years ago, fewer than fifty thousand patent applications were filed in an entire year. Last year, this number rose to nearly one hundred and fifty thousand. These figures do not merely indicate rising numbers. They signify a transformation in which research and innovation are emerging as a strong culture within India.

Friends,

In this second quarter of the 21st century, another question has become extremely important. In the age of AI, how will scientific judgement evolve? The scientists leading our laboratories have developed their expertise through years of experience. On this stage too, several distinguished scientists and Nobel laureates are present. We all know that they developed their understanding by solving small problems, conducting experiments, and learning from failures. A scientist does not merely repeat available information. A scientist questions established patterns. A scientist examines solutions from new perspectives. A scientist identifies aspects that others may have overlooked. It is through this process that scientific judgement develops. Today, however, in the age of AI, a new challenge is emerging before us. AI can complete many routine tasks very quickly. This can improve research productivity. But we must also ensure that AI does not limit scientific thinking and independent judgement, but instead enriches them. The time saved through AI should be used for addressing more challenging problems, conducting new experiments, and testing new ideas. AI can provide answers quickly. But the responsibility of verifying the truth of those answers must remain with the scientist.

Friends,

We must continue preparing our scientists and institutions not only for today's needs but also for future challenges. Semiconductors, Quantum Technologies, Biotechnology, Advanced Materials, Robotics, Space, Clean Energy, and Next-Generation Communications are areas that will shape the future. India is building strong scientific foundations in all these fields. For this purpose, several National Missions have also been launched. Our objective is that new breakthroughs in these domains should emerge from India as well. And our responsibility extends beyond innovation alone. Whether it is AI, synthetic biology, or autonomous systems, safety and security must be given priority. In the age of AI, new challenges and new threats are also emerging in cybersecurity. From our financial networks to our national security systems, everyone faces this challenge. Therefore, it is essential that we work on AI-based solutions and advance quantum security solutions that can secure the country’s systems against these threats. Our goal is to develop technologies that strengthen India while also contributing solutions to the challenges facing humanity.

Friends,

I appeal to every researcher, industry leader, startup founder, and young student present at this conclave to set a concrete goal for themselves. In the next three years, what technology, prototype, pilot project, or product will they contribute towards developing? Let us create innovations that support the making of a Developed India. Let us create innovations that make India a centre point for global solutions. Therefore, it is my hope that this conclave does not remain limited to an exchange of ideas alone. It should become a platform for measurable outcomes.

Friends,

Today, India is the youngest country in the world. We have talent. We have the resolve to create something new. We must build a generation that does not merely participate in Emerging Science and Technology, but leads it. Our spirit should be: We will do it. We will do it. Our confidence should be: We will do it. Once again, I extend my very best wishes for the success of this conclave.

Thank you!

DISCLAIMER: This is the approximate translation of the Prime Minister’s address. Original address was delivered in Hindi. 

****

MJPS/SS/VJ/ST

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
IGNCA and ASI to Launch Timeless India: Protection & Revival of Indian Cultural Identity
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 7:17PM by PIB Delhi

The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), in collaboration with the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA), will organise the launch of the book Timeless India: Protection & Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the Leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday, 28 October 2026, at 3:00 PM at Dharohar Bhawan, Archaeological Survey of India, Mandi House, New Delhi.

Published by IGNCA and Subhi Publication, the book will focus on India’s rich cultural heritage, its historic monuments and the importance of preserving the country’s civilisational legacy. It will explore themes concerning the protection and revival of Indian cultural identity, highlighting the significance of safeguarding the nation’s heritage and historical memory. Shri Tarun Vijay, distinguished author, journalist and former Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha), is the author/editor of the book.

The occasion will be graced by Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Government of India, as the Chief Guest. Dr. Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, Government of India, will be the Guest of Honour. Dr. Vinay Sahasrabuddhe, former Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) and former President of the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), will deliver the keynote address.

The programme will commence with a welcome address by Shri Y. S. Rawat, Director General, Archaeological Survey of India, followed by an opening address by Prof. (Dr.) Ramesh C. Gaur, Dean, Faculty of Arts, Media and Design, South Asian University. Shri Tarun Vijay will also be present at the launch in his capacity as the author/editor of the book. The programme will conclude with a vote of thanks by Prof. K. Anil Kumar, Head of Department, Kala Nidhi Division, IGNCA.

The launch will bring together distinguished guests, scholars and representatives from the cultural and heritage sectors to reflect on the importance of preserving India’s historical monuments, cultural traditions and civilisational heritage. The occasion will also provide an opportunity to engage with the themes explored in the publication and their relevance to the preservation of India’s cultural identity.

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
CONCLUSION OF 33rd EDITION OF SINGAPORE-INDIA MARITIME BILATERAL EXERCISE (SIMBEX-2026)
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 7:13PM by PIB Delhi

The 33rd edition of the Singapore-India Maritime Bilateral Exercise (SIMBEX-2026), hosted by the Indian Navy at Visakhapatnam, concluded on 26 Oct 2026. The exercise further strengthened the longstanding maritime cooperation and operational engagement between the Indian Navy and the Republic of Singapore Navy (RSN).

As part of the bilateral engagement, Colonel Bertram Ang, Fleet Commander of the RSN, called on RAdm Vishal Bishnoi, Flag Officer Commanding Eastern Fleet, and exchanged professional views on strengthening maritime cooperation between the two countries. The meeting provided an opportunity to discuss matters of mutual interest.

SIMBEX-2026 was conducted in two phases. The Harbour Phase featured Subject Matter Expert Exchanges (SMEEs), cross-deck visits, professional interactions, sporting engagements and planning conferences, facilitating the exchange of operational knowledge and enhancing mutual understanding. The Sea Phase in the Bay of Bengal involved Maritime Interdiction Operations, Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW), Anti-Air Warfare and Anti-Surface Warfare drills, seamanship evolutions and cross-deck flying operations, enhancing coordination and interoperability between the participating forces.

The exercise witnessed the participation of RSN ship RSS Supreme, a Formidable-class stealth frigate with an embarked SH-70B helicopter. The Indian Navy was represented by the indigenously built stealth frigate INS Nilgiri, ASW corvette INS Kamorta and participating aviation assets, including P-8I and Dornier maritime patrol aircraft, Hawk Advanced Jet Trainers and MH-60R helicopters.

SIMBEX has served as an important platform for strengthening bilateral maritime cooperation, operational interoperability and professional engagement between India and Singapore. The exercise also demonstrated the commitment of both nations to enhancing maritime security and promoting stability in the Indian Ocean Region (IOR).

*****

Discussions must lead to practical actions that cities can adopt, says MoS. item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
‘Opportunity for Shared Commitment to Improve Future of Our Cities’: Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs Opens ARISE Cities Forum 2026
Second edition of the forum brings together 200+ delegates from 50+ cities across 18+ countries representing the Global South.
Discussions must lead to practical actions that cities can adopt, says MoS.
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 6:55PM by PIB Delhi

The second edition of the ARISE Cities Forum opened today at the India Habitat Centre, New Delhi today. The two-day Forum is being organised by ICLEI South Asia, in collaboration with the National Institute of Urban Affairs (NIUA), with support from the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India.

Themed “From Bharat to Antalya — Commit. Implement. Deliver,” the Forum features 3 technical plenaries and 14 technical sessions, focusing on the experiences of local governments from the Global South region in advancing urban resilience, sustainability, and equitable and low-carbon development. The discussions feed into the Delhi Declaration on Local Action for Global Climate Goals 2026, which will be adopted on 28 October, 2026 at the forum and presented at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye.

The Inaugural Ceremony of the Forum was graced by Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India; Shoko Ishikawa, Country Representative, UN Women India; Dr Debolina Kundu, Director, National Institute of Urban Affairs; Gino Van Begin, Secretary General, ICLEI; and Emani Kumar, Deputy Secretary General, ICLEI and Executive Director, ICLEI South Asia.

Also present were Adv. Minimol V.K, Hon’ble Mayor of Kochi, India; Ismail Rafeeq, Hon’ble Mayor of Fuvahmulah, Maldives; Bhola Pokhrel, Hon’ble Mayor of Karjanha, Nepal; and Thinley Namgay, Hon’ble Mayor of Samdrup Jongkhar, Bhutan, representing urban leadership from across South Asia.

Appreciating the progress made since the first edition of the Forum, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs Shri Tokhan Sahu called for collective efforts to develop sustainable cities to fulfil India’s climate commitments and realise the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. “From resolve to planning, from planning to implementation, and from implementation to results—that should be our way of working. Our goal is to build cities where development reaches every section of society and creates better opportunities for future generations,” he said.

Calling for gender-responsive and inclusive urban development, Country Representative, UN Women India Shoko Ishikawa stated, “Drawing on the lessons gained from our initiatives in India, there are three priorities: integrate gender equality into urban planning, climate policies and investments; invest in urban infrastructure and services that strengthen women's safety, mobility and economic participation; and institutionalise women's leadership and accountability in urban climate action.” She added that UN Women looks forward to working with the ARISE Cities Forum to carry this agenda forward so that women and girls help shape the cities of tomorrow.

Director of the National Institute of Urban Affairs, Dr Debolina Kundu, noted that the theme of this year's Forum, "From Bharat to Antalya – Commit, Implement, Deliver," reflects the urgency of moving from climate commitments to action. “As we look towards COP31, it is important that the experiences, priorities and solutions emerging from our cities find a stronger place in national and global climate conversations,” she remarked.

Secretary General of ICLEI, Gino Van Begin, also spoke of the potential of urban local governments, stating, “Cities are developing innovative solutions, building functioning partnerships and demonstrating pathways towards more resilient, inclusive and sustainable futures. Their experiences and priorities must have a stronger voice in global processes such as the UNFCCC COPs, and this is what the ARISE Cities Forum aims to achieve.”

Emphasising the purpose of the Forum, Deputy Secretary General, ICLEI and Executive Director, ICLEI South Asia, Emani Kumar said, “The ARISE Cities Forum aims to amplify voices from the Global South so they are heard ‘from Bharat to Antalya’. We will carry the Delhi Declaration, a key outcome of our collective efforts and a shared call for stronger local climate action, to the global stage at COP31 to make sure that the perspectives and priorities of our cities and urban stakeholders are heard loud and clear.”

 

Advancing sustainable, equitable and resilient cities Across the Global South: Takeaways from Day 1 of the ARISE Cities Forum 2026

Day 1 of the ARISE Cities Forum 2026 featured 2 Plenary sessions and 8 technical sessions. The discussions, featuring high-level representatives from city governments, state-level bodies, embassies, UN agencies, development institutions, and experts, spanned topics such as

 

  • the need for strengthening multilevel action to translate global climate commitments into measurable action on the ground,
  • climate-resilient water management and sustainable energy transition in cities,
  • advancing urban biodiversity and nature-positive cities,
  • positioning entertainment and culture as an actionable lever for systemic urban resilience,
  • building resilient coastal cities and communities, and
  • integrating public health and child- and youth-focused initiatives with climate-resilient urban planning.

 

The winners of the Youth for Climate Hackathon 2.0 were also felicitated with the Ritu Thakur Memorial Award on Day 1 of the Forum. The Hackathon invited solutions on ‘Action-Oriented Transition: Translating Resilient, Scalable, and Inclusive Solutions for Circular Cities’ by young innovators from countries in South Asia.

A Memorandum of Understanding was also exchanged between Global Buildings Performance Network (GBPN) and ICLEI South Asia.

 

Launches on Day 1 of the ARISE Cities Forum

 

The Inaugural and technical sessions on 27 October also featured the launch of the following:

  • The Centre for Sustainable Urban Mobility and Integrated Transportation (SUMMIT)
  • Investing in Climate Resilient Cities - State-Level Project Pipelines: Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh & Telangana reports
  • Embedding Gender Equity and Responsive Transport - A Compendium of Case Studies for Gender and Mobility in India
  • A Compendium of Case Studies for Mobilising Funds to Enable Integrated Planning and Infrastructure Development
  • Policy Framework for Gender Equality in Public Bus Transport Systems
  • Guidelines on Canal Restoration using Nature-based Solutions
  • Poster for the ‘Early Action for Children’s Health (EACH): Towards Heat Resilience and Clean Air’ project in collaboration with UNICEF India
  • ICLEI South Asia’s Annual Report for 2025–26

 

Looking ahead to COP31

The Forum will continue on 28 October, with one Plenary, six technical sessions, and the Closing Ceremony, where the Delhi Declaration on Local Action for Global Climate Goals 2026 will be adopted and handed over to Samed Ağırbaş, COP31 Climate Champion and President of the Zero Waste Foundation. The Declaration will mark a key milestone in carrying the ARISE Cities Forum’s collective commitments and urban priorities forward to COP31 in Antalya, strengthening the presence of cities from the Global South on the global climate stage.

For more information on the ARISE Cities Forum 2026 and its agenda, please visit: https://arisecitiesforum.org/

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
DPIIT Launches 6th Edition of National Startup Awards to Recognise Innovation and Entrepreneurship
National Startup Awards 6.0 to Recognise Startups Across 20 Sectoral and 3 Special Categories, Introduces 12 New Sectors
National Startup Awards 6.0 Introduces Student Innovator Award, Offers ₹25 Lakh Cash Prize Across Eligible Categories
Applications for National Startup Awards 6.0 Open from 27 October to 20 November 2026
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, has launched the 6th Edition of the National Startup Awards (NSA 6.0) under the Startup India initiative to recognise innovation and entrepreneurship and strengthen India’s startup ecosystem.

The year 2026 marks the completion of ten years of the Startup India initiative, launched in January 2016 to build a strong, inclusive and innovation-driven entrepreneurial ecosystem in the country. Since its inception in 2019, the National Startup Awards have emerged as a flagship initiative under Startup India, providing a national platform to recognise entrepreneurial excellence and showcase innovative solutions addressing critical challenges across sectors.

The National Startup Awards recognise startups demonstrating outstanding performance in innovation, scalability, sustainability and socio-economic impact. Building upon the success of the previous five editions, NSA 6.0 seeks to strengthen India’s startup ecosystem by encouraging innovation-led entrepreneurship, fostering inclusive participation and promoting globally competitive startups.

NSA 6.0 will recognise innovation, entrepreneurship and excellence across 20 sectoral categories and three special award categories, reflecting India’s evolving startup ecosystem, emerging technologies and national development priorities. This edition introduces 12 new sectoral categories: Biomanufacturing; Consumer Industries; Defence & Security; Rural Economy, Traditional Industries & Livelihoods; Education & Skilling; Electronics, Semiconductors & Advanced Manufacturing; Sports, Fitness & Sports-Tech; Future Mobility & Automotive; Ocean & Blue Economy; Space-Tech, Drones & Aerospace; Telecom, Connectivity & Digital Infrastructure; and Travel, Tourism & Hospitality.

The three special award categories are Women-Led Startup of the Year, North-East Startup Excellence and the newly introduced Student Innovator / Aspiring Entrepreneur Award. Introduced for the first time, the student award aims to foster a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship among school and college students across all 36 States and Union Territories. It marks a step towards nurturing the next generation of innovators and entrepreneurs and expanding the reach of the National Startup Awards.

Winning startups across the 20 sectoral categories and the two startup-focused special categories will be eligible for a cash prize of ₹25 lakh per category, subject to the applicable award guidelines. The Student Innovator / Aspiring Entrepreneur Award will carry a total prize pool of ₹25 lakh across four sub-categories.

In addition to monetary recognition, the National Startup Awards seek to facilitate mentorship, investor engagement, market access, industry partnerships and enhanced visibility within India’s startup ecosystem.

NSA 6.0 aims to encourage participation from startups across States and Union Territories, including emerging entrepreneurial ecosystems in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities. DPIIT will engage Central Ministries and Departments, State and UT Governments, incubators, academic institutions, banks and financial institutions, Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), industry associations and other ecosystem stakeholders to support outreach, participation and evaluation under the awards.

Applications for NSA 6.0 open on 27 October 2026 and will remain open until 20 November 2026. Eligible startups and student innovators are encouraged to apply and showcase their innovations at the national level through the official Startup India portal at www.startupindia.gov.in.

Through the sixth edition of the National Startup Awards, DPIIT reaffirms the Government of India’s commitment to fostering an inclusive, innovation-driven and globally competitive startup ecosystem, while recognising entrepreneurial excellence and nurturing the next generation of innovators.

The 20 sectoral award categories under NSA 6.0 are:

  1. Agriculture, AgriTech & Food Systems
  2. Biomanufacturing
  3. DeepTech & Frontier Technologies
  4. Climate-Tech, Clean Energy & Sustainability
  5. Consumer Industries
  6. Creative Industries, Media & Digital Content (Orange Economy)
  7. Defence & Security
  8. Rural Economy, Traditional Industries & Livelihoods
  9. Education & Skilling
  10. Electronics, Semiconductors & Advanced Manufacturing
  11. FinTech, Financial Services & Inclusion
  12. Food-Tech, Biotechnology & Nutrition
  13. Healthcare, MedTech & Life Sciences
  14. Supply Chain & Logistics
  15. Sports, Fitness & Sports-Tech
  16. Future Mobility & Automotive
  17. Ocean & Blue Economy
  18. Space-Tech, Drones & Aerospace
  19. Telecom, Connectivity & Digital Infrastructure
  20. Travel, Tourism & Hospitality

The three special award categories are:

  1. Women-Led Startups
  2. Startups from the North-Eastern Region
  3. Student Innovator / Aspiring Entrepreneur

The journey of Mohan Lal (name changed) , a 65-year-old waste picker from Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh, highlights how social protection and healthcare support can help vulnerable workers overcome serious medical challenges and move…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Hardship To Recovery: Mohan Lal’s Journey
Healthcare Support Through the NAMASTE Scheme and Ayushman Bharat–PM-JAY
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi

Access to timely healthcare makes a life-changing difference, particularly for workers facing economic hardship.

The journey of Mohan Lal (name changed), a 65-year-old waste picker from Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh, highlights how social protection and healthcare support can help vulnerable workers overcome serious medical challenges and move towards a healthier life.

Coming from a financially disadvantaged family, Mohan Lal spent most of his life working as a contractual sanitation worker and waste picker, earning between Rs 101 and Rs 250 per day. His modest income was barely sufficient to meet his family’s basic needs, leaving little scope for savings or unexpected expenses. When he was diagnosed with a serious heart blockage requiring specialised treatment, the high cost of medical care became a major concern for him and his family.

Enrolled under the Waste Pickers component of the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme, Mohan Lal received an Ayushman Card under Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY). This support enabled him to access treatment for his heart blockage at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, on 8 May 2026, with the full cost of his medical treatment covered.

Following successful treatment, Mohan Lal recovered and was able to return to work and resume supporting his family. Access to healthcare eased the financial burden associated with his medical emergency and helped him focus on recovery. The timely intervention also restored his confidence and provided renewed hope for the future.

Mohan Lal’s journey demonstrates the importance of accessible healthcare and social protection for waste pickers and other vulnerable workers. His recovery reflects how welfare initiatives can help reduce barriers to essential medical treatment, safeguard dignity and strengthen family well-being. His story stands as an encouraging example of how timely support can help individuals move beyond difficult circumstances and look towards the future with renewed confidence.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Special Campaign 6: Department of Posts Organises Dedicated One-day Nationwide Activities
Department of Posts Holds 1,861 Dak Chaupals
Cleanliness activities cover 55,952 sites; Resolves 9,007 Public Grievances
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 6:40PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Posts, Ministry of Communications, organised 1,861 Dak Chaupals across the country on 23rd October 2026 as part of Special Campaign 6, strengthening citizen engagement and bringing postal and government services closer to the people. This dedicated one-day programme also witnessed cleanliness activities at approximately 55,952 sites nationwide and the resolution of 9,007 public grievances.

Undertaken in response to the initiative of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), the programme focused on citizen outreach, grievance redressal, cleanliness, environmental sustainability and improvement of postal infrastructure.

Dak Chaupals: Bringing Government Services to Citizens

Dak Chaupals served as platforms for direct interaction between postal officials and citizens, facilitating awareness of postal and citizen-centric services, addressing public grievances and obtaining feedback to improve service delivery.

Activities included awareness and facilitation of Postal Life Insurance (PLI) and Rural Postal Life Insurance (RPLI) schemes, promotion of accessible postal services and engagement with local communities. The resolution of   9,007 public grievances during the programme further reflects the Department’s commitment to responsive governance and timely redressal of citizens’ concerns.

Nationwide Cleanliness and Environmental Sustainability Drives

Special cleanliness drives were undertaken across post offices, including Branch Post Offices, mail offices and administrative establishments. Cleanliness activities covered 55,952 sites, contributing to cleaner surroundings and improved public spaces.

Postal Circles also undertook initiatives to promote environmental sustainability, including awareness campaigns on waste segregation, composting and responsible waste management. These activities encouraged community participation and reinforced the principles of Swachhata and environmental responsibility.

Infrastructure Improvement and Community Engagement

Postal establishments undertook initiatives to improve office infrastructure, enhance public-facing areas and ensure better utilisation of available space. Creative beautification, maintenance and other improvement activities contributed to cleaner and more welcoming postal establishments.

The dedicated one-day programme reflects the Department of Posts commitment to the objectives of Special Campaign 6, particularly institutionalising cleanliness, strengthening grievance redressal, improving citizen engagement and promoting sustainable practices.

The Department will continue to build on these initiatives to make postal establishments cleaner, more accessible and more responsive to citizens’ needs.

Chief Guest for the Launching and Keel Laying Ceremony was RAdm Kapil Mehta, Assistant Controller of Warship Production and Acquisition (ACWP&A).

The contract for construction of Four 300T Sullage Barge and Three Bottom Opening Dumb Barge was concluded with M/s Suryadipta Projects Pvt Ltd, Thane, an MSME Shipyard, in Nov 2024 and Jan 2026 respectively.

These Barges have been indigenously designed and built by the shipyard in collaboration with an Indian Ship Design firm and Indian Register of Shipping (IRS) respectively. The Barges will aid in operations of Indian Navy platforms and compliance with MARPOL regulations.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Ministry Organises Health Check-up Camp and ‘Samvaad’ for Safai Mitras under Special Campaign 6.0
Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare Shri Prataprao Jadhav Reviews Cleanliness at Ministry’s Offices, Visits Health Check-up Camp and Interacts with Safai Mitras
Health Screening and Medical Consultations Organised for Safai Mitras as Part of Kayakalp Activities under Special Campaign 6.0
‘Samvaad’ Programme Recognises Contributions of Safai Mitras and Reinforces the Importance of Sustaining a Culture of Cleanliness
Posted On: 27 OCT 2026 6:06PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the ongoing Special Campaign 6.0, the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare organised a health check-up camp and a ‘Samvaad’ programme for Safai Mitras (sanitation workers) at Kartavya Bhawan-1. Conducted under the Ministry’s Kayakalp activities, the initiatives focused on promoting the health and well-being of Safai Mitras, recognising their contribution to maintaining hygienic workplaces and strengthening a culture of cleanliness.

Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare and Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush, Shri Prataprao Jadhav visited the health check-up camp and interacted with Safai Mitras. During the visit, he enquired about their health and well-being and expressed appreciation for their dedicated efforts in maintaining cleanliness and hygiene across the Ministry’s premises. Dr. L.G. Krishna, Director General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, was also present.

As part of Special Campaign 6.0, Shri Jadhav also undertook a round of the Ministry’s office premises to take stock of cleanliness and hygiene. During the visit, he reviewed the cleanliness of the office premises and took stock of the upkeep of the working environment.

The health check-up camp provided Safai Mitras with essential health screening and consultation services, including Body Mass Index (BMI) assessment based on height and weight, blood pressure measurement, blood sugar testing and haemoglobin testing. General medicine consultations, basic eye check-ups and Ear, Nose and Throat (ENT) examinations were also conducted to assess their health status and facilitate early identification of potential health concerns.

As part of the Special Campaign 6.0 activities, the Ministry also organised a ‘Samvaad’ programme to acknowledge the important role of Safai Mitras in ensuring clean and hygienic workplaces. Joint Secretary Shri Elangbam Robert Singh interacted with the Safai Mitras and thanked them for their dedicated service. He emphasised the importance of making cleanliness an integral part of everyday life, maintaining hygienic surroundings and instilling these values in future generations. The programme also provided Safai Mitras with an opportunity to share their experiences, feedback and suggestions.

The initiatives under Special Campaign 6.0 underscored the Ministry’s commitment to promoting cleanliness alongside the health, dignity and well-being of those who play a vital role in maintaining hygienic workplaces. By bringing together cleanliness reviews, preventive healthcare, recognition and dialogue, the Ministry reinforced the importance of collective responsibility and sustained efforts towards a clean, healthy and inclusive working environment.

***
