item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
English rendering of PM’s address in the 139th Episode of Mann Ki Baat on 25.10.2026
Posted On: 25 OCT 2026 11:45AM by PIB Delhi

My dear countrymen,

Welcome once again to ‘Mann Ki Baat’. Twelve years ago, on the pious occasion of Vijayadashami, we began ‘Mann Ki Baat’. Since then, this journey of our’s has continued without a break. You are both my fellow travellers and my guides on this path. Friends, for me, ‘Mann Ki Baat’ has been an auspicious opportunity to proudly celebrate the hard work, valour, commitment, dedication, and spirit of service of the common people of our nation. Our country has had a long-standing tradition of Teerth Yatra. ‘Mann Ki Baat’ is, for me, nothing less than a pilgrimage - a journey to closely understand the efforts of our people and to salute their contributions. Friends, those who live for society and the nation are, in themselves, like a ‘Teerth’. Over these 12 years, many individuals from every corner of the country have come to the fore - people whose extraordinary work often goes unnoticed by society at large. ‘Mann Ki Baat’ has served to bring such countless, inspiring stories to all of you.

Friends,

Through this program, I am, in a sense, paying obeisance to the ‘collective strength of the people’; Lok-Shakti of our nation. It provides me with an opportunity to connect with every family across the country. I receive hundreds of messages in which people share that listening to ‘Mann Ki Baat’ makes them feel as though I am amidst them - like a member of their own family - engaging in a conversation. For me, this deep connection and the affection shown by all of you - my listeners - is a priceless treasure.

My dear countrymen,

Our nation possesses many traditional skills that have been a part of our identity for generations. And it is heartening to see that these traditions are now being integrated with diverse, innovative approaches, allowing them to evolve and remain relevant to the present day. One such initiative has been underway in Punjab for some time; an organization called ‘Kheti Virasat Mission’ has begun to breathe new life into organic farming and traditional agricultural practices. The team aimed to promote natural cotton cultivation in the Malwa region of Punjab. This initiative was named ‘Nav-Trinjan’.

Under this project, organic cotton is grown there without the use of any chemicals. They also cultivate cotton that possesses natural colors, eliminating the need for additional chemicals to dye the resulting yarn or fabric. You can imagine what a significant contribution this makes towards protecting the environment.

Friends,

A few years ago, ‘Nav-Trinjan’ also established a weaving school with the goal of passing on the craft of weaving to the next generation. This school has transformed the lives of many women. Ramandeep Kaur ji is one such example; she previously worked as a labourer, but following her training at the school, she is now recognized as a skilled weaver. Rekha Rani ji had never even seen a handloom before undergoing training; a shawl woven by her has been presented to the Honorable President of India. Similarly, Suneha Devi ji, who once worked as a domestic help, is now creating exquisite fabrics on a handloom. Rajni Kaur ji, who once depended on manual labour in the fields, has found that her new skills have significantly helped her in supporting her household.

Following training from the school, many such women are now crafting shawls, towels, and other textiles using yarn made from indigenous organic cotton. These efforts are bringing prosperity to their lives. A few months ago, on National Handloom Day, I too had the opportunity to meet this team. During that, I experienced their passion and dedication towards their work. I extend my heartfelt best wishes to the entire team for a bright future.

My dear countrymen,

We have had a long-standing tradition of respecting nature. Our ancestors taught us that maintaining cleanliness in our surroundings and caring for water sources is our own responsibility. It brings me great joy to see so many people across the country embodying this spirit. The same sentiment can also be seen in the Tehri Garhwal region of Uttarakhand. There, people have come together in an effort to breathe new life into a river - the 'Heval' river. Some time ago, the water level in the Heval river began to decline… the natural water sources in the surrounding area were also drying up. In this scenario, the local administration and the villagers joined forces to launch a campaign to save the Heval river.

Measures were undertaken to capture rainwater, facilitate groundwater recharge and plant a large number of trees. Today, thanks to these efforts, the Heval river has been revitalized and simultaneously dozens of natural water sources have received help in their restoration.

Friends,

When a society unites imbuing such a spirit, change is definitely guaranteed. We can see a glimpse of that in our festivals as well. In just a few days, the auspicious festivals of Diwali and Chhath are approaching; For that, cleanliness drives are being run at many places. It is essential that we maintain the cleanliness of the places where we live. Only our small, individual efforts can bring about significant change in our surroundings.

My dear countrymen,

During this festive season, you must have noticed a shift in your surroundings. People are now placing great importance on Swadeshi products while shopping. This spirit of 'Vocal for Local' is now taking our products to global markets.

For instance, *makhana* from Purnia in Bihar is now reaching Greece, and *arhar dal* from Kalaburagi in Karnataka is being exported to the Maldives - meaning, new global markets are opening up for India's farmers. Friends, while discussing local products, I would like to draw your attention to another important aspect: the packaging of a product is just as significant as its quality. Often, when we see an item in the market, it is its attractive packaging that draws us to pick it up. We want to know about a product just by looking at its packaging. Realizing that, there is now an increasing emphasis on packaging.

Friends,

In Maharashtra, tribal communities have placed a strong focus on the packaging of the products they create. There, through an initiative called ‘Shabari Naturals,’ products like honey, mahua, chironji and bamboo-based items are being brought to the market - their packaging reflects tribal art. You will be pleased to know that this packaging has received Japan’s prestigious ‘Good Design Award.’ Our youth are also experimenting anew in this field; a ‘bamboo’ start-up in Karnataka is creating packaging material from bamboo and agricultural residue.

Friends,

When we talk about local products, it is only natural to mention Khadi. This time on Gandhi Jayanti, sales of the products of Khadi Gram Udyog exceeded ₹28 crore in a single day. It is an increase of ₹1.5 crore over the previous year. This means that the popularity of Khadi continues to grow, and the benefits are reaching those whose skills and hard work bring items like Khadi and various handicrafts to life.

Friends,

During the festive season, we often buy many things for our families and loved ones. This time too, do prioritize products made by local artisans when you shop; your purchases will boost their morale. This sense of affection will further strengthen the ‘Vocal for Local’ movement. As this movement gains momentum, the dream of ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ will be realized all the faster. For that, I personally urge you to prioritize and highlight products crafted by local artisans.

My dear countrymen,

There’s a remarkable trait of our people… we quickly embrace new technology. We naturally integrate technology into our daily lives - the ‘e-Sanjeevani’ yojana is an excellent example of that. This demonstrates how technology can be effectively utilized to make people's lives easier. It gives me great satisfaction to note that approximately 50 crore tele-consultations have been conducted through this platform so far – It is a massive figure. It serves as an excellent testament to the power of technology, the dedicated spirit of our doctors, and the trust placed in the system by our countrymen.

Friends,

Today, through its extensive network, the 'e-Sanjeevani' service has reached even the remotest corners of the country. The stories of those who have benefited from it will make you emotional. In the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Oho-Tahane, from the Jarawa tribe on Baratang Island, was suffering from a high fever… breathing too was getting difficult. Amid that, local health workers used e-Sanjeevani to consult an expert doctor. The child had pneumonia; once he came under the care of the expert doctor, his condition began to improve rapidly.

Friends,

In Kalpeni, Lakshadweep, a man named Kunhi Koya—around 60 years of age - suddenly fell ill. Through e-Sanjeevani, contact was established with an experienced doctor located across the sea in Kavaratti. That experienced doctor provided guidance to the local medical team, which helped bring relief to Kunhi Koya. In Zanskar, Ladakh, Kunjang Dolma experienced some complications during her pregnancy; during that situation, e-Sanjeevani worked for her, allowing a specialist doctor to provide immediate assistance. In Peren, Nagaland, a 12-year-old boy named Mushem suffered from an ear infection and fever; he, too, benefited from e-Sanjeevani… The expert doctor was able to promptly diagnose his condition and recommend the appropriate medication.

Friends,

There was a time when even a simple health check-up or a visit to a doctor would take a long time and involve significant hardship. Today, nearly 190,000 'Ayushman Arogya Mandirs' across the country have brought new facilities into people's lives. These Arogya Mandirs are in a way, evolving into wellness centres for village panchayats.

It’s most heartening to know that, people in rural areas are now undergoing regular health check-ups to stay healthy, in which 'e-Sanjeevani' is playing a vital role.

My dear countrymen,

Earlier this month, I visited Chennai. There I met many of the nation's scientists, researchers, and young talents. Our youth are currently working on subjects that have the potential to transform the future of all humanity; one such field is 'Brain Research.' In that connection, I inaugurated the 'Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre' at IIT Madras. This centre has developed a brain-imaging technology platform that serves as a global benchmark. Through that, high-resolution, digital 3D images of the human brain, are being created, with the goal of mapping and studying 100 human brains in minute detail. This is the first mission of its kind in the world, and it utilizes the 'Param Shakti' supercomputer.

Friends,

The nation's industry has played a significant role, in collaboration with the government, in establishing this brain centre. Many IIT alumni and academia have also come together to support this research centre. This project is of immense importance because, despite significant scientific progress, the human brain remains a major scientific enigma. Even in the present day, conditions like Alzheimer's and Dementia still lack a definitive cure. Therefore, the deeper our scientific understanding of how the human brain functions, the more new scope will be created in the future. It has also been decided that this data from 100 human brains will be made available as an open-source resource for research across various fields.

Friends,

Organ donation plays a vital role in such advanced research. Those who choose to donate their organs after their lifetime not only save the lives of many others but also make research possible. One such example is that of Shivani-ji from Narmadapuram in Madhya Pradesh.

Shivani ji had met with a road accident; while this brought a great tragedy upon her family, even in such a difficult time, they made a decision that serves as an inspiration to us all - the decision was to donate Shivani ji’s organs. This choice by Shivani ji’s family sends a powerful message to society and the nation. Such a step of humanity can bring happiness back into a family’s life, while also providing significant support to research efforts.

My dear countrymen,

I would also like to share some other experiences from my visit to Chennai. The first was my interaction with young people on the metro, while another was my visit to IIT Madras. It was truly heartening to see how our youth are working on innovative solutions to problems. One of the start-ups I met focuses on verifying the quality of gold, which can help prevent fraud in gold purchases. Another team of young people is developing a platform that could enable the rapid recovery of funds lost to bank fraud. Meanwhile, another team is exploring how AI can assist in the screening for cervical cancer.

Friends,

The interaction at IIT was entirely focused on 'deep-tech.' These start-ups are being supported by the incubation ecosystem at IIT Madras. Among them is a start-up that is developing an electric vehicle capable of flying over the sea. Another start-up is developing fast-charging batteries for drones and electric vehicles. One team is working on the application of AI in defence technology.

Friends, our youth are achieving such extraordinary things today because they are receiving the right environment and support. It is not as if there has ever been a shortage of talent in our country. In just a few days, on October 31st, we will mark the 100th birth anniversary of one such great Indian scientist, Narinder Singh Kapany. The world knows him as the 'Father of Fiber Optics.' He was born in the Moga district of Punjab. His advanced research into the technology of transmitting light through thin fibers lent a new direction to the world of communication. It is difficult to even imagine the era of internet and digital communication that we live in today without fiber optics.

On this occasion, we pay our respects to Narinder Singh Kapany. I would like our youth to read and learn about scientists like him, and draw inspiration from them.

Friends,

Just in a few days, the 31st of October marks the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel - a day the nation observes as 'Ekta Diwas'. On this occasion, a 'Run for Unity' is organized across the country. ‘Run For Unity’ offers a significant opportunity to strengthen our unity and reaffirm our commitment to the nation. I urge all of you to participate enthusiastically in this year’s 'Run for Unity' and to bring along your family, friends, and those around you.

Friends,

You may recall that, at India’s call, 2023 was celebrated as the 'International Year of Millets.' It received a very positive response globally. Through this initiative, people discovered how deeply the superfood 'Shree Anna' i.e. millets - are rooted in our own culture. In the North-East, too, there has long been a rich tradition of millet cultivation; however, over time, people had begun to drift away from it. Now, that situation is changing.

Friends,

In the West Jaintia Hills district of Meghalaya, there is a village called Khanduli. Over many generations, millets have been an integral part of the local food culture there. Yet, for some time, the number of farmers cultivating them had been on the decline. Amid that, two women friends from the village undertook a new initiative: they focused on creating new products from millets. Lending value addition to these grains, they developed items such as cookies, cakes, and muffins, as well as baby food. This led to an increase in the sales of millet-based products and a subsequent rise in the demand for millets themselves. Amid that, farmers there have also begun cultivating millets once again. Friends, in the village of Sadolpara, located in the West Garo Hills district of Meghalaya, some new initiatives are underway. A local farmer there, Chekjing Sangma, recognizing the importance of millets, has started cultivating them using modern methods. This has not only increased his income but has also fostered greater awareness within the village. Similarly, there is a village called Kezoma in Kohima, Nagaland, where the cultivation of millets had ceased for over a decade.

As a result, an entire generation grew up unfamiliar with this traditional crop - imagine… a crop once grown by their own grandparents, was being forgotten by the villagers themselves. In 2024, the local community resumed the cultivation of millets, and in 2025, Kezoma celebrated its first-ever millet festival. Now, there is a rapidly growing demand for products made from millets in this region as well.

Friends,

Examples related to millet cultivation carry a significant message. These examples demonstrate how our youth are linking traditional crops with new opportunities, and how our villages are advancing on the path to prosperity while preserving their heritage.

My dear countrymen,

Tomorrow, October 26th, marks the birth anniversary of Maharishi Valmiki. Though thousands of years have passed, the Ramayan, of Maharishi Valmiki ji, continues to offer us new insights even today.

Through the Ramayan, Maharishi Valmiki has imparted profound life lessons to us… on the one hand he emphasizes the value of persistent effort; on the other he also highlights the importance of service, compassion, and social harmony. In the Valmiki Ramayan, the character of Bhagwan Ram serves as a beautiful embodiment of these values – Bhagwan Ram embraced the love and devotion of Mata Shabari… honored his friendship with Nishadraj. The spirit of taking everyone along - these ideals continue to guide us even today. This sentiment is also reflected in the grand Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, where shrines dedicated to Maharishi Valmiki, Nishadraj and Mata Shabari as well have been built. I am pleased that the airport in Ayodhya has also been named after Maharishi Valmiki. These initiatives enrich our great tradition - the very tradition that places the highest value on service, social harmony, and compassion.

My dear countrymen,

The soil of India has given birth to many such great personalities who have left an indelible mark. One such great figure is Bhai Parmanand ji. In a few days, on November 4th, we will celebrate his 150th birth anniversary.

A major source of inspiration and ideals for Bhai Parmanand ji was his deep association with Arya Samaj. In the very early 20th century, he traveled to South Africa for the work of Arya Samaj, where he also met revered Bapu. He also worked among the 'Girmitiya' community in Guyana, which was a significant centre for Arya Samaj at that time. During my own visit to Guyana, I had the privilege of visiting the Arya Samaj memorial.

Friends,

Bhai Parmanand ji played a major role in the freedom movement. It is said that it was Bhai Parmanand ji who had persuaded Lala Har Dayal ji to go to America. He was also one of the founding members of the Ghadar Party. His influence on the struggle for independence was so profound that the British authorities sentenced him to 'Kala Pani'. He authored a book titled 'Aapbeeti: Kaale Paani Ki Kaaraavaas Kahaani'. This book is a must-read to truly understand the sacrifices made by freedom fighters. After completing his sentence, Bhai Parmanand ji turned his focus towards the field of education. You might be surprised to learn that he even taught Veer Bhagat Singh.

In later years, he remained associated with the Hindu Mahasabha for many years as well. In other words, from his connection to Gandhiji to his time in Guyana, and from the Ghadar movement to the Andamans, his personality stands as a great source of inspiration. I offer my respectful homage to Bhai Parmanand ji. I urge the youth to learn about them and inspire others as well.

My dear countrymen,

The coming days will be filled with the festive spirit of Diwali, the great festival of Chhath, and several other celebrations. Do celebrate these festivals with your entire family while staying healthy and safe and include others in your joy. I extend my best wishes to all of you for the upcoming festivals.

As always, I look forward to receiving your messages and suggestions. Your suggestions provide new topics and new direction to ‘Mann Ki Baat’. We shall meet again next month, with new endeavors and inspiring stories from our fellow countrymen.

Thank you very much.

Namaskar.

*****

MJPS/SS/VJ/VK

The Ministry and its associated organisations have achieved approximately 60-70% progress against identified targets, with…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of New & Renewable Energy Actively Implementing Special Campaign 6
Ministry Achieves nearly 70% progress against identified targets and efforts towards cleanliness
Posted On: 25 OCT 2026 11:42AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of New & Renewable Energy (MNRE), along with its Central Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs) and Autonomous Institutes, is actively implementing Special Campaign 6.

The Ministry and its associated organisations have achieved approximately 60-70% progress against identified targets, with sustained efforts towards cleanliness, efficient record management, optimum utilisation of office space and disposal of pending matters.

Key activities include cleanliness drives in offices, corridors and canteens; review and weeding out of physical records; removal of redundant materials; and identification and disposal of e-waste in accordance with applicable guidelines.

The Ministry, its two CPSUs — Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency Ltd. (IREDA) and Solar Energy Corporation of India Ltd. (SECI) and three Autonomous Institutes — National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE), National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE) and Sardar Swaran Singh National Institute of Bio-Energy (SSS-NIBE) — are participating actively in the Campaign.

Launched by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), the campaign aims to institutionalise Swachhata and minimise pendency in Government offices. The Implementation Phase commenced on 2nd October, 2026, and will continue until 31st October, 2026.

MNRE remains committed to achieving the identified targets by 31st October, 2026, and sustaining the culture of cleanliness, accountability and efficient workplace management beyond the Campaign period.

 

***

PIB Backgrounder
Ramsar Sites in India
Safeguarding Wetlands of International Importance
Posted On: 25 OCT 2026 9:43AM by PIB Delhi

India’s network of Wetlands of International Importance under the Ramsar Convention has expanded nearly fourfold since 2014. It has grown from 26 to 103 designated sites covering over 13.87 lakh hectares. Ranking first in Asia and third globally, these ecosystems safeguard biodiversity, buffer floods, recharge groundwater, and sustain livelihoods. Anchored by the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017, the Government of India drives scientific and participatory conservation through the National Plan for Conservation of Aquatic Ecosystems (NPCA), Amrit Dharohar, MISHTI, and Mission Sahbhagita to secure long-term ecological resilience.

 

Ramsar Sites in India — At a Glance

As per the Ramsar Convention, "Wetlands are the areas of marsh, fen, peatland or water, whether natural or artificial, permanent or temporary, with water that is static or flowing, fresh, brackish or salt, including areas of marine water the depth of which at low tide does not exceed six metres”. Linking land and water, wetlands store fresh water, recharge groundwater, buffer floods and sustain fisheries and farming. They also shelter migratory birds and rich biodiversity, placing them among the most productive ecosystems on Earth.

Globally, these habitats are protected under the Convention on Wetlands or the Ramsar Convention, an intergovernmental treaty. It was adopted at Ramsar, Iran, on 2 February 1971 and entered into force in 1975. As on October 2026, it now includes 172 Contracting Parties and over 2,536 designated "Ramsar Sites" worldwide.

India, home to a large number of wetlands, became a Party to the Convention on 1 February 1982. It has steadily expanded its network since then. The country now has 103 Ramsar Sites, a nearly fourfold rise from just 26 sites in 2014. India’s network ranks first in Asia and third in the world in terms of number of sites. Collectively, these sites cover more than 13.87 lakh hectares across 28 States and Union Territories.

 

Understanding Ramsar Sites

A Ramsar Site is a wetland designated as a Wetland of International Importance under the Ramsar Convention. These sites are recognised for their ecological, botanical, zoological, limnological or hydrological significance. The Ramsar Convention rests on three pillars. These are the wise use of all wetlands, the designation and effective management of Ramsar Sites, and international cooperation on wetland conservation.

How a Wetland is Designated

In India, the process begins with the State Government or Union Territory Administration identifying a suitable wetland. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change then coordinates approval and forwards the proposal to the Ramsar Secretariat.

Criteria for Designation

A wetland must meet at least one of nine criteria to qualify as a Wetland of International Importance. The criteria fall into two groups, covering wetland types and the conservation of biological diversity.

Group

Criteria

A wetland should be considered internationally important

Group A: Wetland types

 

Criterion 1

If it contains a representative, rare, or unique example of a natural or near-natural wetland type found within the appropriate biogeographic region.

Group B: Biological diversity

Criteria based on species and ecological communities

Criterion 2

If it supports vulnerable, endangered, or critically endangered species or threatened ecological communities.

Criterion3

If it supports populations of plant and/or animal species important for maintaining the biological diversity of a particular biogeographic region.

Criterion4

If it supports plant and/or animal species at a critical stage in their life cycles, or provides refuge during adverse conditions.

Specific criteria based on waterbirds

Criterion5

If it regularly supports 20,000 or more waterbirds.

Criterion6

If it regularly supports 1% of the individuals in a population of one species or subspecies of waterbird.

Specific criteria based on fish

Criterion7

If it supports a significant proportion of indigenous fish subspecies, species or families, life-history stages, species interactions and/or populations that are representative of wetland benefits and/ or values and thereby contributes to global biological diversity.

Criterion8

If it is an important source of food for fishes, spawning ground, nursery and/or migration path on which fish stocks, either within the wetland or elsewhere, depend.

Specific criteria based on other taxa

Criterion9

If it regularly supports 1% of the individuals in a population of one species or subspecies of wetland-dependent non-avian animal species.

 

Did You Know? A taxon is a group of organisms classified together based on shared characteristics, while taxa is the plural form, referring to multiple groups. For example, flowering plants, such as roses, form a plant taxon, while butterflies belong to an insect taxon. Major taxa in biodiversity include amphibians, reptiles and mammals.

 

Benefits of Designating Wetlands to Ramsar List

Designating wetlands to the Ramsar list and meeting Ramsar Convention commitments is a contribution to global efforts for biodiversity conservation. Ramsar Sites are recognized as being of significant value not only for a country but for humanity as a whole. Designating Ramsar Sites and ensuring their conservation and wise use:

  • Provides a platform for international representation: Enables countries to voice their concerns at the principal intergovernmental forum on wetland conservation and wise use. At the Ramsar 15th Conference of Parties held at Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe, India introduced a Resolution on ‘Promoting Sustainable Lifestyles for the Wise Use of Wetlands’. The resolution was adopted at the Conference. The resolution received overwhelming support from the 172 Ramsar Contracting Parties, Six International Organisation Partners, and other observers.
  • Enhances visibility and recognition: Increases the international visibility and recognition of Ramsar Sites. This can strengthen support for their conservation and wise use.
  • Provides access to international standards and guidance: Offers access to the latest information on internationally accepted standards for identifying wetlands of international importance. It also provides guidance on wise use and wetland management planning.
  • Facilitates expert assistance: Enables access to expert advice on national and site-specific wetland conservation and management challenges. Support is available through the Ramsar Secretariat, its collaborators, and Ramsar Advisory Missions, where appropriate.
  • Promotes international cooperation and financial support: Encourages cooperation on wetland conservation and management. It can also facilitate project support through the Convention’s small-grant programmes and links with multilateral and bilateral funding agencies.

Commitments After Designation

Designation commits the State or Union Territory to the wise use of the wetland and its resources. The site is deemed notified under the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017, and also the guidelines recommend to be formally notified under these rules with an Integrated Management Plan. The Ramsar Information Sheet must be updated every six years, and the site’s ecological character monitored regularly. Guided by these criteria and commitments, India has built a large and remarkably diverse network of Ramsar Sites.


India’s Ramsar Sites — From 26 to 103

India’s Ramsar Sites span high-altitude lakes, river floodplains, mangroves, coral reefs, village tanks and urban marshes. Tamil Nadu has the highest number with 20 sites, followed by Uttar Pradesh with 14 sites. Growth has been rapid, and in 2025 alone, 11 wetlands were added, taking the national total to 96. Surha Tal in Uttar Pradesh became the 100th site in June 2026, and Glaw Lake the 101st in August. India’s Ramsar site tally has reached 103 on October 15, 2026, with the designation of Sukhna Wetland in Chandigarh and Sauj Jheel in Uttar Pradesh as the latest additions to the list.

 

Did You Know?

The First Ramsar Sites

Chilika Lake in Odisha and Keoladeo National Park in Rajasthan became India’s first Ramsar Sites on 1 October 1981. After successful ecological restoration, Chilika was removed from the Montreux Record in 2002. Chilika Development Authority later won the Ramsar Wetland Conservation Award.

What is Montreux Record: It is a register of Ramsar Sites where changes in ecological character have occurred, are occurring or are likely to occur. It identifies wetlands requiring priority conservation attention and guides monitoring, remedial action and resource allocation. Sites are included in consultation with the concerned country and relevant scientific experts. Sites may be removed from the record once successful remedial measures are documented or when the threat of ecological change no longer exists.

 

India’s latest additions to Ramsar Sites

 

Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) is a human-made reservoir created in 1958 at the foothills of the Shivalik hills. It shelters threatened species such as Pallas's fish eagle, the common pochard and the black pond turtle. Migratory birds on the Central Asian Flyway rely on it for feeding and wintering.

Sauj Jheel (UP) is a shallow floodplain lake in Mainpuri district that regularly hosts more than 30,000 waterbirds. It provides nesting and foraging grounds for threatened birds such as the sarus crane and the greater spotted eagle. Its sacred lotus and wild sugarcane beds offer cover for nesting birds, fish and amphibians.

Did You Know?

The Largest Ramsar Site

Sundarban Wetland in West Bengal, designated on 30 January 2019, is India’s largest Ramsar Site at 4,23,000 hectares. It holds over 60 per cent of India’s mangrove area and a tiger population with unique aquatic hunting skills.

 

How Ramsar Sites Aid in Conservation

Ramsar status brings global recognition, scientific guidance and access to expert advice for designated wetlands. It also places clear duties on States to protect each site’s ecological character through planning and monitoring.

  • Restoring Ecosystems: Chilika Lake shows how sustained restoration can revive a wetland and the communities that depend on it. Today, the lagoon supports 118 fish species and serves as a breeding, wintering and staging ground for waterbirds.
  • Sustaining Livelihoods: The East Kolkata Wetlands treat the city’s wastewater naturally through about 4,000 hectares of fish ponds. They yield about 10,500 tonnes of fish a year and directly support about 50,000 people.
  • Building Climate Resilience: The Sundarban mangroves shield inland areas from storms, cyclones, tidal surges and saltwater intrusion. They also serve as nurseries for fish and shellfish, sustaining fisheries along India’s entire eastern coast.
  • Reviving Threatened Species: The Beas Conservation Reserve in Punjab holds India's only known population of the endangered Indus River dolphin. A reintroduction programme launched in 2017 released 47 gharials, nearly three decades after they vanished from the river. The 185-kilometre river stretch also supports more than 500 bird species and over 90 fish species.
  • Community Stewardship: Khichan Wetland in Rajasthan hosts more than 22,000 wintering demoiselle cranes each year on just 54 hectares. Residents of the adjoining village actively protect the birds from power line collisions and stray dog attacks.

 

Government Initiatives for Wetland Conservation

India’s Ramsar network is backed by a strong framework of laws, schemes and people’s participation.

Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017

Notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, these Rules provide the regulatory framework for wetland conservation. They establish State/UT Wetlands Authorities and prohibit activities such as encroachment, waste dumping and untreated effluent discharge.

National Plan for Conservation of Aquatic Ecosystems (NPCA)

NPCA merged the national programmes for lake and wetland conservation into one scheme.  Updated NPCA Guidelines issued in 2024 give States an integrated and scientific framework for managing wetlands.

Amrit Dharohar

Amrit Dharohar promotes the unique conservation values of India’s Ramsar Sites. It covers species and habitat conservation, nature tourism, wetland livelihoods and wetland carbon assessment. Under this, studies for the inventory of flora and fauna of 75 Ramsar Sites have been conducted by the Botanical Survey of India and the Zoological Survey of India, respectively. A ‘Standard Operating Procedure for Assessment of Carbon Stock in Wetlands’ was released, and has been utilised to assess the Carbon stock of 39 Ramsar Sites across the country.

Mission Sahbhagita and the Save Wetlands Campaign

Mission Sahbhagita promotes participatory conservation; its Save Wetlands Campaign began in Goa on 4 February 2023. Over 2 million citizen volunteers have since helped map more than 1.7 lakh wetlands across the country.

Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes (MISHTI)

MISHTI targets mangrove restoration over 540 square kilometres in nine States and four UTs. So far, ₹88.44 crore has been released to restore 9,949.5 hectares of degraded mangroves.

Wetlands of India Portal

Inaugurated on 2 October 2021, the portal serves as a dynamic knowledge repository on India’s wetlands. It offers single-point access to information on sites, projects, initiatives and training for managers and citizens.

Wetland City Accreditation

Indore and Udaipur became India’s first Ramsar-accredited Wetland Cities in January 2025, joining the global network of Ramsar-accredited Wetland Cities.

 

Way Forward

India’s expanding Ramsar network offers an opportunity to strengthen wetland conservation through science, effective management and community participation. The focus ahead must be on translating international recognition into lasting ecological outcomes. Regular monitoring, evidence-based planning and coordination among governments, institutions and local communities can help maintain the ecological character of these wetlands. Sustained efforts will be essential to ensure that wetlands continue to support biodiversity, water security, climate resilience and livelihoods for future generations.

Equally important is the need to integrate wetland conservation into wider development planning. Strengthening local stewardship, improving data and knowledge sharing, and promoting sustainable livelihood opportunities can deepen conservation efforts. By combining ecological priorities with the needs of communities, India can build a more inclusive and resilient approach to wetland management, ensuring these ecosystems remain productive and protected over the long term.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister hails India’s historic best-ever performance and record 114 medals at the Asian Para Games 2026
Posted On: 25 OCT 2026 8:17AM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today lauded the extraordinary achievement of India's para-athletes at the just concluded Asian Para Games 2026.

The Prime Minister highlighted that with a record 114 medals, this marks India’s best-ever performance at the Games, noting that this is an occasion of immense pride and joy for the entire nation. He congratulated every member of the contingent for their exceptional determination, emphasizing that each athlete has contributed to this historic achievement and inspired countless Indians with their accomplishments.

The Prime Minister shared on X:

"What an extraordinary achievement by our para-athletes at the just concluded Asian Para Games 2026!

With a record 114 medals, this marks India’s best-ever performance at the Games. This is an occasion of immense pride and joy for the entire nation!

I congratulate every member of our contingent for their exceptional determination. 

Each athlete has contributed to this historic achievement and inspired countless Indians with their accomplishments."


What an extraordinary achievement by our para-athletes at the just concluded Asian Para Games 2026! With a record 114 medals, this marks India’s best-ever performance at the Games. This is an occasion of immense pride and joy for the entire nation! I congratulate every member of our contingent for their exceptional determination. Each athlete has contributed to this historic achievement and inspired countless Indians with their accomplishments.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Agricultural Biological Resources generate around ₹1.04 Crore in ABS Benefits for Biodiversity Initiatives across India
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 10:38PM by PIB Delhi

The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed around Rs. 1.04 crore of Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) amount among 27 State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs), two Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs). This demonstrates how benefits arising from the utilisation of agricultural biological resources can be channelled towards biodiversity conservation and sustainable use.

The amount represents benefit-sharing contributions received from Crystal Crop Protection Limited, Savannah Seeds Pvt. Ltd. and Nunhems India Pvt. Ltd. for access to agricultural biological resources for research and commercial purposes. The contributions relate to the utilisation of pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum), jowar (Sorghum bicolor), maize (Zea mays), rice (Oryza sativa L.) and bottle gourd (Lagenaria siceraria). These crops are important components of India’s agricultural biodiversity, supporting food security, farming livelihoods and agricultural innovation.

NBA has adopted an area-based approach to distribute the benefit-sharing component, where biological resources are procured through markets, traders or intermediaries and individual benefit claimers cannot be identified. Allocations are determined proportionately, taking into account the geographical distribution and cultivation area of the relevant crops, based on agricultural statistics published by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare through its Unified Portal for Agricultural Statistics.

The disbursal of around Rs. 1.04 crore covers allocations to SBBs and UTBCs. The state-wise distribution includes allocations for the top 10 States and the remaining States collectively, based on the applicable area-based methodology.

The agriculture sector, which has generated approximately Rs. 87 crore ($9.16 mn) in ABS contributions, is emerging as an important contributor to India’s ABS mechanism. These contributions can support the conservation and sustainable use of agricultural biological resources, including traditional crop varieties and genetic diversity, while strengthening biodiversity-related initiatives at the State and Union Territory levels.

Till date, the NBA has released over Rs. 204 crore ($21.48 mn) in ABS benefits, supporting biodiversity conservation and benefit sharing across the country. India’s ABS framework contributes to the objectives of the Convention on Biological Diversity and the Nagoya Protocol and supports Target 13 of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, which calls for effective measures to ensure the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilisation of genetic resources, digital sequence information and associated traditional knowledge.

India’s experience in implementing ABS will be highlighted at the CBD COP 17 side event ‘From Policy to Practice: Advancing India’s Biodiversity Commitments through Innovation, Finance, and ABS’, scheduled on 28th October 2026 in Yerevan, Armenia. The event will showcase India’s efforts to translate biodiversity commitments into action through policy implementation, innovation, financing and benefit sharing.

Funds allocated to SBBs and UTBCs are to be utilised in accordance with the applicable provisions of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, and for activities relating to biodiversity conservation and sustainable use, documentation, research, capacity building and strengthening local biodiversity governance, as applicable. India’s ABS framework is governed by the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, as amended in 2023, the Biological Diversity Rules, 2024, and the Access and Benefit-Sharing Regulations, 2025. Section 21 of the Act provides for the determination of fair and equitable benefit sharing arising from the utilisation of biological resources. The present release of money demonstrates the practical application of this framework in agricultural supply chains, linking research and commercial utilisation with support for biodiversity-related initiatives.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Digital India BHASHINI Division Showcases Multilingual AI Solutions for Accessible Research at ETD-2026, IIT Delhi
BHASHINI explores collaboration with higher education institutions and research repositories to expand access to theses, dissertations and scholarly content across Indian languages
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 8:45PM by PIB Delhi

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, participated in the 29th International Symposium on Electronic Theses and Dissertations (ETD-2026), held at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi from 23 to 25 October 2026. Ms. Baishali Chakraborty, speaking on behalf of DIBD, conducted a session on BHASHINI’s multilingual artificial intelligence capabilities and their potential to make scholarly knowledge more accessible across languages.

Titled “Workshop on AI BHASHINI: Bridging Divides and Increasing Productivity,” the session highlighted how BHASHINI’s Language-First Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) can support higher education institutions, libraries and research repositories in addressing language barriers and expanding access to academic content.

During the session, Ms. Chakraborty demonstrated how voice-first multilingual AI, speech-to-text, translation, optical character recognition (OCR) and document translation can support multilingual access in academic and research settings. A live demonstration of Shrutlekh showcased real-time speech transcription with simultaneous translation, illustrating its potential applications in lecture halls, research seminars, conferences and academic discussions.

The session also highlighted BHASHINI’s broader multilingual AI ecosystem, which brings together language datasets, AI models, APIs and applications to support a range of language technology use cases. BHASHINI has recorded over 10 billion cumulative AI inferences and supports 36 Indian languages for text, 23 Indian languages for voice and 35 international languages. Its website translation plugin enables multilingual access across more than 800 government websites.

A key focus of the session was the potential to extend AI-powered translation to electronic theses and dissertations (ETDs), including lengthy and specialised academic documents. BHASHINI Pragati, a document translation workbench developed for the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG), was presented as an example of structured document translation and review. The workbench supports the processing of large documents, including those spanning 100 to 500 pages, with quality checks and data security considerations.

The discussion explored how similar workflows could be adapted for research repositories such as Shodhganga, maintained by INFLIBNET, as well as universities and other higher education institutions. Such solutions could help make theses, dissertations, research reports and other scholarly material available across Indian languages while preserving document structure, specialised terminology and meaning.

Speaking on the occasion, Harshad Sharma, Senior Manager (Finance), Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), said, “Making research and scholarly knowledge accessible across Indian languages is an important step towards a more inclusive knowledge ecosystem. BHASHINI’s multilingual AI capabilities, including document translation and speech technologies, can help universities, libraries and research repositories reach wider audiences. Engagement with academic institutions will be key to understanding their requirements and developing reliable solutions for multilingual access to theses, dissertations and other research content.”

During the interaction, participants raised questions about translating PDF documents on the fly and the reliability of AI translation for specialised academic and scientific content. Ms. Chakraborty discussed the importance of combining domain-specific machine translation with human review and quality assurance. The discussion also explored opportunities to work with research organisations to understand their requirements and develop customised solutions suited to their repositories and academic domains.

The session further covered BHASHINI’s capabilities in OCR for extracting text from scanned documents and images, terminology management through SHABD UDYAN, and transliteration to help preserve technical terms, names and expressions across scripts. These capabilities can support workflows that improve the accessibility and discoverability of research content while accounting for the linguistic and formatting requirements of academic documents.

Beyond translation, the session highlighted BhashaDaan, BHASHINI’s citizen-contribution initiative, which helps build and enrich language resources through speech and text contributions, audio transcription, and text extraction from images and documents. Granthika was also presented as a tool for digitising and preserving books, manuscripts, literary works, folk tales and oral histories, contributing to the development of digital resources for India’s multilingual knowledge ecosystem.

BHASHINI invited higher education institutions, research repositories, libraries and academic organisations to explore collaboration in identifying priority use cases, developing domain-specific language resources and adapting translation workflows to their needs. Such engagement can help address repository-specific requirements, strengthen translation quality through human validation and expand multilingual access to India’s scholarly output.

BHASHINI’s participation at ETD-2026 reflects its broader objective of advancing language technology as a public digital resource. Engagement with academic institutions and research repositories offers an opportunity to extend multilingual AI capabilities to scholarly communication, helping research and knowledge reach audiences across linguistic boundaries.

About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, is advancing India’s Language-First Digital Public Infrastructure to enable multilingual access to digital services. BHASHINI brings together language datasets, AI models, APIs and applications to support government departments, developers, researchers and other stakeholders in building multilingual AI solutions. It powers more than 800 government websites, has enabled over 10 billion cumulative AI inferences and supports 36 Indian languages for text, 23 Indian languages for voice and 35 international languages, advancing language technology across India’s digital ecosystem.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026-Guwahati
On Day 4, Visitors Witness India’s Rich And Diverse Heritage Of Traditional Handicrafts And Handloom Products At Farm Gate, Khanapara, Guwahati
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 8:20PM by PIB Delhi

The 08 days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 is underway at Guwahati, the State Capital of Assam. The Mela is 2nd of the Shilp Samagam Mela Series being organized by the Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, during Financial Year 2026-27.

As part of bringing together artisans from across the country, including the North-Eastern States, the Mela showcases India’s rich and diverse heritage of traditional handicrafts and handloom products.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Mela will continue until October 28 Wednesday.

He said the Mela remains open to public at Farm Gate, Khanapara, Guwahati, from 11 A.M. onwards till 9 O’ Clock.

The Official said the visitors are exploring the diverse range of traditional products to purchase the creations and support the artisans.

He said the the visitors also witness and enjoy traditional musical and dance programmes presented by a galaxy of artists. 

The Official said a total of 75 artisans, including 31 women artisans, are participating in the Mela, displaying approximately 40 varieties of handloom and handicraft products.

He said the event is providing participating artisans with a platform to exhibit and sell their products directly to visitors, establish connections with prospective customers and explore opportunities to expand their market reach.

By facilitating direct interaction between artisans and consumers, the Mela seeks to strengthen market access, encourage entrepreneurship and improve livelihood opportunities for participating artisans, he added.

The Official said the Guwahati edition features a wide range of traditional crafts and handloom products representing different regions of India.

The participation of artisans from the North-Eastern States, alongside those from other parts of the country, will provide visitors with an opportunity to appreciate the diversity of India’s artistic traditions, indigenous craftsmanship and cultural heritage, he added.

He said the event aims to also encourage greater appreciation of the skills and creativity of artisans whose work contributes to preserving traditional knowledge and craft practices.

The Official further said a key focus of the Mela is the promotion of BHARAT-TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme), an initiative aimed at facilitating the marketing of products made by artisans belonging to the target groups through physical outlets and e-commerce platforms.

 

By promoting access to wider markets and digital channels, the initiative is aimed to strengthen market linkages, expand customer outreach and create additional opportunities for artisans to enhance their earnings.

It also supports the preservation and promotion of traditional arts and crafts by connecting artisans and their products with evolving consumer markets, he said.

The Shilp Samagam Mela (SSM-2026) is an important initiative of the Ministry to provide marketing support to artisans and beneficiaries associated with its three National Corporations: the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), and the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC).

The first edition of SSM 2026 concluded in Mysuru on October 19, with thousands of visitors thronging the nine days Mela at Dasara Exhibition Ground, Mysuru in Karnataka.

Guided by the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s principle of “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas”, the Mela is promotiong the economic empowerment of artisans belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Safai Mitras and Denotified Tribes (DNTs).

The Mela is providing a dedicated platform for these communities to showcase their skills, market their products and strengthen their economic self-reliance through sustainable livelihood opportunities.

In addition to promoting the sale of traditional products, the Mela is creating awareness among visitors and participating communities about the welfare, financial assistance and development schemes implemented by the Ministry and its three National Corporations.

The initiative is complementing financial and developmental support with market-oriented interventions, enabling artisans to translate their traditional skills and craftsmanship into viable livelihood opportunities, the official said.

It is pertinent to mention that through initiatives such as Shilp Samagam Mela, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to advance its efforts towards the socio-economic empowerment of communities having financial constraints, by promoting entrepreneurship, facilitating market access and supporting sustainable livelihoods.

The Mela is enhancing the visibility of participating artisans, expanding awareness of their products and encouraging greater public engagement with India’s rich handloom and handicraft traditions.

item.description: Ministry of Railways Satna-Devendranagar (53 km) and Rewa-Churhat (65 km) Rail Sections Dedicated to the Nation; Vindhya and Bundelkhand Regions Brought Closer, Sidhi District to Benefit Significantly Railway Minister and Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Inaugurate Satna-Devendranagar and Rewa-Churhat Rail Sections Devendranagar-Churhat New Passenger Train Service Flagged Off; Will Serve as a Lifeline for Local Students, Patients and Daily Commuters Mineral-Rich Vindhya Region Connected with Major Industrial and Transport Centres Across the Country, Boosting the Rural Economy of the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Railways
Satna-Devendranagar (53 km) and Rewa-Churhat (65 km) Rail Sections Dedicated to the Nation; Vindhya and Bundelkhand Regions Brought Closer, Sidhi District to Benefit Significantly
Railway Minister and Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Inaugurate Satna-Devendranagar and Rewa-Churhat Rail Sections
Devendranagar-Churhat New Passenger Train Service Flagged Off; Will Serve as a Lifeline for Local Students, Patients and Daily Commuters
Mineral-Rich Vindhya Region Connected with Major Industrial and Transport Centres Across the Country, Boosting the Rural Economy of the Region
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 8:11PM by PIB Delhi

A historic milestone was achieved today in the expansion of rail connectivity in the Vindhya region of Madhya Pradesh. In the presence of Hon’ble Union Minister for Railways Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw and Hon’ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Dr. Mohan Yadav, Satna-Devendranagar and Rewa-Churhat rail sections were inaugurated. On this occasion, the new Devendranagar-Churhat passenger train service was also flagged off. Railway Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw joined from New Delhi in the programme through video conferencing.

The programme held at Churhat Railway Station was attended by Deputy Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Shri Rajendra Shukla, Member of Parliament from Rewa Shri Janardan Mishra, Member of Parliament from Sidhi Shri Rajesh Mishra, along with other public representatives and dignitaries. The programme held at Nagod Railway Station was attended by Minister of State in the Government of Madhya Pradesh Smt. Pratima Bagri, Member of Parliament from Satna Shri Ganesh Singh, Member of Parliament from Khajuraho Shri Vishnu Datt Sharma, along with other public representatives and dignitaries.

मध्य प्रदेश में, करीब-करीब एक लाख करोड़ के प्रोजेक्ट चल रहे हैं : माननीय रेल मंत्री श्री @AshwiniVaishnaw #RailInfra4MadhyaPradesh https://t.co/o7Ermadf6P

— Ministry of Railways (@RailMinIndia) October 24, 2026

Railway Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw said that improved rail connectivity is establishing a new lifeline for the Vindhya and Bundelkhand regions. He said that the project would fulfil a long-standing demand and improve access to education, employment and healthcare services for the people of the region.

Shri Vaishnaw referred to the expansion of railway connectivity across the country and highlighted the work undertaken in Srinagar, Mizoram and at the Pamban Bridge. He also mentioned the recent achievement of connecting Raoghat in Chhattisgarh and Tanda Road in Madhya Pradesh to the railway network.

The commencement of rail operations on the Devendranagar-Satna and Rewa-Churhat rail sections under the Lalitpur-Singrauli Railway Project will further strengthen connectivity in the Vindhya and Bundelkhand regions. He said that improved rail connectivity would accelerate industrial development in Madhya Pradesh and expand economic activities.

The Railway Minister stated that railway projects worth approximately ₹1 lakh crore are underway in Madhya Pradesh. These include new railway lines, doubling, construction of third and fourth railway lines, and gauge conversion projects. Work is being undertaken on railway sections such as Lalitpur-Singrauli, Satna-Rewa, Katni-Singrauli, Jabalpur-Gondia, Bina-Bhopal-Itarsi, Itarsi-Nagpur, Ratlam-Khandwa, Indore-Budni, Indore-Dahod and Indore-Manmad.

He said that the completion of these projects would pave the way for the introduction of new train services in the state. In the coming years, more than 100 long-distance trains and 50 to 60 short-distance train services, such as MEMU and Intercity trains, could be introduced.

Regarding station redevelopment, Shri Vaishnaw stated that Khajuraho station is being developed with architecture reflecting the culture and heritage of Madhya Pradesh. In addition, redevelopment work is being undertaken at several stations, including Ashoknagar, Balaghat, Beohari, Nainpur, Narmadapuram, Chhatarpur, Orchha, Shivpuri, Harpalpur, Chhindwara and Seoni. He also mentioned that approximately 80 railway stations in the state have been included under the redevelopment programme.

Emphasising the environmental commitments associated with the railway project, the Railway Minister referred to the felling of trees in the Anna region. He stated that a plan had been made to plant more saplings than the number of trees felled. He directed the General Manager, Divisional Railway Manager and District Magistrate to visit the site and inspect the plantation, ensure the survival of the planted saplings and plant new saplings wherever required.

Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Dr. Mohan Yadav said during the programme that the new rail connectivity marked a fresh beginning for the Bundelkhand and Vindhya regions, bringing railway services to areas that had remained unconnected by rail. He described the occasion as a Diwali gift for the people of the region.

Dr. Yadav said that the 541-km-long Lalitpur-Singrauli Railway Project would strengthen connectivity between Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, benefiting the regions of Lalitpur, Chhatarpur, Panna, Satna, Rewa, Sidhi and Singrauli.

The Chief Minister said that improved rail connectivity would provide farmers access to larger markets, facilitate freight transportation for industries, create opportunities for young people and students, improve access to healthcare services and promote tourism. He said that connectivity would boost economic activities in the mineral-rich Bundelkhand region, particularly benefiting the diamond trade in Panna. He also appreciated the railway projects being undertaken in Madhya Pradesh, including the Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga-Khandwa railway line.

Rewa-Churhat Railway Line to Benefit Sidhi District

The approximately 65-km-long new railway line from Rewa to Churhat has been constructed at a cost of approximately ₹1,070 crore. The project was completed with the completion of the final approximately 22.5-km railway line section between Rampur Naikin and Churhat. With rail connectivity extending to Churhat, residents of Sidhi district have gained an opportunity to connect with the national railway network.

This railway line is not merely a new mode of transportation for the region but also a means of creating new development opportunities. It will facilitate access for students to educational institutions, patients to better medical facilities, and young people and working professionals to employment and business opportunities. Considering the availability of limestone and other minerals in the region, along with the potential for the cement industry, rail connectivity is also expected to encourage industrial activities and freight transportation.

Satna-Devendranagar Railway Line to Boost Industrial and Rural Economy

The approximately 53-km-long new railway line from Satna to Devendranagar has been constructed at a cost of approximately ₹873 crore. The project was completed with the completion of the final 8-km railway line section between Phulwari and Devendranagar.

Satna and its surrounding areas have a significant presence of limestone, cement and other mineral-based industries. Improved rail connectivity will help facilitate the transportation of cement, clinker and other goods. This will improve the logistics arrangements of industries, reduce dependence on road-based freight transportation and enhance the prospects for the expansion of industrial activities in the future.

Rail connectivity will also provide farmers and rural traders in the Devendranagar, Nagod and Panna regions with better options for accessing larger markets. Railway connectivity will help agricultural produce, local products and handicrafts reach wider markets. In addition, new employment opportunities are likely to emerge in warehousing, transportation, trade and other allied activities.

New Passenger Train Service to Facilitate Students, Patients and Daily Commuters

With the commencement of the new Devendranagar-Churhat-Devendranagar passenger train service, passengers in the concerned areas will have improved rail connectivity through Satna and Rewa. This will provide a convenient travel option for students, working professionals, traders, patients, farmers and other daily commuters.

The new rail connectivity will also enhance the prospects of transporting local agricultural produce, stone crafts, handicrafts and other products to larger markets. This may provide a boost to local trade, transportation, food services and other small businesses.

Tourism to Receive a Boost, Local Employment Opportunities to Increase

The Vindhya and Bundelkhand regions are known for their natural beauty, historical heritage and numerous sites of cultural significance. Improved rail connectivity will help facilitate access to tourist destinations in Panna, Khajuraho, Rewa and the surrounding areas.

Major tourist attractions in the region include the White Tiger Safari, Mukundpur, Chachai and Bahuti waterfalls, Rewa Fort and Govindgarh. Improved rail connectivity is expected to make travel to these destinations more convenient and promote regional tourism. An increase in tourist movement may also benefit hotels, local transport services, guides, handicrafts and small businesses.

*****

Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Vanshita Jaiswal

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
NICDC Advances Industrial Development in Bihar with Launch of Bihar Integrated Manufacturing City Gaya Limited
12 MoUs signed for approximately 300 acres with proposed investments of ₹4,200 crore at IMC Gaya
Curtain raiser of Bihar Business Connect 2027 attended by approximately 250 delegates, including Ambassadors and senior representatives of the Embassies of Japan, Thailand and Laos
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 8:07PM by PIB Delhi

The National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC) marked a significant milestone in advancing industrial development in Bihar with the formal launch of Bihar Integrated Manufacturing City Gaya Limited (BIMCGL) by the Chief Minister of Bihar, Shri Samrat Choudhary, at Bodh Gaya today. The event also marked the inauguration of the curtain raiser of Bihar Business Connect 2027, highlighting the State's industrial potential and investment opportunities.

A key highlight of the event was the signing of 12 Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with prospective investors for approximately 300 acres of industrial land at IMC Gaya. These MoUs represent proposed investments of around ₹4,200 crore and an estimated employment potential of 16,095 opportunities. The proposed investments span sectors including food processing, automobile components, medicinal products, pharmaceuticals and other manufacturing activities.

Earlier, the Government of Bihar had also executed MoUs with prospective investors across multiple sectors at IMC Gaya, covering approximately 2,586 acres of land, with a total proposed investment of ₹31,750 crore and an estimated employment potential of 52,050 opportunities.

The programme was attended by approximately 250 delegates, including the Ambassadors and senior representatives of the Embassies of Japan, Thailand and Laos, senior government officials, representatives of the National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC), industry associations and prospective investors. Representatives of Bihar Foundation Chapters from 55 countries also participated virtually.

During the programme, the Chief Minister unveiled the BIMCGL logo and launched its official website and Integrated Land Allotment Portal, aimed at strengthening investor facilitation, improving transparency and streamlining industrial land allotment.

Addressing the gathering, Chief Minister Shri Samrat Choudhary reiterated the State Government's commitment to accelerating industrial development, attracting investments and generating employment through improved infrastructure and investor-friendly initiatives.  Deputy Chief Minister Shri Vijay Kumar Choudhary made special mention of NICDC's role in the planning and development of IMC Gaya.

Union Minister for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi, highlighted the Government's determination to strengthen industrialisation in Bihar with continued support from the Central Government, particularly for promoting manufacturing, MSMEs and employment generation.

The programme was also attended by Deputy Chief Minister Shri Bijendra Prasad Yadav, Speaker of Bihar Vidhan Sabha Shri Prem Kumar and Minister of Industries Ms. Shreyasi Singh, along with other senior dignitaries. The State Government reaffirmed its commitment to supporting industrial development and facilitating investments.

BIMCGL is the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) responsible for implementing the Integrated Manufacturing Cluster (IMC) at Gaya, being developed under the Amritsar–Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC) as part of the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP). Spread across 1,670 acres in Dobhi block of Gaya district, the project was approved by the Government of India on 28 August 2024 at a total cost of ₹1,339 crore, including land cost. It is expected to attract investments of approximately ₹16,500 crore and generate employment opportunities for around 1.10 lakh people.

Incorporated on 6 January 2025, BIMCGL is a joint venture between the Bihar Industrial Area Development Authority (BIADA) and the National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation Trust (NICDIT), with equal equity participation. As the dedicated implementing agency, BIMCGL will expedite project execution through coordinated planning, infrastructure development, statutory clearances, utility connectivity and investor facilitation. The institutional framework will enable faster decision-making, effective monitoring and timely resolution of implementation-related issues.

Infrastructure development at IMC Gaya is progressing, with the State Government having taken possession of the entire project land. The Government of India released the first tranche of equity amounting to ₹132 crore in September 2025 against the transfer of 415 acres. Project Management & Construction Supervision Consultant and EPC contractor for trunk infrastructure works had already been onboarded. The physical construction has already commenced.

Construction of an exclusive helipad at IMC Gaya is also at an advanced stage. It will enhance accessibility for investors, business delegations and senior officials, facilitating project monitoring and investment promotion activities.

The industrial cluster is being developed with integrated infrastructure, including internal roads, water supply, sewerage and wastewater treatment facilities, power distribution, solid waste management and fire safety systems. Its strategic location near NH-22 and NH-19, with Gaya Airport approximately 39 kilometres away, provides connectivity to major industrial and commercial centres. NICDC's role in planning the above, including assessing industrial water requirements and ensuring year-round water availability through adequate water storage facilities to support sustainable industrial operations, was formally acknowledged during the launch.

IMC Gaya will focus on sectors including agro-based industries, textiles and readymade garments, furniture, handicrafts and handloom, and engineering and fabrication. The planned infrastructure will support large manufacturers and MSMEs, encourage local entrepreneurship and strengthen industrial value chains across the region.

The curtain raiser of Bihar Business Connect 2027 provided an opportunity to showcase Bihar's investment potential and engage with prospective investors, industry associations and international stakeholders. The launch of BIMCGL reinforces the partnership between the Government of India and the Government of Bihar in developing modern, investment-ready industrial infrastructure.

With a dedicated institutional framework, ongoing infrastructure development and sustained investor engagement, BIMCGL is poised to accelerate the development of IMC Gaya as a major manufacturing destination in eastern India, contributing to Bihar's industrial transformation and the national vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat 2047.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
19th Urban Mobility India Conference and Exhibition concludes in Bhubaneswar with participation of around 1,500 delegates and experts
Urban Mobility must be integrated with Urban Planning from the outset: Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal
Union Minister calls for Integration, Inclusiveness and Intelligence as the three pillars of future urban mobility
Over ₹59,000 crore worth of nine Metro projects approved since December 2025; 1,100 electric buses operational in 28 cities: Shri Manohar Lal
Union Minister presents Awards for Excellence and Best Practices in Urban Transport; 28 exhibitors showcase innovations and mobility solutions
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 7:39PM by PIB Delhi

The 19th Urban Mobility India (UMI) Conference and Exhibition 2026 concluded in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, today, with Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs and Power, Shri Manohar Lal, addressing the valedictory session and presenting awards for excellence and best practices in urban transport. The two-day Conference, held on 23–24 October 2026, was organised by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) through the Institute of Urban Transport (India), with the support of the Government of Odisha.

The valedictory session was attended by Dr. Krushna Chandra Mahapatra, Minister, Housing & Urban Development, Government of Odisha; Smt. Usha Padhee, Additional Chief Secretary, Housing & Urban Development Department, Government of Odisha; and other senior officials, policymakers, urban transport experts and delegates from India and abroad.

Addressing the valedictory session, Shri Manohar Lal emphasised that urban mobility must be integrated with urban planning from the very beginning. He said that better transport infrastructure is no longer merely an outcome of development but has become a foundation for economic growth and urban development. He highlighted the importance of planning cities around the mobility needs of citizens, ensuring easy access to workplaces, schools, hospitals and other essential services.

The Minister stated that India’s future urban mobility systems must be guided by the three principles of Integration, Inclusiveness and Intelligence (3-I). He explained that Integration means seamless connectivity between metro, bus, rail and other transport services, with strong first- and last-mile connectivity. Inclusiveness calls for safe, accessible and convenient transport for women, senior citizens, persons with disabilities and all sections of society. Intelligence involves the use of Artificial Intelligence and real-time data to improve traffic management, passenger safety and efficiency of public transport.

Highlighting progress in urban transport infrastructure, Shri Manohar Lal informed that since December 2025, the Government of India has approved nine Metro projects covering approximately 174 kilometres at a cost of over ₹59,000 crore. During the same period, an additional 102 kilometres of Metro network has become operational. He further stated that India’s operational Metro network has expanded to 1,185 kilometres across 26 cities.

The Minister also highlighted progress under the PM e-Bus Sewa Scheme. He informed that 1,100 electric buses have commenced operations in 28 cities, carrying an average of around 2.5 lakh passengers daily. Referring to the Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Policy 2026 approved for Delhi in April 2026, he said that the policy will promote planned development and affordable housing across approximately 207 square kilometres along Metro, RRTS and railway corridors.

Referring to the deliberations during the Conference, the Minister said that 14 sessions were organised over two days, with participation from around 1,500 delegates and experts from India and abroad. He noted that 28 exhibitors showcased innovations and solutions in urban transport. He highlighted that the discussions had placed particular emphasis on integrating mobility into city planning and using data from telecom networks, mobile applications and digital platforms for evidence-based planning of Metro, bus and other transport services.

Shri Manohar Lal expressed satisfaction that the Conference had also focused on walking, cycling, people-centric streets and the mobility needs of women, senior citizens and persons with disabilities. Congratulating the States, cities and organisations recognised for excellence in urban transport, he urged all stakeholders to translate the suggestions emerging from the Conference into concrete action plans that deliver tangible benefits to citizens.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Krushna Chandra Mahapatra, Minister, Housing & Urban Development, Government of Odisha, said that the true success of a conference lies not merely in the ideas discussed but in translating them into meaningful action on the ground. He stated that the 19th Urban Mobility India Conference had provided a valuable platform for policymakers, urban experts, industry partners and other stakeholders to exchange experiences, innovative ideas and best practices. He emphasised that the learnings from the Conference must be converted into practical solutions suited to the needs of cities, with a focus on making urban spaces safer, more accessible, inclusive and liveable.

Additional Chief Secretary, Housing and Urban Development, Govt. Of Odisha in her remarks said “Odisha is proud to have hosted the 19th Urban Mobility India Conference & Exhibition and the National Urban Conclave 2026. The discussions and deliberations over the past few days have been truly enriching and engaging, bringing together valuable ideas and perspectives on sustainable urban development and people-centric mobility. As hosts, we endeavoured to uphold the spirit of Atithi Devo Bhava, ensuring that every delegate felt welcomed and valued in Odisha. We hope the insights and collaborations emerging from this platform will translate into meaningful action towards building inclusive, accessible and sustainable cities for the future.”

Awards for Excellence and Best Practices in Urban Transport

During the valedictory session, Shri Manohar Lal, along with Dr. Krushna Chandra Mahapatra, presented awards recognising excellence and best practices in urban transport. The awards acknowledged innovative initiatives undertaken by cities, States and transport organisations to improve public transport, promote sustainable mobility and strengthen urban transport systems.

The following organisations were recognised across different categories:

  1. City with the Best Green Transport Initiative: Bhubaneswar – Comprehensive Region Urban Transport (CRUT).
  2. City with the Best Non-Motorized Transport System: Chennai – Greater Chennai Corporation.
  3. Excellence in Innovation & Smart Mobility Solutions: Delhi – Delhi Transport Corporation and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.
  4. City with the Best Public Transport System: Delhi – Delhi Transport Corporation.
  5. Metro Station with Best Multi-modal Integration: Kochi – Kochi Metro Rail Ltd.
  6. Metro Rail with the Best Passenger Services and Satisfaction: Chennai Metro Rail Ltd. and National Capital Region Transport Corporation (Delhi/Uttar Pradesh).
  7. Best Use of Big Data Analytics for Operations and Evidence-based Transport Planning: Delhi – Delhi Transport Corporation.
  8. Special Award for Optimizing Civil Structural Design: Uttar Pradesh – Noida Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.
