Technical Sessions and Deliberations

The second day of the Conference featured technical sessions, round table discussions and a plenary session covering various aspects of sustainable and integrated urban mobility.

The Technical Session on ‘Land Use and Transport Beyond City Limits – TOD, Urban Form and Peri-Urban Corridors’ focused on integrating land-use and transport planning beyond traditional city boundaries. Discussions covered Transit-Oriented Development, compact urban growth, mixed-use development along mass transit corridors and the need for seamless connectivity between suburban areas and major transport networks. The session also examined governance challenges, affordable housing linkages and financing mechanisms for developing transit-oriented peri-urban corridors.

The Round Table on ‘People-Centric Streets – Safe, Walkable, Cyclable’ discussed the importance of designing urban streets that prioritise pedestrians, cyclists and public safety. Deliberations covered continuous footpaths, protected cycling networks, safe crossings, traffic-calming measures and institutional mechanisms for developing accessible and people-friendly streets.

The Round Table on ‘Behaviour Change and Public Communication – Enhancing Modal Shift through Public Outreach’ examined strategies to encourage citizens to shift from private vehicles to sustainable modes of transport. Discussions focused on targeted communication campaigns, community participation, incentives, digital applications and behavioural change initiatives to increase the use of public transport.

The Round Table on ‘Intelligence Driven Safe and Secure Mobility’ focused on the application of Artificial Intelligence, real-time data, connected infrastructure and emerging digital technologies in improving urban transport safety and efficiency. The discussions explored the potential of intelligent traffic management systems, connected vehicles and technology-enabled solutions for safer and more reliable mobility.

The Plenary Session on ‘Rail-Led Integrated Urban Development’ discussed the role of Metro and other mass rapid transit systems in shaping sustainable and liveable cities. Deliberations highlighted the need for economically viable rail-based transport systems, seamless multimodal integration and stronger first- and last-mile connectivity. The session also examined how mass transit infrastructure can support integrated urban growth and future-ready mobility networks.           

Conference Highlights

The 19th Urban Mobility India Conference and Exhibition was held under the theme ‘Urban Accessibility and Liveability in Digital Age’. The Conference brought together policymakers, senior officials from Central and State Governments, international experts, transport professionals, researchers and industry representatives to deliberate on emerging challenges and opportunities in urban mobility.

An exhibition featuring 28 exhibitors from the Government of Odisha, Metro Rail Companies, public sector organisations and private sector entities showcased emerging technologies, innovations and best practices in urban transport.

The Conference also provided a platform for research scholars and PhD students through a Research Symposium, with 46 selected research papers comprising 20 oral presentations and 26 poster presentations.

The Conference concluded with a renewed emphasis on integrated planning, evidence-based decision-making, technological innovation and inclusive public transport systems to improve accessibility and quality of life in Indian cities.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
National Urban Conclave 2026 inaugurated in Bhubaneswar, Odisha
Three things must be looked at: systems that plan and govern our cities, the solutions we apply on the ground, and the way services are finally delivered to citizens :Shri Tokhan Sahu,MoS MoHUA
Odisha is moving towards a new era of planned urbanisation, modern infrastructure and sustainable mobility, guided by the vision of Samruddha Odisha and Viksit Bharat 2047 : Shri Mohan Charan Majhi
Day-one deliberations focused on seven thematic areas
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 7:17PM by PIB Delhi

The second edition of the National Urban Conclave was inaugurated by Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Union Minister of State, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. The Conclave, being held on 24-25 October 2026, is organised by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and  supported by State Government of Odisha. National Institute of Urban Affairs is  the knowledge partner with Housing and Urban Development Corporation Limited, National Buildings Construction Corporation Limited, as the principal sponsors.

Organised under the theme ‘Urban Rising - Rethinking Urban Systems, Solutions and Delivery’, it brings together over 1,200 participants at the venue  including urban development Ministers, Mayors,  and representatives from urban local bodies (ULB), urban development authorities, academia, industry, civil society, and the wider urban development ecosystem. The conclave focuses on reimagining systems, institutions, and implementation mechanisms that shape how cities function.

Inauguration of the Conclave

Lighting the ceremonial lamp during the inaugural session, Shri Tokhan Sahu, the Hon’ble Union Minister of State, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, emphasised India’s ongoing urban transformation, wherein urban population had grown from approximately 377 million in 2011 to around 500 million, and is expected to reach 600 million by 2036. By the centenary of India’s independence, nearly one in every two Indians would live in a city. He noted that national programmes, including PMAY, AMRUT, Swachh Bharat Mission, PM SVANidhi, DAY-NULM and the Smart Cities Mission, had laid a strong foundation for the next phase of urban development.

Gracing the occasion, Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Odisha shared the state’s ambition to become a key growth engine in India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047. “Odisha is moving towards a new era of planned urbanisation, modern infrastructure and sustainable mobility, guided by the vision of Samruddha Odisha and Viksit Bharat 2047. As we work towards building a $500 billion economy by 2036, our focus is on creating inclusive, technology-enabled and people-centric cities. The expansion of Ama Bus services, the introduction of electric buses and the development of the Bhubaneswar-Kataka-Puri-Paradip Economic Region reflect our commitment to cleaner mobility, better urban infrastructure and improved quality of life for our citizens. We are building cities that are not only engines of economic growth but also safer, more accessible and more liveable for everyone”, he said.

Speaking on the occasion Smt. Anu Garg, Chief Secretary of Odisha stated “Urban mobility is about much more than roads, buses and infrastructure; it is about people, their dignity and their everyday experiences. Urban development must begin with the basic needs of citizens—access to safe drinking water, efficient public transport, clean surroundings and well-planned public spaces. Odisha’s expansion of the Drink from Tap initiative to 11 cities, along with piped drinking water coverage across 114 urban areas, reflects our commitment to reliable and citizen-centric urban services. As our cities grow, we must ensure that infrastructure and public services keep pace with urbanisation, while recognising the frontline workers who play a vital role in keeping our cities moving. Through coordinated planning, institutional strengthening and effective implementation, we must translate urban reforms into tangible improvements in the everyday lives of our citizens.”

Shri Satendra Singh, Secretary, Department of Urban Development, highlighted the opportunity to rethink urban systems, co-create innovative solutions, and strengthen delivery mechanisms to make cities more liveable, inclusive, resilient, and future-ready. He highlighted the role of flagship initiatives, including Swachh Bharat Mission, AMRUT, Housing for All, metro rail, PM-eBus Sewa and PM SVANidhi, in improving service delivery, encouraging citizen participation and strengthening urban resilience. He also outlined recent initiatives and reforms, including the Urban Challenge Fund of ₹1 lakh crore, the ₹5,000 crore Credit Repayment Guarantee Scheme, the ₹10,000 crore Urbanisation Premium Grant recommended by the Sixteenth Finance Commission, and reforms under the SASCI Scheme.

Shri Anurag Jain, Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog, in his keynote address stated the importance of institutionalising dialogue and sustaining engagement with state governments to advance India’s urban development agenda. He noted that the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 emerged through extensive participation and consultation, highlighting cities' role in driving societal and economic development. With nearly 50 per cent of India’s population expected to be urban by 2047, contributing around 75 per cent of GDP, he stressed the need for well-planned and coordinated urbanisation, supported by three pillars: investment, institutional response and capacity building.

Smt Usha Padhee, Additional Chief Secretary, Government of Odisha, delivered the vote of thanks, expressing appreciation for the opportunity to host the National Urban Conclave and showcase Odisha’s initiatives and experiences in urban development. She noted that the Conclave gave urban practitioners and stakeholders an opportunity to gain insights and learn from the state’s efforts. She extended her gratitude to the Hon’ble Minister of State, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Odisha, senior officials, state commissioners, and all those who contributed to the organisation of the conclave.            

Launches and Releases

The inaugural programme launched several initiatives and publications

Urban Invest Window (UiWIN) Journal

HUDCO's Urban Invest Window (UiWIN), supports states and ULBs through project development, capacity building and the preparation of investment-ready projects. Strong project preparation and innovative financing are essential for converting urban aspirations into implementable projects that create tangible benefits for citizens.

Samarthya Platform for CPHEEO

Integrated portal for knowledge management and capacity building in solid waste / used water/water sector.

ANKUR Handbook

The ANKUR Handbook: 2025–26 Key Achievements and 2026–27 Reform Priorities, presents the progress and outcomes of Atal Network for Knowledge, Urbanisation and Reform (ANKUR). The handbook highlights work across urban planning, municipal finance, institutional capacity building and digital governance through SUJOG.

Odisha Town Planning Handbooks

Developed by the Directorate of Town Planning, Housing & Urban Development Department, Government of Odisha, in collaboration with NIUA, the handbooks aim to simplify urban planning procedures and regulations, and offer citizens guidance on building plan and layout plan approvals.

Framework on Government and Privately Owned Public Spaces for Odisha

The proposed Government-Owned Public Spaces (GOPS) and Privately-Owned Public Spaces (POPS) Policy seeks to expand access to inclusive, accessible and well-maintained public spaces. GOPS focuses on activating underutilised government and institutional land, while POPS integrates publicly accessible plazas, landscaped areas and community spaces into private developments through planning regulations and incentives.

E-Book: Mera Ghar Mera Abhimaan

A compendium celebrating the voices and experiences of beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Urban. (PMAY-U)

E-Launch of PMAY-U 2.0 Mobile Application

The application is an updated version of the existing mobile application.

Standard Operating Procedure for PMAY-U Awards 2027

The SOP will establish the parameters and framework against which States' performance will be assessed, further encouraging and strengthening implementation of urban housing interventions.

Advisory on C & D Waste Management

This advisory for ULBs outlines how to implement the Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules 2025, which supersede the 2016 rules with a circular economy approach built on Extended Producer Responsibility, mandatory waste management and utilisation plans, recycling targets, and an online compliance portal.

Outcome Report on ‘Adequate Housing for All’

The Outcome Report collates the deliberations and recommendations of the technical sessions held on World Habitat Day, 2026, which examined how the potential of rental housing can be unlocked, what regulatory interventions can help bridge the gap between housing demand and supply, and how local and indigenous technologies can help scale up resilient, affordable housing.

The ‘Guidance Document on Compliance of Bulk Waste Generators’ was also launched.

Technical Deliberations

The first day of the Conclave featured seven thematic deliberations.

The session on ‘Right to Walk’ addressed an everyday concern in our cities: how to make streets safer and more accessible through continuous footpaths, safe school zones, better pedestrian crossings and improved last-mile connectivity.

Under ‘Water, Waste and Resource Efficiency’, the emphasis was on moving beyond infrastructure creation to improving service efficiency, reducing water losses, promoting treated-water reuse and recovering value from waste.

The session on ‘Affordable Housing’ brought attention to the growing need for rental accommodation, simpler regulatory approvals, better access to land and finance, and wider adoption of affordable, climate-resilient construction technologies.

Through ‘Integrated Urban Development and Infrastructure Delivery’, the session examined how better coordination between agencies, integrated utility planning and GIS-based systems can reduce duplication and improve the planning and execution of urban infrastructure.

A key question under the session on ‘New Paradigms for Urban Service Delivery’ was how municipalities can deliver better services through clearer institutional responsibilities, stronger finances, procurement reforms, technical capacity and partnerships with the private sector.

The session on ‘Model Building Bye-Laws’ focussed on how the existing regulatory framework can be revised to simplify building approvals, strengthen safety and accessibility, and respond to climate resilience and emerging construction technologies.

Finally, ‘Model Municipal Law’ examined the legislative reforms needed to strengthen municipal autonomy, clarify the powers of elected representatives and executive authorities, and improve institutional capacity and accountability in urban governance.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
CAQM reviews Paddy Stubble Management measures in Amritsar and Tarn Taran
Directs Field Officers to ensure Timely Availability and Maximizing Facilities for Utilisation of Paddy Stubble
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 6:53PM by PIB Delhi

A high-level team led by Shri Rajesh Verma, Chairperson, Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), today held a review meeting with the Deputy Commissioners and other concerned officers of Amritsar and Tarn Taran districts of Punjab. The meeting reviewed the measures being undertaken for comprehensive management of paddy stubble. It also focused on further containing and eliminating incidents of paddy stubble burning.

        

The team reviewed the in-situ and ex-situ utilisation of paddy stubble management, facilities and infrastructure for stubble management in the two Districts. The action taken by two District in light of the increased number of fire incidents was also reviewed. The team expressed concern at the increased number of fire incidents, and the concerned officers were directed to ensure all the efforts to arrest the numbers henceforth.

The Commission emphasized on ensuring maximum utilisation of paddy stubble as a fuel in thermal power plants, brick kilns and industries where such fuel usage is feasible. The Commission further directed that sector-wise Nodal Officers must be given responsibility for ensuring actual utilisation of paddy stubble by the respective sectors/ industries and for regularly monitoring and reporting compliance.

Emphasising the importance of timely field-level intervention, the Commission directed the officers to undertake regular visits to villages and farmers and not merely inform them about the availability of stubble management facilities but also ensure that the required machinery and facilities reach the farmers in a timely manner. The District Administrations were asked to strengthen coordination between farmers, Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs), machinery providers and other stakeholders so that farmers are able to access residue management solutions without delay.

As Tarn Taran District continues to report amongst the highest number of paddy stubble burning incidents, the Deputy Commissioner was directed to accord topmost priority to the issue and intensify field-level measures for prevention and management of such incidents. The Commission also warned that any laxity or failure in taking effective measures would invite strict action and accountability.

During the visit, the high-level team also inspected facilities in Amritsar where paddy stubble is being utilised as a source of fuel. The team visited the industrial boiler at an industrial complex in Amritsar, where paddy stubble pellets are being used as fuel in the industrial boiler. The visit provided an opportunity to assess the practical utilisation of processed paddy residue and the potential for scaling up such productive end-use models.

The Commission reiterated that paddy stubble management needs to be approached as a comprehensive residue-management and resource-utilisation exercise from the farmer facilitation standpoint. It was stressed that concerted efforts by District Administrations must be made by all concerned stakeholders to ensure that available in-situ and ex-situ solutions are effectively deployed, residue is channelized for productive use and incidents of paddy stubble burning are brought to an end.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Indigenous AIP system for Indian Navy’s diesel-electric submarines achieves key milestone with inauguration of Setting to Work Phase-2 Activity
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 6:53PM by PIB Delhi

A significant milestone towards enhancing Indian Navy’s underwater capabilities has been achieved with the inauguration of ‘Setting to Work Phase (STW)-2’ activity of the Air Independent Propulsion (AIP) system Energy Module developed indigenously by Naval Materials Research Laboratory, DRDO. The AIP system boosts the underwater endurance of the diesel-electric submarines by reducing its dependence on atmospheric oxygen.

The inauguration ceremony took place at Larsen and Toubro’s, AM Naik Heavy Engineering Complex in Hazira, Gujarat on October 24, 2026. Defence Secretary and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D and Chairman DRDO Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh was the Chief Guest who graced the ceremony virtually. Chief of Materiel, Indian Navy Vice Admiral B Sivakumar and Director General (Naval Systems & Materials), DRDO Dr R Balamuralikrishnan attended the event at L&T Hazira, Gujarat.

Speaking on the occasion, the Chairman DRDO congratulated DRDO and the industry partners and appreciated the scientific perseverance & industrial cooperation in the indigenous AIP Program, which has culminated into productive reality on the shop floor. He also acknowledged the cooperation rendered by the Indian Navy to DRDO throughout the course of this programme, including testing and validating at every stage of the trials. He emphasised on working towards next phases of the program towards achieving Navy’s induction timelines for AIP system while maintaining the exacting safety culture that hydrogen and fuel cell systems require without compromise.

In the next phase, the AIP Energy Module will be energised for power production and tested rigorously as per Indian Navy’s protocols before handing over to Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited for integration on Kalvari-class Submarine in early 2027.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Union MoS Raksha Khadse Calls for Stronger Pathways for Women in Indian Sports at All-Women Coaches Course
At the AITA ACE 2032 initiative in New Delhi, she highlights grassroots participation, women’s coaching, talent development and professional opportunities in sports
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 5:54PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Khadse addressed the All-Women Coaches Course under the All India Tennis Association’s (AITA) ACE 2032 initiative at the Delhi Lawn Tennis Association (DLTA) Tennis Stadium in New Delhi on Saturday. She emphasised the need to expand opportunities for women across sports, from grassroots participation and coaching to high-performance competition and leadership.

The event was attended by Shri Rohit Rajpal, President, DLTA; Shri Kawaljeet Singh, Director of Coaching, AITA; Shri Ashutosh Singh, Davis Cup Coach; Shri Sunder Iyer, Honorary Secretary, AITA; Shri Dinesh Arora, Treasurer, AITA; and Coach Radhika Kanitkar, associated with the BKJC Cup. Coaches and sporting professionals also shared perspectives on strengthening coach education, grassroots tennis and athlete development.


 

Supported by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS) and the Sports Authority of India (SAI), the initiative aims to strengthen the links between coach education, talent identification and high-performance training.

Expanding Women’s Participation from Grassroots to High Performance

Union MoS Raksha Khadse stressed that India’s ambition to become a leading sporting nation depends on identifying talent early and ensuring that women and girls have access to qualified coaches, suitable infrastructure, regular competition and sustained support.

She highlighted that sporting talent exists across rural, tribal, semi-urban and urban communities. Expanding participation, she noted, is vital to widening India’s talent pool and strengthening its prospects at national and international competitions. She also underlined that opportunities for women must extend beyond playing fields to coaching, sports science, administration, event management and other professional roles.



 

The discussions highlighted the role of ASMITA women’s leagues under the Khelo India framework in expanding access to organised sports. Launched in 2021, the leagues have reached more than three lakh women, creating opportunities for participation and competition across regions and communities.

The need to connect grassroots initiatives with Khelo India Centres, accredited academies and Centres of Excellence was also emphasised to help promising athletes progress towards higher levels of performance.

Building a Stronger Women Coaching Workforce

A key focus of the course was increasing the number of qualified women coaches and expanding access to coaching education and certification across states. Greater representation of women in coaching can help encourage girls to participate in sports while strengthening the quality and reach of athlete development.



 

The AITA ACE 2032 initiative seeks to connect coach education with talent identification and elite player development. Participants highlighted the importance of practical training, mentorship and continued professional development in preparing coaches for the demands of competitive sport.

Discussions also covered high-performance training and specialised coaching capabilities. Sheerika Burman, associated with high-performance training, highlighted the importance of developing expertise in this area. The programme also discussed the prospect of conducting a course in Bengaluru beginning on 10 December, with 16 players to be selected for the CHP course.



 

Regional Perspectives on Coaching and Player Development

Participants shared insights from their respective regions on strengthening grassroots tennis and improving coaching practices.

Preeti Srinivasan from Tamil Nadu highlighted the importance of focused coaching attention and grassroots tennis development. Marnu Riba from Arunachal Pradesh emphasised holistic player development and the importance of ensuring that athletes enjoy the sport as they build their abilities. Harjot Kaur from Jammu and Kashmir stressed the need to make Level One fitness programmes more comprehensive, particularly for beginners.



 

The discussions underscored the importance of coaching and fitness programmes that meet the needs of players at different stages of development and across diverse regional settings.

Creating Safe and Sustainable Careers in Sports

The course also highlighted the growing range of professional opportunities in sports, including coaching, fitness training, sports science, event management and administration. Participants stressed the need to equip more women with the skills and qualifications required to enter these fields and progress into leadership roles.

Safe sporting environments, athlete welfare and professional accountability were identified as essential to sustaining women’s participation. Coaches, sporting associations and governing bodies have a shared responsibility to uphold standards of safety, conduct and athlete protection.



 

The All-Women Coaches Course under AITA ACE 2032 reflects the wider effort to strengthen women’s participation and leadership in Indian sports. By expanding coaching opportunities, supporting grassroots talent and improving pathways to high-performance sport, the initiative seeks to contribute to India’s sporting ambitions for 2036 and the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
MY Bharat - NSS Takes ‘Gram Seva evam Parampragat Khel Diwas’ to Villages Nationwide Under Week 6 of Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 4:54PM by PIB Delhi

The MY Bharat National Service Scheme (NSS), under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, organised ‘Gram Seva evam Parampragat Khel Diwas’ (Village Service and Traditional Sports Day) as part of the sixth week of the ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat 100 Week Sankalp Abhiyan’, taking the campaign beyond educational institutions and into rural communities.


Implemented by the Directorate of NSS along with 15 NSS Regional Directorates, the initiative was conducted across more than 160 institutions and their adopted villages, mobilising over 80,000 participants, including youth, Gram Panchayat members, village elders and local residents. The activities were organised under the second month's theme, ‘Fit Youth, Addiction-Free Youth (Shakti evam Seva)’, highlighting the role of physical fitness, community participation and social responsibility in promoting a substance-free society.

As part of the traditional sports activities, NSS units organised local tournaments featuring Kabaddi, Kho-Kho, Tug of War and Kushti. These activities engaged over 21,500 participants, encouraging healthy recreation, teamwork and positive engagement among rural youth.


The Gram Seva component brought NSS volunteers and Gram Panchayats together to undertake community service activities, including cleaning village lanes, sanitation around public wells and handpumps, and sapling plantation drives. More than 19,800 participants took part in these activities, reflecting the NSS motto, ‘Not Me, But You’, through collective action for rural development.

Additionally, community awareness programmes and youth-led dialogues on healthy living and the Nasha Mukt campaign engaged over 18,600 individuals. The initiative also recorded the participation of more than 29,500 young women across sporting and community service activities, demonstrating a strong emphasis on gender inclusivity.


To amplify the campaign's reach, youth participants generated over 4,000 social media posts using the hashtag #NashaMuktYuva, extending the visibility of grassroots activities to a wider audience.

Through the integration of traditional sports, community service and awareness activities, Week 6 of the campaign strengthened the connection between educational institutions and rural communities. The initiative reaffirmed the importance of collective participation in fostering healthy lifestyles, positive youth engagement and the vision of a Nasha Mukt Viksit Bharat.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals
Three-day event ‘India Chem-2026’ concludes in Mumbai today
14th Biennial International Expo and Conference paves the way to attract investments and promote sustainable growth in the Chemicals and Petrochemicals sector
Brainstorming sessions held during CEO Forum, India Japan, India-USA and India-EU Forum on challenges pertaining to Chemicals and Petrochemicals Sector
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 4:51PM by PIB Delhi

The three-day event ‘India Chem-2026’ which was inaugurated on 22nd October concluded in Mumbai today.

The 14th edition of India Chem 2026 held under the theme “Advantage Bharat : An Emerging Global Chemicals Hub” strengthened global partnerships, paved the way to attract investments and promote sustainable growth in the chemicals and petrochemicals sector.

During the event brainstorming sessions, business parleys and fruitful discussions were held during CEO Forum, India Japan, India-USA and India-EU Forum and roundtable talks on different challenges pertaining to Chemicals and Petrochemicals Sector.

Japan, with whom India shares a robust trade relationship, particularly in the chemical and petrochemical sector, was the partner country for the event.

While inaugurating the India Chem 2026 Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, the Union Minister for Chemicals & Fertilizers and Health and Family Welfare in the august presence of the Chief Ministers of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha and Union Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers and Health and Family Welfare Smt. Anupriya Patel urged industry leaders, investors, innovators and policymakers of Chemicals Sector to work hand in hand to achieve the goal of ViksitBharat@2047.

Shri Nadda said Chemical and Petrochemical industry is a sunrise sector and it has huge potential to grow and contribute towards economic development.

The Union Minister said for the country to achieve the ambition of Viksit Bharat by 2047, this sector has to play an indispensable role. The sector needs to grow from its current market size of about USD 220 billion to about USD 1 trillion by 2040 and further to around USD 1.6 trillion by 2047.

The CEOs Forum presided by Shri JP Nadda focused on strengthening industry, competitiveness and advancing India’s ambition to emerge as a globally competitive chemicals and petrochemical hub.

Industry leaders from across the globe discussed the opportunities and challenges of the Indian chemical industry.

During the brainstorming sessions under India-Japan, India-US and India-EU Chemicals and Petrochemicals Forum at India Chem 2026 , representatives and industry leaders explored opportunities for deeper collaboration in trade, investment and technology related to sector.

The event held under the theme “Advantage Bharat : An Emerging Global Chemicals Hub” witnessed several roundtables like Specialty Chemicals, Infrastructure for Chemicals and Petrochemicals, Agrochemicals, Environment Issues, Plant Machinery, Pumps and Valves which are contemporary challenges for the rapid growth of the sector.

India Chem 2026 in its 14th edition witnessed a new feature “India Chem Youth Innovation Challenge” which was aligned to connect Young Innovators to the India’s Chemicals and Petrochemicals sector. It consisted of young students working on problem statements of the chemical industry and their solutions being judged by a jury of the industry. The First Prize was clinched by Soumya Bhole and Sarthak Kale, students of ICT, Mumbai. Suman Batwe and Saloni Mhadesar of VNIT, Nagpur and Jash Prasad and Smit Bambhorliya of IIT, Gandhinagar clinched second and third prizes respectively.

This event, organized jointly by the Department of Chemicals & Petrochemicals and FICCI, provided a platform for brainstorming discussions amongst industry leaders and Government representatives on specific topics of relevance to the sector, facilitating dialogue on investment prospects, regulatory frameworks, and strategic challenges.

The world class exhibition consisted of pavilions from leading Indian and global companies in the sector, several Indian States including partner states Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Bihar.

The event witnessed international participation from number of countries including Japan, the USA, Canada, UK, countries across the European Union, Latin America, Republic of Korea and ASEAN nations, with a footfall over more than 5000 visitors across 3 days.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Earth Sciences
Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh inaugurates World's first- of -its-kind 'Air Pollution Analysis' facility for Delhi NCR
'Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory ' (AATAL) also equipped to identify Real-Time Sources of Air Pollution
New facility to go beyond AQI numbers to reveal what is polluting Delhi’s air, where it is coming from and its potential health implications: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Integrated with AIRWISE to strengthen real-time source apportionment, air-quality forecasting and scientific decision-making, says Dr. Jitendra Singh
Facility to support CAQM and pollution-control agencies in targeting interventions and assessing their effectiveness: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Dr. Jitendra Singh says coordinated action across government departments is essential for evidence-based air pollution management
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 3:34PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today inaugurated the world's first- of -its-kind 'Air Pollution Analysis' facility for Delhi NCR. Known as 'Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory ' (AATAL), it is also equipped to identify real-time sources of air pollution.

Describing it as a first-of-its-kind integrated facility in the world, the Minister said Delhi-NCR had been chosen in view of the serious public concern over air pollution. He said the facility would take air-quality assessment beyond simply reporting pollution levels to identifying the composition of pollutants, their sources, their relative contributions and their potential health implications, while providing real-time information and advance forecasts to support timely action.

The inauguration took place at IITM’s Delhi Branch in the presence of Dr. T. Srinivasa Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, Dr. A. Suryachandra Rao, Director, IITM and DG IMD Dr Mahapatra. The facility has been established under 'Mission Mausam' announced by PM Sh Narendra Modi to strengthen scientific understanding of atmospheric pollution and provide actionable evidence for air-quality management in Delhi-NCR. The laboratory brings together advanced atmospheric measurement instruments, detailed chemical analysis, pollution-source identification and decision-support capabilities within an integrated framework.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Jitendra Singh said India had made substantial progress over the past 10–12 years in air-quality forecasting and analysis. He said the new facility represented a significant step forward because it would help establish not only how much pollution is present in the atmosphere, but also what it consists of and where it originates.

“Earlier, the discussion would largely revolve around whether the pollution level was 100 or 200. This facility will help us understand the composition of pollution as well as the contribution of different sources. This is important for addressing the concerns of the people of Delhi and ensuring that action is based on scientific evidence,” the Minister said.

AATAL will help scientists distinguish between different sources of air pollution, including vehicular emissions, industrial activity, biomass and crop-residue burning, construction and road dust, and pollutants transported from surrounding regions. By estimating the relative contribution of these sources, the facility will help authorities understand which activities are driving poor air quality at a particular time and where interventions may be most effective.

Explaining the significance of real-time source apportionment, Dr. Jitendra Singh cited an instance, while talking to the reporters, the screen showed that at that precise moment, transport was contributing approximately 25 per cent of Delhi air pollution, with the overall pollution level recorded at around 180. He said such information could help move the response to air pollution from general assessments to more targeted interventions based on the actual sources contributing to the problem.

The laboratory is equipped with advanced instruments for analysing the chemical composition of atmospheric gases and aerosols, including fine particulate matter (PM2.5), metals, toxic elements and other components. Its capabilities will help scientists investigate how pollutants interact and transform in the atmosphere and how different components contribute to the overall pollution burden.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the facility would provide information on the smaller constituents of air pollution, including metallic elements and other potentially harmful components. He explained that pollutants can differ in their health implications, making it important to understand not only their concentration but also their composition and potential toxicity.

The resulting scientific evidence can help health authorities better understand the potential risks associated with different types of particulate pollution. It can also support closer coordination between scientific institutions, health agencies and environmental authorities in assessing the implications of air pollution for public health.

The laboratory is integrated with IITM’s AIRWISE, Air Quality Warning and Integrated Decision Support System for Emissions, which combines air-quality forecasts, observations and source-apportionment information to support pollution management.

The project team explained that AIRWISE provides air-quality forecasts at a spatial resolution of 400 metres for the next 72 hours, enabling the system to assess how pollution may vary across different pockets of Delhi. It can also help identify the sources expected to contribute to deteriorating air quality in specific locations. Dr. Jitendra Singh said the integrated capability would provide real-time information as well as forecasts for the next four days, helping authorities prepare for changing pollution conditions.

Dr. Sachin Ghude, Project Director, MAQWS, said the integrated facility would strengthen air-quality management in Delhi-NCR by providing early warnings and detailed information on the sources contributing to pollution, including stubble burning, vehicular emissions, construction and road dust. He said the information would help the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) and other implementing agencies identify the major sources of pollution, plan targeted interventions and assess their effectiveness.

He added that the associated air-quality forecasting system provides forecasts at a 400-metre resolution for the next 72 hours, enabling pollution levels and their likely sources to be assessed for individual pockets of Delhi. Describing the forecasting capability as a major technological advance, Dr. Ghude said India had developed a high-resolution system comparable with global forecasting systems, with the potential to extend similar capabilities to other cities.

Emphasising the importance of coordination among government agencies, Dr. Jitendra Singh said air pollution could not be addressed by a single department working in isolation. He described the initiative as an example of the whole-of-government approach advocated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, bringing together scientific institutions, environmental authorities, pollution-control agencies and disaster-management stakeholders.

The Minister said coordinated engagement among the Ministry of Earth Sciences, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, pollution-control authorities and disaster-management agencies would be important for translating scientific information into effective action.

For the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) and other implementing agencies, the facility will provide measurement-based evidence to identify the sources responsible for deteriorating air quality, prioritise sectors and locations for intervention, and support coordinated measures across Delhi-NCR. When combined with AIRWISE forecasts, this information can strengthen decisions relating to preventive measures and responses under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP).

The inauguration of AATAL marks an important step towards connecting advanced atmospheric science with public policy and on-ground action. By bringing real-time measurements, chemical characterisation, source apportionment and forecasting together, the facility will help authorities move towards a more precise understanding of air pollution and a more coordinated response to the challenge facing Delhi-NCR.

 

*****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
Two-Day State-Level ‘Shram Samvad’ Programme on Labour Codes, Labour Welfare and Social Protection to begin in Lucknow on 26th October
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 1:59PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Uttar Pradesh, will hold a Two-Day State-Level Capacity-Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes, Labour Welfare and Social Protection on 26th and 27th October 2026 at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. This event is being organised as part of the nationwide “Shram Samvad” initiative focusing on district-level capacity building and awareness on labour reforms.

The Shram Samvad campaign, launched nationwide on September 28, 2026, is a 90-day outreach initiative through which the Ministry is undertaking district-level engagement across 316 districts in all 36 States and Union Territories, with a special focus on industrial clusters. The initiative seeks to provide employers and other stakeholders with greater clarity on the provisions, applicability, and compliance requirements under the new Labour Codes, thereby facilitating effective ground-level implementation.

Day 1 of the Programme will see deliberations centred around 'Labour Reforms', with the keynote address being delivered by the Secretary (Labour & Employment). Key sessions in the first half of the day will throw light on international labour mobility, social protection measures for Unorganised and Gig/Platform Workers, and initiatives for Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW).

The Minister for Labour and Employment, Government of Uttar Pradesh, will address one of the key sessions in the second half of the day, with following sessions bringing in insights from the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) and Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). Discussions will also underline the significance of leveraging technology for workers’ welfare through platforms like e-Shram, Shram Suvidha Portal, SAMADHAN and Labour Stack, along with best practices and rollout strategies by the state government.

Day 2 will focus on 'Implementation of Labour Codes & Way Forward', beginning with technical sessions chaired by senior officials from the Ministry. Deliberations in the first half of the day will feature an overview and detailed breakdown of statutory compliances under all four Labour Codes, i.e., Code on Wages (2019), Industrial Relations Code (2020), Code on Social Security (2020), and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code (2020). This will be followed by dedicated presentations on flagship schemes, including the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan Yojana. Day 2 will also focus on strategies for child labour prevention, rescue, rehabilitation, district-level monitoring, and child & bonded labour eradication. The sessions across both days will see the participation of officials from the Government of Uttar Pradesh.

A central feature across both days will be the structured Open Discussion sessions, providing an interactive platform to address key operational concerns, regulatory compliances, and practical queries raised by participants and industry stakeholders.

Rini Choudhury / Aishwarya Asthana

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
11 Crore Farmer IDs Created Five Months Ahead of Schedule, Marking Major Milestone in Digital Agriculture: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan says unique digital identities will ensure transparent and faster access to government schemes, bank loans, crop insurance and disaster relief
Digital Agriculture Mission advances PM Modi’s vision of a prosperous farming sector and a developed India
Verified farmer database to improve transparency, curb duplication and ensure benefits reach eligible farmers directly
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 1:56PM by PIB Delhi

In a major milestone for digital agriculture, the Government of India has achieved its target of creating 11 crore Farmer IDs, five months ahead of the March 31, 2027 deadline. Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, described the achievement as a significant step towards realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of a developed India with prosperous farmers. The milestone has been achieved under the Digital Agriculture Mission implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare. The Farmer ID initiative is designed to provide farmers with a unique digital identity, enabling transparent, efficient and timely access to government schemes, bank credit, crop insurance and disaster relief, while reducing paperwork and repeated verification.

Target achieved five months ahead of schedule

Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said the creation of 11 crore Farmer IDs was successfully completed by the night of October 23. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had set March 31, 2027, as the deadline for achieving this target. The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, state governments and field-level officials worked in coordination to achieve it five months ahead of schedule. He congratulated farmers across the country on the achievement, describing the Farmer ID as their own digital identity and an important step towards making agriculture more efficient, transparent and prosperous through modern technology.

Reduced paperwork and more transparent delivery of benefits

Shri Chouhan said the Farmer ID system would significantly reduce the need for farmers to repeatedly visit government offices and banks or submit the same documents for different schemes. Earlier, farmers often had to provide documents repeatedly to access various benefits, resulting in a loss of both time and money. With Farmer IDs, access to several key services is expected to become simpler and more transparent.

Bank loans and Kisan Credit Card: The loan process will become easier, reducing the need for repeated document verification.

Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana: In the event of natural disasters or crop losses, the assessment of compensation and its disbursement will be carried out through a more transparent process, with payments made directly into farmers’ bank accounts.

Disaster relief assistance: Relief during emergencies will reach genuine and eligible farmers more quickly.

Crop procurement at Minimum Support Price (MSP): The digital system will help eliminate the role of intermediaries in the procurement process and ensure that farmers receive the full value due for their produce.

The initiative is intended to strengthen transparency and accountability in agricultural service delivery, ensuring that eligible farmers can access government support with fewer procedural hurdles.

More than 6 crore farmers have already received benefits

The Digital Agriculture Mission was launched following the Union Cabinet’s approval on September 2, 2024. The Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) being developed under the mission is already showing results on the ground. Through the Farmer ID-based service delivery system, more than 6 crore farmers across the country have so far received direct benefits under various schemes. Linking a verified farmer database with agricultural services is helping eliminate fraud and the need for duplicate verification. It has also improved coordination among government departments and strengthened policy formulation and the monitoring of schemes, making it easier to track their implementation and delivery of benefits.

A strong example of cooperative federalism

Shri Chouhan credited the achievement to the collective efforts of the Central and state governments, calling it an outstanding example of cooperative federalism. He congratulated and thanked officials of the Central Government, state governments, Union Territory administrations, district-level teams and field personnel working across villages for their contribution to achieving the target ahead of schedule. States and Union Territories are also taking specific steps, in accordance with applicable rules, to bring tenant farmers and actual cultivators onto the digital platform. The objective is to ensure that no eligible farmer is left out of the government’s welfare and support programmes.

Technology to transform Indian agriculture

The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare remains committed to strengthening the Farmer Registry in line with the principle of Minimum Government, Maximum Governance. Farmer ID is not just a digital identity document; it is a strong foundation for a transparent, accountable and farmer-centric system of governance. By creating a verified digital identity for farmers, the initiative aims to improve the delivery of agricultural services and ensure that government support reaches the intended beneficiaries efficiently. Congratulating farmers across the country, Shri Chouhan urged them to embrace modern technology, avail themselves of the schemes and benefits they are entitled to without unnecessary difficulties, and contribute to taking Indian agriculture to new heights. He said the achievement marked an important step towards building a modern agricultural ecosystem in which technology serves farmers’ interests and supports the vision of a developed India.

***

SS/DK

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
PM to visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha on 25 October
PM to Inaugurate New Garment Manufacturing Facility in Varanasi
Women-Led Manufacturing Initiative Connects Varanasi to Global Markets
PM to witness Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat in Varanasi
Programme to commemorate 94th anniversary of Indian Air Force to be held under the theme “Wings over Ganges”
PM to inaugurate RBI’s newly established Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 12:32PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha on 25 October 2026. At around 11 AM, Prime Minister will inaugurate a new garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi. At around 1 PM, he will witness the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat in Varanasi as the Chief Guest.

Thereafter, Prime Minister will travel to Odisha, where at around 4:45 PM, he will inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India’s Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.

PM in Varanasi

Prime Minister will inaugurate Arvind Limited’s new garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh. The facility marks an important step towards strengthening India’s textile and apparel manufacturing ecosystem and promoting industrial growth in the region.

Focusing on modern manufacturing practices, the facility will create meaningful employment opportunities, particularly for women, and contribute to the region’s economic progress. The inauguration also highlights Uttar Pradesh’s growing role as a destination for industrial investment and manufacturing-led growth.  With a global customer base, it is a testament to how products manufactured in Varanasi will reach across the world. Being a predominantly women-led initiative, it is a powerful symbol of women-led development.

Prime Minister will witness the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat in Varanasi. The programme will commemorate the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force and will be held under the theme “Wings over Ganges”.

The aerial display will feature aircraft including the Tejas, Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand, SU-30MKI and Rafale, along with transport aircraft. Aircraft from the Indian Navy and the Indian Army will also participate, showcasing jointness in operations. The Indian Air Force’s premier display teams, including the Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team and the Sarang Helicopter Display Team, will also participate in the event. The display will showcase precision flying, coordination and operational excellence.

PM in Bhubaneswar

Marking a significant milestone in strengthening the technological foundations of India’s financial system, Prime Minister will inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India’s newly established Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar.  They have been designed to meet the Bank's computing requirements and to provide a secure, resilient, scalable and future-ready computing ecosystem for the Bank and the broader financial sector.

Four state-of-the-art data centres will host mission-critical Payment and Settlement systems, along with other flagship initiatives. The facility has been certified to Uptime Institute Tier IV standard - the global benchmark for data centre infrastructure - placing it in the highest tier of operational resilience. It is among the largest Tier IV certified facilities in the BFSI (Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance) sector worldwide. It will contribute to widening the reach, efficiency and reliability of digital financial services, and will form the secure digital foundation on which India's increasingly technology-driven financial economy can grow. It will also help strengthen Reserve Bank’s unique standing as a leader in digital infrastructure amongst the central banking community.

The Cyber Security Training Institute will boost capability building, providing a dedicated institutional platform for cybersecurity and enterprise-technology training, research, and sector-wide capability development. This institute will focus on cutting edge technologies relevant to the BFSI sector including Quantum Computing, Artificial Intelligence and other frontier technologies.

*****

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
Viksit Bharat- G RAM G
“Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)”
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 11:56AM by PIB Delhi

A New Framework for Rural Employment and Development

Aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, the Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) marks a significant reform in rural development. The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 came into force on 1 July 2026 and has been rolled out successfully across all rural areas of the country. The transition from Mahatma Gandhi NREGA to VB-G RAM G has been seamless and disruption-free. Digital systems supporting implementation were operational from the commencement of the new framework.

The Act provides a statutory guarantee of 125 days of wage employment every financial year. The guarantee covers every rural household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work. It promotes empowerment, growth, convergence and saturation for a prosperous and resilient rural Bharat. It focuses on four thematic areas: water security, core rural infrastructure, livelihood-related infrastructure and mitigation of extreme weather events.

The Act institutionalises a Whole-of-Government approach through convergence-driven and saturation-oriented planning. At its core is the preparation of Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans (VGPPs). These provide an integrated framework for addressing the diverse developmental needs of Gram Panchayats.

Bottom-up Planning Envisaged through VGPPs

Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans (VGPPs) are a key institutional reform under VB-G RAM G. They enable participatory, evidence-based, saturation-oriented, and convergence-driven planning at the grassroots level.

VGPPs put local needs at the centre of rural development planning. They are prepared with the active participation of the Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat. The Gram Sabha provides due recommendation and approval of the plans. VGPPs enable villages to identify their actual development needs, existing assets and development gaps and prioritise works accordingly.

How the VGPP Process Works

  • Participatory planning: Gram Panchayats identify and prioritise works based on local needs, with the involvement of the Gram Sabha.
  • Asset mapping: The process begins with a comprehensive inventory of existing assets, infrastructure and service delivery gaps within the Gram Panchayat.
  • Coverage of existing assets: The inventory includes assets created under various Central and State Government schemes and programmes.
  • GIS-based planning: The planning process uses GIS, Yuktdhara, PM Gati Shakti, and other digital tools. Geospatial and non-spatial information supports evidence-based and integrated planning based on local needs and existing assets.
  • Gap assessment: Information from these platforms supports spatial planning, better asset mapping, and avoidance of duplication. It also helps identify infrastructure deficits, development priorities, and potential interventions.
  • Convergence across government: VGPPs promote a Whole-of-Government approach by bringing together resources and interventions from different schemes, departments and stakeholders for integrated village development.
  • Multi-level consolidation: VGPPs are consolidated at the Block, District, State and National levels. The consolidated plans contribute to the Viksit Bharat National Rural Infrastructure Stack.
  • Permissible works: The VGPP Framework identifies 318 types of permissible works across the four thematic areas.

The VGPP process is intended to support integrated village development through employment-linked asset creation, improved infrastructure and convergence of public interventions.

VB G-RAM G: Progress on the Ground

As of 24 September 2026, VB-G RAM G has recorded significant progress since its implementation on 1 July 2026.

  • Active workers: 10.88 crore in 2026-27
  • Assets created: 2.83 lakh
  • Person-days generated: More than 31.69 crore
  • Women’s participation: 61.65 percent in 2026-27
  • Employment provided to workers on demand:  Over 2.81 crore belonging to about 2.23 crore rural households
  • Works under Execution: 97.17 lakh
  • Approved works readily available to meet future employment demand: 73.24 lakh
  • Active worksites operational: Around 20.16 lakh
  • Number of Gram Panchayats executing works presently across the country: Nearly 2.31 lakh
  • DBT transactions: 3.76 crore in 2026-27
  • Wage rate: Ranges from Rs.300 to Rs.450 per day
  • Total number of Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards issued: 15.17 crore

Financial Progress

  • A total of Rs.93,841 crore has been allocated to States/UTs as interim allocation for FY 2026-27
  • Out of this, a Mother Sanction of Rs.25,880 crore has been issued as the first instalment to the States/UTs

Technology Enabled Transparency and Governance

Technology is central to VB-G RAM G implementation. Digital systems support worker verification, monitoring, payments, and transparency. They also link employment with sustainable asset creation and rural development.

  • Digital verification: e-KYC and worker attendance are captured through Face Authentication and biometric authentication. It significantly enhances transparency, accountability, and authenticity.
  • Digital work monitoring: Geo-tagging, digital measurement, electronic Measurement Books (e-MB) and mobile-based monitoring support monitoring across different stages of implementation.
  • Digital payments: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) supports payments under the framework.
  • Technology-enabled oversight: Spatial technology-enabled planning, real-time dashboards, and AI-enabled analytics support monitoring, reporting, and corrective action.
  • Digital platforms and capacity building: Dedicated digital platforms, citizen engagement platforms and large-scale capacity building initiatives further support implementation.

Building Rural Development from the Ground Up

VB-G RAM G brings employment, participatory planning and rural development together. Through VGPPs, Gram Panchayats identify local needs, map existing assets and prioritise development works. Technology, convergence and digital systems strengthen implementation, transparency and accountability. The framework links employment with sustainable asset creation, supporting resilient livelihoods and integrated rural development.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Commerce & Industry
item.description: Ministry of Commerce & Industry Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Holds Meetings with German Industry Leaders and Research Institutions in Berlin India–Germany Economic Cooperation in Focus During Shri Goyal’s Berlin Visit Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 11:40AM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal concluded his two-day official visit to Germany with a series of engagements in Berlin on 23 October 2026, including meetings with senior German government officials, business leaders, research institutions…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Holds Meetings with German Industry Leaders and Research Institutions in Berlin
India–Germany Economic Cooperation in Focus During Shri Goyal’s Berlin Visit
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 11:40AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal concluded his two-day official visit to Germany with a series of engagements in Berlin on 23 October 2026, including meetings with senior German government officials, business leaders, research institutions and members of the Indian diaspora. The engagements focused on strengthening India–Germany cooperation in trade, investment, advanced manufacturing, research and emerging technologies.

Shri Piyush Goyal held a bilateral meeting with the Economic and Financial Policy Advisor and G7/G20 Sherpa at the German Federal Chancellery, Mr. Levin Holle. The discussions covered bilateral economic cooperation and opportunities to further strengthen economic and investment ties between India and Germany.

The Minister held individual meetings with CEO, Siemens Healthineers AG, Mr. Bernd Montag; Mr. Carsten Coesfeld, Member of the Executive Board of Bertelsmann and CEO, Bertelsmann Investments; and, CFO, Volkswagen AG and CEO, Škoda Auto, Mr. Holger Peters. The meetings explored opportunities to expand business partnerships, investment and industrial cooperation between the two countries.

Shri Goyal also participated in a roundtable with leaders of prominent German industrial research institutions to discuss cooperation in advanced industrial technologies and innovation. Separately, members of the accompanying Indian business delegation participated in sectoral roundtables with German industry representatives and sectoral associations to explore opportunities for bilateral business collaboration.

Shri Goyal also interacted with members of the Indian diaspora in Berlin and addressed the media.

As part of his engagements with the research and innovation ecosystem, Shri Goyal interacted with Indian science and technology researchers and students based in Germany. He also held a roundtable with heads of selected Fraunhofer Institutes, covering areas such as microelectronics, power electronics, logistics, smart manufacturing, industrial innovation and battery technologies. The discussions explored avenues for strengthening research collaboration and industry–academia partnerships between India and Germany.

The engagements underscored the growing scope of the India–Germany Strategic Partnership, particularly in trade, investment, advanced manufacturing, science and technology, research and industrial cooperation.

***

C N Abhijith Narayanan/ Abhimanyu Panwar

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Railways
item.description: Ministry of Railways 8th All India Conference of GRP Chiefs Concludes in New Delhi; Focus on Intelligence-Led Policing and Stronger Coordination among RPF, GRP and State Police GRP Personnel Onboarded on RailMadad Platform for Improved Grievance Redressal, Timely Information-Sharing and Complaint Monitoring Safer Railway Journeys During Diwali and Chhath: Emphasis on Crowd Management, Advance Planning and Efficient Passenger-Flow Management From Drone-Assisted “Pink Patrol” to Project DISHA, Women-Led and Community-Based Safety Initiatives Deliberated at GRP Chiefs’ Conference Posted On: …
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Railways
8th All India Conference of GRP Chiefs Concludes in New Delhi; Focus on Intelligence-Led Policing and Stronger Coordination among RPF, GRP and State Police
GRP Personnel Onboarded on RailMadad Platform for Improved Grievance Redressal, Timely Information-Sharing and Complaint Monitoring
Safer Railway Journeys During Diwali and Chhath: Emphasis on Crowd Management, Advance Planning and Efficient Passenger-Flow Management
From Drone-Assisted “Pink Patrol” to Project DISHA, Women-Led and Community-Based Safety Initiatives Deliberated at GRP Chiefs’ Conference
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 10:47AM by PIB Delhi

The 8th All India Conference of Government Railway Police (GRP) Chiefs, convened by the Railway Protection Force (RPF), concluded successfully in New Delhi on 23 October 2026. It provided a platform for discussing emerging security challenges, sharing best practices and strengthening coordination among RPF, GRP and State Police.

The high-level conference was presided over by Director General, RPF, Ms. Sonali Mishra, and attended by Chairman and CEO, Railway Board, Shri Satish Kumar, members of the Railway Board, and GRP chiefs from various States and Union Territories.

A key highlight was the onboarding of GRP personnel onto the RailMadad platform by the Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS), aimed at improving passenger grievance redressal, timely information-sharing and complaint monitoring.

Detailed deliberations were held on various initiatives aimed at enhancing railway security and passenger safety.

South Central Railway’s “Pink Patrol: Eyes in the Sky, SHAKTI on the Ground” showcased a women-led model integrating drone-assisted surveillance with rapid-response teams under the SHAKTI framework.

Stone-pelting on trains was highlighted as a challenge, with emphasis on hotspot-based patrolling, enhanced surveillance, strict action against offenders, youth outreach and stronger RPF-GRP coordination. Community awareness and preventive engagement were recognised as important deterrents.

The conference also deliberated on crowd management during Diwali, Chhath and other festivals. Northern Railway’s Delhi Division highlighted coordinated efforts with Delhi Police, GRP and Delhi Metro authorities, supported by CCTV surveillance, public announcements, barricading, designated holding areas and dedicated control rooms. Emphasis was laid on advance planning, efficient passenger-flow management and coordinated deployment of security personnel to ensure safe and orderly passenger movement during peak periods.

Central Railway’s Pune Division highlighted Project DISHA (Dedicated Initiative for Safety, Harmony & Awareness), an initiative aimed at engaging children living near railway tracks through educational and recreational activities, safety awareness sessions and community-based interventions. Collaboration with NGOs, National Service Scheme (NSS) volunteers and local communities fosters awareness about railway safety and responsible behaviour, while discouraging stone-pelting, theft, trespassing and other unsafe practices.

Deliberations also covered joint RPF-GRP training, sabotage prevention and prompt information-sharing on narcotics detection. Digital evidence handling, standardised procedures, intelligence-sharing, strengthened investigative capabilities and supporting infrastructure were emphasised.

Addressing the gathering, the Chairman and CEO, Railway Board, highlighted the importance of coordinated efforts, technological advancements, innovation and a shared commitment among railway authorities, RPF, GRP and State Police to effectively address the evolving security challenges on Indian Railways. He also emphasised the need to build passenger confidence, ensure courteous and professional policing, and leverage technology and innovation to enhance productivity and operational efficiency.

The conference concluded with closing remarks by DG/RPF, who emphasised the need for intelligence-led policing to strengthen railway security.

****

Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Manik Sharma

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
CSIR-CRRI Inaugurates Indian Airport Pavement Symposium (IAPS 2026) in New Delhi
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 9:21PM by PIB Delhi

 

CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CSIR-CRRI), in association with Bharat Tiki Tar Shell India Private Limited (BTS), successfully organized the Indian Airport Pavement Symposium (IAPS 2026) today at the CSIR-CRRI Auditorium, New Delhi. Convened under the theme "Advancing Performance-Based Airport Pavements for a Resilient and Sustainable Aviation Future," the national symposium brought together key stakeholders—including regulators, airport operators, armed forces, academic leaders, and global pavement experts—to chart a comprehensive technical roadmap for India’s expanding airside infrastructure.

The symposium was inaugurated by Dr. (Mrs.) N. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR and Secretary, DSIR, Government of India, and emphasized the importance of indigenous research and development, technological innovation and institutional collaboration in strengthening critical national transportation infrastructure.

As guest of honour Mr. Manoj Menon, Executive Director, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), delivered the special address, highlighting the role of industry-driven innovation and material technologies in meeting the evolving requirements of aviation infrastructure.

Dr. Ch. Ravi Sekhar, Director, CSIR-CRRI, highlighted the Institute’s longstanding contributions to pavement engineering, road and airport infrastructure research, asset management and the development of technical standards. He underscored the importance of translating scientific research into practical engineering solutions to enhance the durability, safety and sustainability of airport pavements.

The welcome address and contextual remarks were delivered by Dr. Ashish Walia, Sr.Scientist, CSIR-CRRI & Organizing Secretary. The vote of thanks was proposed by Dr. K. Ravinder, Head, Information, Liaison and Training, CSIR-CRRI.

The technical sessions address key challenges in pavement planning, quality control, sustainable airfields, and modified bituminous materials. The symposium underscores CSIR-CRRI’s commitment to translating scientific research into innovative engineering solutions for India’s rapidly expanding aviation infrastructure.

A key highlight of the symposium was the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between CSIR-CRRI and Bharat Tiki Tar Shell India Private Limited to promote collaborative research, technology development and deployment in advanced modified bituminous binders and specialized airport pavement solutions.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Soliciting public opinion and stake holders input on Design of Network Architecture for the proposed Broadband Public Protection and Disaster Relief (BB-PPDR) System
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 8:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) purposes to implement Pan India dedicated Broadband Public Protection and Disaster Relief (BB-PPDR) Network to provide Mission Critical Push-to-Talk (MCPTT), Mission Critical Data and Mission Critical Video capabilities to State/UT Police, Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs), National Disaster Relief Force (NDRF), Fire Service, Medical Service and other public safety agencies across the country.

For designing the reference architecture, MHA is soliciting public opinion and stake holders input on Design of Network Architecture for the proposed Broadband Public Protection and Disaster Relief (BB-PPDR) Communication System. Inputs may be provided on design options, technology to be adopted, its’ comparative merits and de-merits, cost efficiency and suitability to Indian conditions. The Concept Note has been uploaded on the websites of MHA (Home/Documents/Orders and Circulars) and DCPW (Home/Documents/ Stakeholder Consultations, Home/Announcements & Home/What’s New).

All stakeholders are invited to send their comments/inputs to dd-ppdr@dcpw.gov.in and ad.ppdr@dcpw.gov.in latest by 5th November 2026, with the subject line “BB-PPDR Architecture — Stakeholder Feedback”.

item.description: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways India's First Maritime NBFC SMFCL Scales up with Rs 5,107 Crs Disbursed, Aims for Rs 60,205 Crs by 2031 Sarbananda Sonowal calls SMFCL's role vital to propel India's maritime growth under PM Narendra Modi's Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 Maritime Development Fund (MDF) moves towards first close of Rs 5,000 crore Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 8:48PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal inaugurated the corporate office of Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited (SMFCL)…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
India's First Maritime NBFC SMFCL Scales up with Rs 5,107 Crs Disbursed, Aims for Rs 60,205 Crs by 2031
Sarbananda Sonowal calls SMFCL's role vital to propel India's maritime growth under PM Narendra Modi's Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047
Maritime Development Fund (MDF) moves towards first close of Rs 5,000 crore
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 8:48PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal inaugurated the corporate office of Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited (SMFCL) at the Institute for Studies in Industrial Development (ISID) in New Delhi today, giving a permanent home to what he called India's first dedicated Non Banking Financial Company (NBFC) in the maritime sector.

The new office opens at a time of fast progress. As on 30 September 2026, SMFCL has sanctioned Rs 11,563 crore of financing and disbursed Rs 5,107 crore, with more than half of the sanctioned amount still to be drawn as projects advance.

The corporation's plan looks well beyond today. It aims to reach cumulative disbursements of Rs 60,205 crore by the end of FY2031, a build-up that depends on equity support to scale up in line with RBI norms and its debt-to-equity ratio.

"As India's first dedicated NBFC in the maritime sector, SMFCL is playing a pivotal role in mobilising long-term finance for port-led development, enhancing shipbuilding and coastal connectivity and catalysing the overall growth of our maritime economy. It has a vital role to play in propelling India’s maritime growth towards achieving the vision of PM Narendra Modi of becoming a leading maritime nation of the world by 2047,” Sarbananda Sonowal said.

The Maritime Development Fund (MDF), which has two components, is also taking shape. For its MIF component, SBI Ventures Limited has been appointed official Fund Manager. Registration as an Alternative Investment Fund with SEBI is due to be completed by the end of November, and the first close of Rs 5,000 crore is targeted by January, 2027.

The Interest Incentivisation Fund (IIF) is already delivering. Its online portal, www.iifmdf.in, is live, and loans of Rs 4,500 crore have been supported so far. About Rs 25 crore of interest subvention has been released against interest paid by borrowers.

"Under PM Narendra Modi’s transformative Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047, India is building a stronger, more self-reliant and globally competitive maritime sector," Sonowal said.

The schemes SMFCL runs now cover a maritime project from first idea to final loan. The Government of India's contribution to the Maritime Investment Fund, up to Rs 9,800 crore, is channelled through SMFCL, while SBI Ventures, selected as Fund Manager, brings professional management to the fund.

The Interest Incentivisation Fund eases the cost of borrowing for eligible shipyards, with SMFCL working out the incentive, running the application and claims portal, and releasing the interest support. Under the Shipbuilding Development Scheme, the credit risk cover corpus is managed centrally and backed by premium and claims review, giving shipyards and lenders a safety net against payment risk.

SMFCL's own lending appraises, sanctions and monitors projects across ports, rail and road links, inland waterways, coastal infrastructure, port-hinterland logistics, shipbuilding and ship repair. It also oversees the release and use of Sagarmala and National Maritime Heritage Complex (NMHC) funds, so that money reaches projects and is tracked until it is spent.
